A first real run had ended with 'the read pass differs with and without the app database': the month walk counted calls and read the list's footer after a fixed pause that slow reads outlast. That was a defect of the check, reproduced over an invented ledger with delayed reads and fixed by waiting for the calls to finish before the run was repeated. The dry run and the deliberate breaks of the failure output were made over an invented ledger. Nothing changed in this repository.

title: Write the rule that only the latest load lands once in the interface, and its test helper once
description:
## Outcome
The rule "an answer lands only if it belongs to the latest load that place started" is written once in
`web/src` and used by every place that loads from the server and loads again, and the test helper that
holds an answer back until released is written once. Nothing a person sees changes, and no place loads
at a different moment than before.

## Context
**Why.** Each screen, composable and store of the interface that shows server data has its own `load`,
and each guards against an older answer arriving after a newer one with the same few lines: a counter
taken when the load starts and compared when its answer arrives. Seven places had those lines first; the
work this item waits for puts them in fifteen more, by decision, because moving every screen to a shared
loader in the same step was judged too much at once. After it there are about twenty-two hand copies.
This item removes the copying, and starts by looking at what that work actually left.

**The terms.** After a write the interface bumps a counter kept in a store (`web/src/stores/revision.ts`);
places that show server data watch it, and usually the selected month or a route parameter too, and call
their own `load` again. A *load* awaits one or more methods of the API and assigns the answers. Tests fake
the backend with `createFakeApi`; a test of reordered answers replaces one method so that each call's
answer is held until the test releases it.

**The places** (paths under `web/src`). Ordered before the waited-for work:
`screens/budget/BudgetScreen.vue`, the evaluation in `screens/budget/ScenariosScreen.vue`,
`screens/patrimonio/PatrimonioScreen.vue`, `screens/cofrinhos/CofrinhosScreen.vue`, the panel's menus in
`components/transaction-panel/panelActions.ts`, and the lines menu of
`screens/assinaturas/AssinaturaScreen.vue`. Ordered by that work: `screens/inicio/InicioScreen.vue`,
`components/transactions/useTransactionList.ts`,
`components/transaction-panel/useTransactionDetail.ts`, `screens/budget/useOpenLine.ts`, the documents'
load of `screens/budget/ScenariosScreen.vue`, `screens/contas/AccountScreen.vue`,
`screens/cofrinhos/CofrinhoScreen.vue`, `screens/assinaturas/SubscriptionsTab.vue`, the detail of
`screens/assinaturas/AssinaturaScreen.vue`, `screens/revisao/WeeklyTab.vue`,
`screens/revisao/PaydayTab.vue`, `screens/revisao/ClosingTab.vue`, `stores/shell.ts`,
`screens/contas/CardScreen.vue` and `screens/config/ConfigScreen.vue`. The list is what was planned; the
first criterion checks it against the code.

**What differs between the places, which is why this is a small shared piece and not one loader.** Some
load two methods together and have a quiet and a loud mode (the transaction list). One chains a second
load with a cache (the weekly tab). Some blank what they show when the id changes and keep it across a
bump; others never blank. The budget puts a draft in the key and treats a read-only answer by discarding
the draft. The shell store writes its answer from two paths. A single loader that owned the watching, the
loading state and the assignment would have to carry all of that as options. What every place has in
common is only the ordering, so the shared piece is the ordering alone: something a `load` asks "am I
still the latest?" before it assigns.

**The test helper.** `holdNext`, which holds the next answer of an API method until released, is defined
separately in `screens/patrimonio/patrimonio.test.ts`, `screens/cofrinhos/cofrinhos.test.ts` and
`screens/cofrinhos/cofrinho.test.ts`; `hold` in `test/lineMenu.ts` does the same for one method. The
waited-for work may have added one more under `web/src/test/` for its fifteen tests.

**Decided, and what lost.** One loader for every screen: rejected for the reasons above. Leaving the
copies: rejected by the owner, who asked for this item. Changing what triggers a load anywhere: out of
scope, as it was for the work before.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The pull request opens with an inventory taken from the code as that work left it: each place that
orders its loads, with its file, and each definition of a hold-and-release test helper; where the
inventory differs from the list in the Context, the code is right and the difference is stated.
- [ ] One function or composable under `web/src/lib/` holds the ordering, and no place in the inventory
keeps a counter of its own: a search of the interface's source for the hand-written comparison finds it
only inside that one piece.
- [ ] The piece is covered by a test of its own: two loads started, answered last first, the older one
told it is no longer the latest; and a new key behaving as a new load.
- [ ] Every reordering test that exists when this starts (the four older ones and those the waited-for
work added) passes with no change to what it asserts.
- [ ] One hold-and-release helper is left, under `web/src/test/`, and the local copies in the three screen
tests are removed in its favour.
- [ ] No place gains or loses a trigger: `git diff` shows no added or removed `watch` source, and the
existing tests that count calls of an API method pass unchanged.
- [ ] Nothing of the server, the contract, the HTTP client or the stand-in changes.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` passes on both viewports with no limit raised and no state removed,
and its output is in the pull request body.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`.
- [ ] Done when: the ordering is written once and every place uses it, the hold-and-release helper is
written once, and every reordering test passes as it was.

## Tests
- Unit, in `web/src`: the shared piece by itself.
- Unit, existing, with screens mounted over `createFakeApi`: every reordering test, unchanged in what it
asserts.
- E2E, by hand: the parity run over every screen touched, in a real browser, with its output kept.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/screens/`, `web/src/components/transactions/useTransactionList.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/useTransactionDetail.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelActions.ts`, `web/src/stores/shell.ts`, `web/src/lib/`,
`web/src/test/`
**Reads only:** `web/src/stores/revision.ts`, `web/src/stores/month.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/index.ts`,
`web/scripts/parity/states.mjs`, `bin/ci`

About twenty-two places, each losing a few lines to one call, one new small file for the shared piece and
one for the test helper. It is wide and shallow: no server code, no contract, no stand-in, no style. It
cannot run beside the work it waits for, since it edits the same lines.

## Recovery path
Nothing is stored and nothing visible changes. Reverting the pull request brings the copies back.
close_reason: The rule that an answer lands only if it belongs to the latest load is one function, createLatestLoad in web/src/lib/latestLoad.ts, with a test of its own, and the twenty-one places that ordered their loads with a counter of their own use it; the three screen tests that carried a hold-and-release helper use the shared one. Nothing on screen changes. Verified by the gate and the design parity (174 checked, none over the limit) on the branch after main was merged in, by every reordering test passing with no change to what it asserts, by the author's four deliberate breaks and by six more in review: three killed by a named test, three judged to change nothing reachable and said so in the pull request.

title: Attribute ledger movements to savings pots so a planned transfer is marked done by itself
description:
## What changes for the user
On payday the app lists the transfers the budget plans (to a pot, to a reserve line, to investments), and
each one stays "pending" until the person marks it done by hand, because the app cannot tell which
movement in the bank was that transfer. After this lands, when the money really moved into the pot, the
transfer shows as done on its own, with the day it happened, and the pot's page and the closing view agree
without a click. If it were wrong the person would see a transfer marked done that never happened (the
worst case: a month closed believing a reserve was funded) or one that happened and stays pending as it does
today.

## Outcome
This is a tracking bead. It holds the subject so it is not lost and tells whoever picks it up what was
decided, why it waits, what it will need from the write side and what must be decided first. It is not ready
to implement. It is finished when the open decisions below are answered by the person and written here,
including whether the balance history is long enough to attribute from, and the implementation beads exist,
each written whole and depending on the write side being complete.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database*
(`finwise.db`) holds what the person authors. *A pot* is a savings pot of a bank account (identity
`reserve:<account>/<reserveId>`, `investment:<id>`, or `slot:<account>/<n>` when the bank does not keep it
stable). *A transfer* is a planned movement derived from the month's budget: one per pot that has linked
provision or reserve lines (key `pot:<id>`, the sum of their amounts, named after the pot, or "Sem nome" for a
pot the bank gives no name), one per such line linked to no pot (`line:<id>`), and `investment` for the
residual above zero. *Marking* a transfer done is a write (`review.markTransferDone(month, key)`) stored per
month in `transfer_marks(month, transfer_key, done_on)`.

**What was decided.** A transfer is done only when marked by hand, for the month the screen shows. An
unknown or already marked transfer answers null.

**Decided by the person on 2026-11-23.** This item stays held until the measurement named under "Why it
waits" can be made, and decisions 2 to 7 below are taken with that measurement in hand. Two other courses
lost. Deciding all seven now, on the rule that exists: no case exists yet to say how often that rule is
right. Matching a movement to a planned transfer by amount and day alone, without the sightings: measured
the same day, an amount repeats within one account and month often enough to be unsafe for a mark that
feeds the month's closing.

**What the write side delivers that this builds on:**

- `transfer_marks` and the transfer keys above; a mark is a recorded change that can be undone.
- A pot's page shows its movements from the ledger only, and shows no synthetic deposit: a movement into a
  pot is not a transaction the API lists, because the transaction rules take the movements of savings pots
  out of the clean list (`internal/txrules`, `potmovements.go`).
- A movement is already placed on a pot, for the pot's page: `potrules.AttributeMovements`
  (`internal/potrules/movements.go`), called by `attachMovements` in `internal/api/pots_model.go`. The
  bank's row does not name the pot, so the rule reads the account's next sighting of its pots, at most
  three days after the movement: the movement belongs to a pot when that sighting holds that one pot only,
  or when exactly one pot's balance moved by the movement's amount since the sighting before. A pot that
  also earned yield in that interval does not match by amount, and its movement stays on the account. What
  does not exist is the step from a deposit placed on a pot to the planned transfer and its mark.
- A pot's contribution state on its page: closed; none planned when the current month's transfers have none
  for it; otherwise pending, or done with its day once marked. An investment pot follows the `investment`
  transfer.
- The net worth's contribution (planned, done, progress) comes from the current month's transfers and their
  marks; its investment rate is the budget's rate as planned, and the same rate as actual once the
  `investment` transfer is marked, zero before.
- A provision or reserve line counts as made, for its planned amount, in the closing view when the
  transfer that carries it is marked for that month or the month is closed.
- A `slot:` pot has an unstable identity, so anything attributed to it would not be stable either.
- `internal/potrules` also pairs and reads pot movements and balance histories for the yield.

**Why it waits, as measured on 2026-11-23.** The rule above applies only to a movement that is followed,
within three days, by a sighting of its account's pots. Over the real ledger the sightings around the
movements were too sparse for the rule to apply, so the measurement could not say how often the rule is
right, and in particular how often a pot's yield in the same interval keeps a deposit from matching. The
length of the history is therefore not the condition; that sightings are nightly around the movements is.

**The trigger to pick this up again:** the movements of at least one payday fall on days that are followed
by nightly sightings. Then run `TestPotRulesOverARealSnapshot` (`internal/potrules/realsnapshot_test.go`)
with `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` naming a current snapshot: its last log line counts the movements the rule
placed and the ones it left on the account. Show the counts to the person and take decisions 2 to 7 from
them. A real ledger is a person's whole financial history:
a real snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from it (amount, description, name, document, id) is
ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the
person running the test and goes into no file; the test runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a
file. Fixtures are invented.

**What an implementer must respect**: money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path;
every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant; an automatic mark is a recorded change
in the journal with its author (which author is part of the decisions below) and can be undone; a mark the
person made by hand is never overwritten by an automatic one.

## What must be decided first
Decided by the person who uses the app, since a transfer marked done feeds the month's closing.

1. **When the history is long enough.** Answered 2026-11-23: not a number of days. The condition is the
   trigger under "Why it waits"; until then the app keeps asking for the mark by hand.
2. **How a movement is attributed to a pot**: by amount and day against the planned transfer, by the change
   of the pot's balance, or otherwise; and how close is close enough (days, cents).
3. **What an ambiguous match does**: two plausible movements for one transfer, one movement for two
   transfers (two lines linked to one pot), a movement that is a yield or a withdrawal. Whether the app
   leaves the transfer pending and says why, or asks the person to confirm.
4. **How an automatic mark and a manual one coexist, and under which author the automatic one is
   journaled**: which wins when they disagree, whether an automatic
   mark can be taken back (it should be a journaled change like any other), and whether the person can
   unmark one.
5. **What happens with a `slot:` pot** (unstable identity): attributed never, or attributed within a day.
6. **What the `investment` transfer follows**: a movement in an investment pot, in a brokerage account, or
   both.
7. **Whether the past is filled in** (months already marked by hand or closed) or only the months from the
   change on.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every item of "What must be decided first" has an answer written into this bead by the person, or is
struck out with the reason; item 1 is answered (a condition, not a number), and items 2 to 7 are answered
after the measurement its trigger names, which prints only counts.
- [ ] The implementation beads exist, each written to the standard (self-contained, checkable criteria),
each depending on the write side's last piece.
- [ ] This bead changes no code: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` before and after, and no test is added, so
there is none to see failing.
- [ ] Done when: the decisions are recorded here, the implementation beads are written and ready, and
nobody mistakes the by-hand mark for something the app already infers.

## Tests
None: nothing is implemented here. The implementation beads must carry: a movement that matches a transfer
and marks it with its day; two movements and one transfer; one movement and two transfers; a manual mark
that stays; the undo of an automatic mark; a pot with no stable identity; the measurement over a real
ledger printing counts and fixed sentences only.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none now (this bead edits only the tracker). When implemented, expect: `internal/potrules` (the
attribution), `internal/ingest` (where it would run), `internal/api` (the payday read, the pot page's
contribution, the net worth's contribution), `internal/authored` if a mark records its origin, and the
golden files of the reads that change.
**Reads only:** `internal/potrules/`, `internal/txrules/potmovements.go`, `internal/api/review_payday.go`,
`internal/api/pots*.go`, `internal/authored/`

Not statable in a few lines until the decisions are made.

title: Document in AGENTS.md how to run the app with its own database, how its writes are tested, the backup and ingest commands, and what a refused write shows
description:
## What changes for the user
Everything the app can now do (keep a budget, put purchases on lines, close a month, change the PIN) works
only if the person, or an agent working for them, can start the app the right way, copy its database
safely and understand what it says when it refuses to save. Today the repository's briefing for anyone
working on it still describes a read-only app: it says every write is refused, it lists a file that no
longer exists, and it has no word about the database where the person's own decisions are kept. After
this lands that briefing is true again, and a person or an agent can follow it, line by line, to start the
app with a database of its own, take a backup that can be restored, check the change journal, and read
what each refusal means. If it were wrong the person would find out by following it: a command that fails,
a flag that does not exist, or a database started in a way that fails to protect their data.

## Outcome
`AGENTS.md` is brought in line with the write side that has landed, in English, in the file's existing
voice and without rewriting what is still true. It states: the recipe to run `finwise serve` with
`--db` (and how that differs from running without it); the write conformance and its golden files; the
commands `finwise backup` and `finwise ingest`; what a refusal looks like on the wire and what the person
reads; and it replaces the sentence about `pendingReads`, which names a list in a file that does not
exist, with what the coverage test really does. Every command and path it names was run or opened by the
implementer. No file other than `AGENTS.md` changes.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* (or *snapshot*) is the SQLite
file that a separate collector, pluggy-sync, fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, and
no code here ever writes to it. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, a file of the app's own where
everything the person authors is kept (budget, categories on transactions, tags, notes, splits,
subscriptions, closed months, settings, the PIN once changed); it is owned by the package
`internal/authored`, which is the only package that executes SQL against it. *The journal* is what that
package writes for every change: who made it (`person` for an HTTP session, `rule` for the ingest,
`model` reserved for a later nightly call), the method, the instant and the Brazil day, and one row per
effect, so that every change can be undone. *The manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, the
generated description of the API's methods: 82 today, of which 55 are of class `write`, 1 of class
`evaluate`, 23 `read` and 3 `session`. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend in `web/src/api/fake/`
that the design prototype runs on. *The ingest* (`internal/ingest`) is the one function that brings the
app's database up to date with a new snapshot: it indexes the transactions the ledger lists, pairs a bank's
pending row that vanished with the posted row that replaced it, and applies the rules (a default line, or
examples the person already gave) once per new transaction, or puts what it cannot decide in the pending
queue.

**What `AGENTS.md` says today, and what has become false** (each point checked in the file as it stands
before this work; re-check each against the repository as it stands when this starts, since the earlier
work may have edited a line itself):

- The `Serve` paragraph says `finwise serve` "is read-only: every write and evaluation of the contract is
  refused with `read_only`". That stays true only without `--db`. With `--db` it is false.
- The same paragraph lists the settings: `--listen` / `FINWISE_LISTEN`, `--ledger` / `FINWISE_LEDGER`,
  `FINWISE_PIN_HASH` (required), `FINWISE_SESSION_TTL`. It has no `--db` / `FINWISE_DB`.
- It says "A read handler is registered in `internal/api` with `Registry.Register("domain.name",
  handler)`, one `register<Domain>` function per domain listed in `domainRegistrations`; `pendingReads`
  in `reads_pending_test.go` lists the reads still without one." There is no `reads_pending_test.go`. The
  file is `internal/api/reads_coverage_test.go`, and it holds no list of pending reads: it holds
  `readCoverageProblems` and the test `TestEveryReadMethodHasAHandler`, which fails for every read method of
  the manifest without a handler and for every registered name that is not a read of the manifest. The
  third parameter of a read handler (today a `*ledger.Reader`) also changes with the write side: it becomes
  one value carrying a view of the ledger and a view of the app's database, opened for the request. State
  what the code has when this starts, and name the type as the code calls it.
- The `Real data at the desktop` paragraph says "a read with no handler yet answers `internal`" and "What
  only the person can author (budget lines, tags, nicknames, splits) is the contract's empty value, never a
  guess." Both are true only without `--db`.
- The `Money on the wire` bullet says "no source file of `internal/api` may touch a float, and a test
  fails if one does". The test now also covers the new packages (`authored`, `ingest` and the three rule
  packages `budgetrules`, `classrules`, `subrules`).
- The `Conformance and golden files` bullet describes only the read side.
- The `Tests` section says the real-ledger rule for one opt-in test. The write side adds more opt-in
  tests and one more thing that holds real values (below).
- The `Backend` bullet says `internal/ledger` reads the snapshot read-only; that stays true. Add that the
  app's own database is the one SQLite file the code writes, and only through `internal/authored`, where
  every statement is a registered constant and no package other than `internal/authored` executes SQL
  against it. Also say, where the file states its rules about the API, that the files of `internal/api` log
  nothing and read the clock only from the request, because a test enforces both.

**What to write, section by section.** Content is fixed here; wording, order inside a section and where a
sentence goes are the implementer's, matching the file's voice (short, imperative, the reason after the
rule). Keep to the file's size habit: `AGENTS.md` is a briefing, not a manual. Where a longer text already
has a home (the golden files' own `README.md`), point to it instead of copying it.

1. **Running with `--db`.**
   - `--db` / `FINWISE_DB` is a file path. Absent: the server is the read-only server, unchanged, and every
     one of the 56 write and evaluate methods is refused with `read_only` before its body is read. Present:
     the file is created if it does not exist (its directory must exist), migrated and kept open for the
     life of the process; it is not reopened per call.
   - The file is recognised before anything is written, without opening it as a database: its first hundred
     bytes must be an SQLite header whose application id is `0x46494E57` (decimal 1179209303). A file that
     is missing or empty is a new database. Any other file, the collector's snapshot included, is refused
     at start with a message naming the path and the reason, and is left byte for byte as it was. Say it
     plainly: never point `--db` at the ledger.
   - Migrations are applied at start, each in one transaction, and recorded by name with a checksum. A
     changed or unknown migration is refused. Before migrating a database that already holds data, the
     file is copied with `VACUUM INTO` to `<name>.before-<UTC timestamp>` beside it, never over an existing
     copy.
   - `FINWISE_PIN_HASH` is still required at start. Once a PIN has been changed in the app, the hash stored
     in the app's database is the one that opens the app and the environment's is ignored; the server says
     so in one log line at start.
   - The tracking start month: the month, in Brazil time, in which the database was first created. The
     app asks about uncategorised transactions only from that month on; earlier ones are never queued and
     can still be categorised by hand. It is set once, at creation, and nothing sets it again, so a
     database created for a test on the day it was created has today's month and a restored backup keeps
     the month it was taken with.
   - The ingest runs at start, on a timer (default every ten minutes), right after a budget is saved or
     applied, and by `finwise ingest`. State the flag or variable that sets the interval only if the code
     has one when this starts.
   - A complete command pair for trying it on a desk, in the file's own style, with a scratch database
     (it works with the stand-in's PIN recipe already in the file):

     ```
     printf '%s\n' 123456 | go run ./cmd/finwise hash-pin
     FINWISE_PIN_HASH='<that string>' go run ./cmd/finwise serve --ledger <snapshot.db> --db <scratch.db> --dev-insecure-cookie
     ```

     followed by `npm --prefix web run dev:backend` as the file already says. The implementer runs this
     pair for real (see the criteria) and writes what the code does, not what this bead guesses.
   - What a person looking at the interface sees in each mode: without `--db` a write toasts that the app
     is read-only; with it, the write is saved.
   - The privacy consequence, once, in the `Tests` section where the real-ledger rule already is: a
     `finwise.db` fed from a real snapshot holds real values (the index of transactions has account ids,
     days, amounts and establishment keys), so a scratch database made for a check against a real ledger
     lives in a temporary directory, is never committed, never printed and is removed afterwards.
2. **Write conformance and golden files.**
   - Every write and evaluation is of exactly one mode, and a test requires a case for each registered
     handler in its mode: a *recorded change* (the answer validates against the manifest; its effects match
     a golden file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`; undoing it returns a canonical dump of
     every journaled table to the dump taken before); *nothing to do* (a null answer, no row added to the
     journal); an *evaluation* (no table changes at all); an *extension of an earlier change*
     (`transactions.applyLineToEstablishment`: undoing it returns the dump taken before its origin);
     `changes.undo` and `session.changePin` have tests of their own.
   - Read conformance has a third state, the full invented ledger with an invented authored state, in
     `testdata/golden/full-authored/`, with its cases in a list of its own, `authoredReadCases`, apart from
     `readCases`. Say why they are apart: the interface's equality test finds the cases of `readCases` by
     their written shape and requires a golden file in `empty/` for each; an authored-state case has none.
   - One test case per refusal reason (the list below).
   - A manifest walk requires that every write or evaluation has exactly one implementation, a registered
     handler or, for `session.changePin` alone, the session service; or that it is in the explicit list
     `writesWithoutHandler`, which must be empty when the write side is complete. Name the file the list is
     in, as the code has it.
   - The command that rewrites the write goldens, named from the code as it stands (the read side's is
     `go test ./internal/api -run TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile -update`); it refuses to run while
     `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set, so that a real ledger cannot reach a committed file. Each golden
     diff is read in review, never accepted by running the command.
   - The opt-in test of the write side over a real ledger: the variable that enables it
     (`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT`), what it does (a scripted series of writes on a scratch database, every
     recorded write undone, the journaled tables compared before and after), and that it says counts and
     fixed sentences only. Name its file from the repository.
3. **The commands `backup` and `ingest`.** Take each flag, exit status and message from the code, not from
   this bead.
   - `finwise backup --db <file> --to <file>`: the source is resolved as `serve` resolves it (the flag, then
     `FINWISE_DB`); `--to` is a flag only. It recognises the source as above, except that a missing or
     empty file is an error and is never created, copies with `VACUUM INTO` to a temporary file beside the
     destination, checks the copy (application id and `PRAGMA integrity_check`), publishes it with an
     operation that cannot replace a file, and then records the instant in the source database (UTC, RFC
     3339), which is what the settings screen's "last backup" shows. A destination that exists, or appears
     meanwhile, is refused and untouched. A plain file copy of a running database is not supported, because
     it can miss the write-ahead log. How to restore: stop the server; check the copy; put it in place of
     the database with no `-wal` or `-shm` file beside it; start the server.
   - `finwise ingest`: runs the ingest once and exits 0 on success or "nothing new", 1 on failure, with a
     fixed message. Counts only; the command logs counts, no value.
   - The usage line the program prints with no argument names every command it has; mention it only if the
     file already shows it.
4. **What a refusal shows.**
   - The error envelope is `{"error":{"kind"}}` with a closed set of kinds. One kind, `refused`, always
     carries one reason of a closed list and is answered with HTTP 409:
     `{"error":{"kind":"refused","reason":"<reason>"}}`. The texts stay in the interface and are
     Brazilian Portuguese:

     | reason | when | what the person reads |
     | --- | --- | --- |
     | `month_closed` | saving or applying a budget for a closed month; closing a month already closed | "Esse mês já está fechado." |
     | `future_month` | closing a month after the current one | "Esse mês ainda não chegou." |
     | `pending_reviews` | closing a month while a transaction of that month or an earlier one waits for review | "Resolva as pendências do mês antes de fechar." |
     | `stale_change` | undoing or extending a change that is unknown, already undone, already extended, or overwritten since | "Isso já foi alterado depois e não pode mais ser desfeito." |
     | `not_found` | a write whose result cannot be null names a transaction, pot, subscription or establishment that the ledger does not list or the app's database does not have | "Esse item não existe mais." |
     | `unknown_line` | a write names a budget line that the budget of the month it is resolved in does not have | "Essa linha não existe no budget desse mês." |
     | `invalid_budget` | saving a budget with a duplicate or empty line name, an unknown or repeated line id, an unknown group | "O budget tem linha sem nome ou repetida." |
     | `unstable_pot` | a write to a pot whose identity the bank does not keep stable | "O banco não identifica esse cofrinho de forma estável." |
     | `split_with_reimbursement` | splitting a purchase that has a linked reimbursement, or linking one to a split purchase | "Uma compra dividida não pode ter reembolso ligado." |

     Check each row against the manifest and `web/src/api/failures.ts` as they stand; a row the code
     changed is written as the code has it, and the difference is reported.
   - The other sentences of the interface: a refusal reason it does not know, "Não foi possível concluir.";
     a write the server answered with `internal` (or `bad_request` or `unknown_method`), "Não foi possível
     salvar."; a write whose answer never arrived, "Não deu para confirmar se foi salvo. Atualizando a
     tela."
   - `bad_request` means the arguments do not match the method's schema or cannot be parsed (a month, a day,
     an amount): a bug in a client, not something a person did. `read_only` is for a server without `--db`
     and for a write method that has no handler yet. `ledger_unavailable` is answered by a write exactly as
     by a read when the snapshot it needs is missing, and nothing is recorded.
   - What the interface does: a refused or failed write shows its sentence with no action and bumps the
     revision at once so the screen shows what the server holds; "Tentar de novo" is for failed reads and
     never replays a write; a `locked` answer brings the PIN screen back with the wait the lockout holds.
   - How a test makes the server refuse: the helper beside `readOnlyApi` that refuses a chosen write with
     a chosen kind and reason. Name it as `web/src/test/` has it.
5. **The stale sentence.** Replace the `pendingReads` sentence with the truth: the file
   `reads_coverage_test.go`, the name `readCoverageProblems`, and that the test fails for a read without a
   handler. Check the code once more at the end: if it still has no list of pending reads, none is
   mentioned; and remove from `AGENTS.md` every claim that a read or a write is "still without" a handler
   if the manifest walk says otherwise.

**Rules for the text itself.** `AGENTS.md` is committed in a public repository and is written as the
project's own rules. So: English; no absolute path from any machine; no reference to a session, a plan, a
bead, a reviewer or an agent that produced it; no value from a real ledger, no count taken from one; and
no mention of any private notes. The private browser check that runs the real build in a real browser over
a real ledger is not named (it lives outside this repository). Do not rewrite sentences that are still
true; do not reformat the file; keep the headings and the order of the sections it has; a sentence made
false by the write side is edited, a new fact goes where a reader would look for it.

**Where the facts are.** Everything in the sections above is delivered by earlier work. The implementer
reads the code, not this bead, for the final names: `cmd/finwise/` (the commands and flags),
`internal/authored/` (recognition, migrations, `meta`), `internal/ingest/`, `internal/api/` (the router,
`reads_coverage_test.go`, `conformance_test.go`, the write conformance and its harness, `golden_test.go`,
`handler_silence_test.go`), `internal/api/testdata/golden/README.md` and `web/src/api/failures.ts`.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a worktree and ends at local commits (atomic, Conventional Commits, no
attribution lines, no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit message). Money is integer cents
and no float may appear in the money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered
constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; a design value in a
component comes from a token. None of these touch code in this work, but the text must say them where the
file already says them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The recipe is run, not only written: the implementer creates a scratch directory, makes a PIN hash,
starts `finwise serve` with `--ledger` set to an invented snapshot (the one `ledgertest` builds, written to
a temporary path by a throwaway test that is deleted afterwards and never committed) and `--db` to a path in that
directory, and shows that the file now exists, carries application id 1179209303, and that an unlocked
session can make one write (for example `budget.save`) that survives stopping and starting the server
again. The same start without `--db` answers `read_only` to that write. Each command line that ends in
`AGENTS.md` is one of the lines run.
- [ ] The collector's snapshot, given as `--db`, is refused at start and its SHA-256 is equal before and
after (run on the invented snapshot, to prove the sentence "never point `--db` at the ledger").
- [ ] `finwise backup --db <file> --to <dest>` and `finwise ingest` are run once each over the scratch
database exactly as `AGENTS.md` writes them; both exit 0, the second `backup` to the same destination
exits non-zero and leaves it unchanged, and every flag, variable and exit status the file names appears in
`go run ./cmd/finwise <command> -h` or in the code of `cmd/finwise`.
- [ ] Every path that `AGENTS.md` names between backticks exists in the worktree (a short throwaway script

title: Add targets on savings pots (Rainy Funds) and show how a pot shared by several budget lines divides between them
description:
## What changes for the user
The design has a place for a rainy-day fund with a target: a pot that fills up to an amount and, when it
reaches it, switches its monthly deposit off, switching it on again if it falls below. Today the budget's
Rainy Funds group is always empty, no pot shows a target or how far it is, and when two budget lines are
linked to one savings pot the budget cannot say how much of the pot's balance belongs to each line. After
this lands the person can give a pot a target, see its progress, see its deposit switch off at the target
and on below it, and see for each line linked to a shared pot its own share of the balance. If it were wrong
the person would see money the app says is saved on a line that has none, or a deposit switched off that
should still be going.

## Outcome
This is a tracking bead. It holds the subject so it is not lost and tells whoever picks it up what was
decided, why it waits, what it will need from the write side and what must be decided first. It is not ready
to implement. It is finished when the open decisions below are answered by the person and written here, and
the implementation beads exist, each written whole and depending on the write side being complete.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database*
(`finwise.db`) holds what the person authors. *A pot* is a savings pot of a bank account: its identity is
`reserve:<account>/<reserveId>` or `investment:<id>`, or `slot:<account>/<n>` when the bank does not keep
the identity stable, and a write to a `slot:` pot is refused with the reason `unstable_pot`. *A bucket*
says where a pot's money counts in the net worth: "Disponível", "Reservado" or "Investido". *The budget*
has five editable groups (income, fixed, variable, provisions, reserves); a *provision* or *reserve* line
can be linked to a pot. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend of the design prototype
(`web/src/api/fake/`).

**What the person decided** (2026-11-21, "A"). Pot targets (Rainy Funds) get no control in the write side.
The Rainy Funds group of the budget is answered empty and no pot shows a target; a tracking bead holds the
subject, with the command-line interface for agents (see its tracking bead) as a likely way to author the
four targets. What was given up: a new contract method and a control that the design does not have.

**What the contract already has** (so that a target is mostly a source for values the screens already
read):

- A pot row's `target: PotTarget | null` (`amount`, `progress` as a percent of the target reached, capped at
  100); a pot detail's `belowTarget: PotBelowTarget | null`, present only while the pot has a target and
  sits under it.
- A budget cell of type `rainy-deposit` with `switchedOn: boolean`: "a rainy fund's deposit: switched off at
  its target, switched on again below it".
- All of them are null or absent today.

**What the write side delivers that this builds on:**

- `pot_lines(line_id, pot_id)`: a budget line is linked to at most one pot; several lines can be linked to
  the same pot. A provision or reserve line's pot is the pot it is linked to, never a pot of the same name;
  with no link the line's balance cell is the contract's `none`. Linking a line to a pot toggles it, and
  linking a line that another pot has moves it. A link is resolved in the current month.
- `pot_settings(pot_id, bucket)`: a pot's bucket overrides the default; there is no other per-pot setting
  and no table for a target.
- The payday's transfers are derived from the month's budget, each with a stable key: one per pot that has
  linked provision or reserve lines (`pot:<id>`, the sum of their amounts), one per such line linked to no pot
  (`line:<id>`), and `investment` for the residual above zero; a transfer is done only when the person marks
  it (`transfer_marks`).
- The pot's contribution state on its page: closed; none planned when the month's transfers have none for
  it; otherwise pending, or done with its day once marked.
- *The per-line balance of a shared pot is not defined.* A pot's balance comes from the ledger; with two
  lines linked to it, nothing says how it divides. This is the part the write side leaves out on purpose.

**What an implementer must respect**: money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path;
every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant; percentages the server computes are
whole numbers rounded half up, while a rate the bank states keeps its two decimals; a write to a `slot:`
pot is refused; a real ledger is a person's whole financial history, so any measurement over it prints
counts only.

## What must be decided first
Decided by the person who uses the app, since it decides what the app does with their savings.

1. **Whether targets get a control in the interface.** The design has none. Either the person authors
   them through something else (the command-line interface for agents is the likely path for the four
   targets), or the design gains a control, which would be a new contract method and a design decision
   first.
2. **What a target belongs to**: a pot, a budget line, or a Rainy Fund as a thing of its own; and how many
   there can be.
3. **What switches a deposit off.** The cell's meaning is "switched off at its target, switched on again
   below it": decide whether that is on the pot's balance alone, whether a withdrawal counts, and what the
   budget's planned amount and the payday's transfer do while it is off.
4. **How the balance of a shared pot divides between its lines.** The write side makes no division and
   states none; the person names the rule (the options are theirs to name, for example by what each line
   plans or by what each has contributed, and "no division" is also an answer).
5. **What the Rainy Funds group of the budget contains** once it is no longer empty (which lines, in what
   order, with which three cells), and how it differs from the reserves group.
6. **What a pot with a target but no stable identity does** (it would be refused as `slot:`).
7. **How it is verified.** What is proved with invented pots and what, if anything, with a real ledger
   under the rule that no value of it is printed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every item of "What must be decided first" has an answer written into this bead by the person, or is
struck out with the reason.
- [ ] The implementation beads exist, each written to the standard (self-contained, checkable criteria),
each depending on the write side's last piece.
- [ ] This bead changes no code: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` before and after, and no test is added, so
there is none to see failing.
- [ ] Done when: the decisions are recorded here, the implementation beads are written and ready, and
nobody mistakes the empty Rainy Funds group and the absent targets for finished work.

## Tests
None: nothing is implemented here. The implementation beads must carry: a target that fills and the
deposit that switches off at it and on below it; progress as a whole percent capped at 100; the division of
a shared pot summing back to the pot's balance exactly, in cents, with a remainder rule; a `slot:` pot
refused; an undo of each target write.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none now (this bead edits only the tracker). When implemented, expect: `internal/authored` (a
table or a column for a target, a migration owned by that work), `internal/budgetrules` (the group and the
cell), `internal/api` (the pots reads, the budget view, the payday transfers), the contract manifest if a
method is added, and `web/` if a control is added.
**Reads only:** `internal/api/pots*.go`, `internal/potrules/`, `internal/authored/`,
`web/src/api/contract/savings-pots.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/budget.ts`

Not statable in a few lines until the decisions are made.

title: Make every screen hold on a fresh install
description:
## What changes for the user
Every screen was built against a design that shows a year of use: a budget, subscriptions, months already closed, a chart with history. Nobody has seen the app on its first day, and a real backend that only reads the bank's records is exactly that first day. Today several screens would show `NaN`, a blank area or nothing at all. After this lands every screen opens cleanly both when the bank data exists and nothing else does, and when there is no data whatsoever: zero where zero is true, a dash where a figure is not known, a short sentence where a list is empty.

## Outcome
The in-memory stand-in can start in two new states, a fresh install with bank data and an empty ledger; the contract is nullable wherever a fresh install has no honest value; every screen renders both states without an error; and a test sweeps every route over both.

## Context
finwise's interface (`web/`, Vue 3) reaches its backend through a TypeScript contract, `FinwiseApi` (`web/src/api/types.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/`). An in-memory stand-in (`web/src/api/fake/`) implements it over the design prototype's dataset, and `createFakeApi(options)` accepts a `state`. A real, read-only backend is being built: it will answer what the bank's records support and return everything the person authors inside the app (budget, budget lines on transactions, tags, nicknames, subscriptions, review marks, settings) as on a fresh install. The design prototype has no first-run screens, so those states were never built or measured.

A generated manifest, `internal/contract/contract.json`, carries a JSON Schema for every method's result, and an existing test validates the stand-in's answers against it. Changing a contract type means regenerating the manifest (the gate fails otherwise).

**Two states.**
- *Fresh install*: accounts, transactions, the card's bills, pots and investments exist; nothing the person authors does. Transactions have no budget line, no tag, no nickname and nobody classified them; pots have no bucket, no target and no linked line; there is no budget, no subscription, nothing to review, no closed month; settings are the defaults.
- *Empty ledger*: nothing at all, as before the first synchronisation. No account, no transaction, no card, no pot.

Both are built from invented data, like every fixture in the repository.

**Never invent a value.** Where the contract requires a field that has no honest value in one of these states, the field becomes nullable in the contract and the screen learns to show its absence. Known candidates, to be confirmed against the types: who classified a transaction when it has no line; the bucket of a pot and of an account; the card overview when there is no card; the last backup in the settings; the suggested threshold with no corrections behind it; the salary account's balance with no such account. A zero is used only where zero is the truth (a budget cap with no budget is 0). The full list of widened fields goes in the pull request.

**What the screens show.** Follow the vocabulary the interface already has: the empty block of the transaction list (`web/src/components/transactions/TransactionList.vue`) for an empty list, a dash for an unknown figure, `R$ 0,00` for a true zero. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese. No new visual component and no new token unless a state cannot be expressed without one; a color, size, radius, shadow or spacing step is never written as a literal.

**Known breaks.** `web/src/screens/patrimonio/chartGeometry.ts` divides by the chart's maximum with no guard for zero. `FakeState.card` is required, so a state with no card does not type-check. The Início, Budget, Patrimônio and card screens were partly read and assume their objects exist; Revisão, Cofrinhos, Assinaturas, Contas, Configuração and the transaction panel were not audited at all.

**The design does not move.** The prototype's dataset and every existing parity state stay as they are: the parity check must report the same result. The new states have no reference to be measured against, so they are covered by tests and looked at by a person.

**Looking at it.** The dev server starts the stand-in in one of the new states when `VITE_FINWISE_STATE` is `fresh` or `empty` (`VITE_FINWISE_STATE=fresh npm --prefix web run dev`); unset, it is the prototype's dataset as today, and the built interface never reads the variable. One screenshot per screen in each state, taken with the pinned Playwright against that dev server at the two parity viewports, is saved under the git-ignored `work/fresh-install/`.

Writes over the new states are out of scope; so is any change to how a write is called.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The stand-in exports a fresh-install state and an empty-ledger state, and `createFakeApi({ state })` runs on each.
- [ ] Every answer of every `read` method over each of the two states validates against its result schema in the manifest.
- [ ] A sweep test mounts every route of `web/src/router.ts`, plus the transaction panel, a pot's page, an account's page, the card page and a subscription's page where the state has one, over both states: no error is thrown, no promise rejection is left unhandled, and the rendered text contains none of `NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity`, `null`, `Invalid Date`.
- [ ] The chart geometry returns a finite height when the maximum is 0.
- [ ] A transaction with no line renders its row and its panel; a pot with no bucket renders in the list and on its page; the card page renders with no card.
- [ ] An unknown figure renders as a dash and never as `R$ 0,00`; a test asserts it for at least the last backup and an unknown yield.
- [ ] The prototype dataset is unchanged, and `npm --prefix web run parity` still reports every state at or under 0.05%.
- [ ] The manifest is regenerated and the gate's freshness check passes.
- [ ] No component gains a raw design value: `npm --prefix web run check:tokens` passes.
- [ ] `VITE_FINWISE_STATE=fresh` and `=empty` start the dev server's stand-in in those states; with the variable unset the prototype dataset is served, and the production build's output does not change with the variable set.
- [ ] One screenshot per screen for each state and each of the two parity viewports exists under `work/fresh-install/`, and the pull request lists every widened field with what its screen shows.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, parity is unchanged, and the sweep passes over both states.

## Tests
- Conformance: the stand-in's answers over both new states against the manifest's schemas.
- Component: the sweep over every route and both states.
- Unit: the chart geometry at zero; each widened field's rendering.
- Parity: the full run, unchanged.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose (a `NaN` reintroduced, a required field restored) and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/api/contract/`, `web/src/api/fake/`, `web/src/screens/`, `web/src/components/`, `web/src/stores/`, `web/src/test/`, `web/src/main.ts`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `web/src/router.ts`, `web/scripts/parity/`, `design/`, `bin/ci`

Wide on purpose: the same defect, a screen that assumes a year of data, is spread over every screen, and each fix is a few lines. The contract types change only by becoming nullable, the stand-in gains two states and keeps its dataset, and no write call, no route and no reference screenshot is touched.
close_reason: The stand-in starts as a fresh install or an empty ledger, the contract is nullable wherever a first day has no honest value, every screen shows a dash for an unknown figure, R$ 0,00 for a true zero and a sentence for an empty list, and a sweep mounts every route over both states. VITE_FINWISE_STATE starts the dev server's stand-in in either state; the prototype build is identical with and without it. A fresh pot starts in the bucket its bank declares, so the net worth counts it from the first day. bin/ci: CI green, 877 tests. Parity on the merged tree: 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%. Every read answer over the three states validates against the regenerated manifest. 83 screenshots under work/fresh-install were looked at.

title: Derive the payday transfers from the month's budget under a stable key, mark one done by month and key, and let the pot page, the net worth and the budget follow
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, over their real bank data, the "Dia do salário" tab of the review shows the balance of the account
the salary lands on and nothing to do with it: the cushion reads R$ 0,00, the difference is a dash, the
list says "Nenhuma transferência planejada", a pot's page says "Sem aporte planejado" whatever the budget
plans for it, the net worth's "Aporte do mês" is two empty bars and the budget never shows the month's
investment as made. After this lands the tab says how much the account must hold before the salary is
set aside (the fixed and the variable lines of the month), whether the balance covers it and by how much,
and lists what to transfer on payday: one transfer for each pot the budget feeds, one for each provision
or reserve line that has no pot, and what is left to invest. "Marcar como feita" marks one of them for
the month on screen, dated today, and "Desfazer" takes it back. The pot's own page then says "Ainda não
feito" or "Feito em 20/03", the net worth shows how much of the month's plan is done and the real
investment rate, and the budget shows the investment as made. If this were wrong the person would see a
transfer for the wrong amount, a cushion that says "covered" when it is not, or, with two pots of the
same name, would mark one and find the other marked.

## Outcome
`PaydayTransfer` carries a `key`, and `review.markTransferDone` takes the month and that key. Over a
server with its own database, `review.payday(month)` answers the cushion, the balance, the difference
and the transfers derived from the budget in force for the month, each with its mark;
`review.markTransferDone` records a mark as one undoable change and answers null for a transfer that is
unknown or already marked; `savingsPots.detail` answers the pot's contribution state from the current
month's transfers; `netWorth.overview` answers the month's contribution and the investment rate from
them; `budget.view` answers the investment as made once its transfer is marked. The payday tab sends the
month it shows and the transfer's key, and the stand-in follows the two type changes and nothing else.
Without a database every one of these answers is what it is today.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, through `internal/ledger`.
*The app's own database* is `finwise.db`: everything the person authors (a budget, a link between a
budget line and a pot, a mark) lives there and never in the snapshot. *The contract* is the TypeScript
interface `FinwiseApi` under `web/src/api/contract/`; *the manifest* is
`internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it by `npm --prefix web run contract`, versioned and
never edited by hand, which gives Go each method's route, class and schemas. *The stand-in* is the
in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it and its tests are
the only existing statement of how writes behave, and its behaviour is the rule wherever this text does
not say otherwise. *The journal* is the record of every change made to authored data, which is what
makes a change undoable. *A pot* is what the pots screens list: a reserve entry of a bank account (id
`reserve:<account>/<reserveId>`), an investment (id `investment:<id>`) or, when the bank does not keep
an entry's identity stable, a slot (id `slot:<account>/<n>`). *A month* is `YYYY-MM` and *a day*
`YYYY-MM-DD`, both in Brazil time (`internal/brday`); "today" and "the current month" are the Brazil day
and month of the instant in the request's context, never of the host's clock. The budget has five
groups a person edits, by key: income (`rec`), fixed (`fix`), variable (`var`), provisions (`prov`) and
reserves (`res`). A provision is money set aside every month for a bill that comes once in a while; a
reserve is money set aside for something wanted.

**What earlier work provides.** None of this exists in the repository when this text is written; each
piece is delivered before this one and is used here as delivered.

- The app's own database (finwise-9h2): the package `internal/authored`, which owns `finwise.db`, opens it
  when the server is started with `--db` / `FINWISE_DB`, applies its migrations by name and keeps every
  SQL statement over it as a registered constant; without `--db` the server is today's read-only server.
- The recorder (finwise-wi4): the layer of `internal/authored` through which every change to a journaled
  table is written as one recorded change that `changes.undo` can take back. It knows two shapes of
  table; a *set table* holds rows that are facts by existing, and an effect on it is one row appearing
  or disappearing.
- The per-request views (finwise-jzw): a handler's third parameter is one value carrying a view of the
  ledger (one read-only transaction on the snapshot) and a view of the app's database (one read-only
  transaction, or an empty view that answers nothing when there is no database), and the clock is a
  required part of the configuration.
- Write dispatch (finwise-2s5): the router runs a registered write handler inside one transaction and one
  recorded change that it commits, after checking the arguments against the method's schema in the
  manifest; a write with no handler, or any write on a server without a database, answers `read_only`
  before its body is read; a test walks the manifest and requires every write to have a handler or be
  named in the list `writesWithoutHandler`, where `review.markTransferDone` stands until this slice.
- The write conformance harness (finwise-fst): a test requires a case for every write handler in its mode (a
  recorded change, whose effects are compared with a golden file under `testdata/golden/writes/` and
  whose undo must return a canonical dump of every journaled table to the dump taken before; or nothing
  to do, a null answer that adds no row to the journal), and the package
  `internal/authored/authoredtest` builds invented authored states for tests.
- The third read state (finwise-tsr): the read conformance runs a third time over the full invented ledger
  with an invented authored state, with golden files in `testdata/golden/full-authored/` and cases in a
  list of their own, `authoredReadCases`.
- The budget's tables (finwise-ef7): `lines(id, builtin)`, `budget_versions(from_month)`,
  `budget_version_lines(from_month, group_key, position, line_id, name, cents, flag)` and
  `closed_months(month, closed_on)`. A budget is a list of versions, each valid from a month on; the
  budget in force for a month is the latest version at or before it, and a month before the first
  version uses the first. A line has an integer id minted once and a name that belongs to the version.
- The budget view (finwise-jsx): the pure package `internal/budgetrules`, whose `View` computes, in integer
  cents, the income, the investment as the residual (income less the fixed, variable, provision and
  reserve groups; it can be negative), the rate as a whole percent of the income and every cell of the
  budget screen, and the real `budget.view` with and without a draft. It answers the investment as "not
  made" until this slice.
- The pots' links (finwise-rju): the migration `0005_pots` with `pot_lines(line_id, pot_id)`, a line linked
  to at most one pot, and `pot_settings(pot_id, bucket)`; the write that toggles a link, refused for a
  `slot:` pot because its id changes between days; and the pots list, a pot's page and the net worth
  screen fetching again when something was written.
- The review's migration (finwise-rf3): `0007_review`, which creates `transfer_marks(month, transfer_key,
  done_on)` beside `closing_steps(month, step)` and `dismissed_warnings(id)` and enters them in the
  recorder's registry as set tables. If the store functions that read and write a mark are not there
  yet, they are part of this slice, in the file of `internal/authored` that holds the review's tables.

One later piece reads what this slice builds: the closing view of the month (finwise-ysr) will list its
contributions from the same transfers and marks, and count a provision or reserve line as made, for its
planned amount, when the transfer that carries it is marked for that month or the month is closed. So
the derivation and the read of a month's marks must be reachable from outside the payday handler.

**What the code is today (each point checked in the file named).**

- `web/src/api/contract/review-payday.ts`: `PaydayTransfer` is `{name, amount, state, doneOn,
  markedByHand}` with `TransferState = 'on-target' | 'done' | 'pending'`; `PaydayView` is `{cushion,
  balance, balanceLabel, difference, covered, transfers}`; `PaydayApi.markTransferDone(name: string)`
  answers `ChangeResult | null`, "Null when the transfer is unknown or already done". The manifest's
  entry for the method takes one string. `web/src/api/contract/classification.ts` classes it `write`
  and `review.payday` `read`.
- `web/src/api/fake/payday.ts`: the stand-in's cushion is the total of the `fix` group plus the total of
  the `var` group of the budget in force for the month asked; the salary account is the fixed id
  `'itau'`; the difference is the balance less the cushion and `covered` is `difference >= 0`; the
  transfers are a seeded list, `state.plannedContributions`, the same whatever month is asked.
  `markTransferDone(name)` finds one by name, answers null unless it is `pending`, and otherwise sets
  `state: 'done'`, `doneOn: state.shell.today`, `markedByHand: true` under one change.
  `FakePlannedContribution` in `model.ts` is `{name, amount, state, doneOn, markedByHand?}`; the seven
  seeded ones are in `prototype-data.ts` (`PLANNED_CONTRIBUTIONS`), in the budget's own order: one pot
  at its target, the three provision lines, the two reserve lines, then "Investimento".
- `web/src/api/fake/payday.test.ts` pins: cushion 6780 against a balance of 7020 gives a difference of
  240 and `covered: true`; a balance of 6000 gives -780 and false; a balance equal to the cushion is
  covered; raising a cap raises the cushion; a mark is dated today and `markedByHand`; a mark shows on
  the pot's page; a mark is taken back by its change; a done, an on-target and an unknown transfer
  answer null. `web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts` also calls `markTransferDone('Compras')`.
- `web/src/api/fake/savings-rules.ts`: `plannedFor(state, pot)` is the first planned deposit, in list
  order, whose name is the pot's or, for a pot that is an investment, whose name is "Investimento".
  `potContribution` answers `closed` for a closed pot, `switched-off` for a pot at its target,
