title: Bring the nightly model call into the app: suggestions with a justification, the month's report, cap proposals, cheaper alternatives and the calibration of its confidence
description:
## What changes for the user
The app already works by hand and by rule: it puts a new purchase on the line the person chose for that
establishment before, and what it cannot decide it puts in the weekly queue with only a reason ("Estabelecimento
novo", "PIX para pessoa sem apelido", "Baixa confiança") and no suggestion, so every unknown establishment
costs the person a decision from nothing. The month's closing shows an empty report, no proposal ever
arrives for the person to approve or refuse, a subscription never shows cheaper plans, and the
settings screen's calibration shows five bands with no figure. After this lands, a model reads what the
rules could not decide once a night and the person finds, in the queue, a suggested line with a short
justification and a confidence; at the month's closing a short written report whose paragraphs can carry a
proposed change; and, on the settings screen, how often the person corrected the model at each level of
confidence, so they can choose the threshold below which the app asks. Nothing it suggests changes a total
until the person accepts it, unless the person decided otherwise (see what must be decided first). If it
were wrong the person would notice in the worst way: a suggestion that looks sure and is not, accepted by
habit, or a purchase's description sent somewhere the person did not agree to.

## Outcome
This is a tracking bead. It exists so that the subject is not lost and so that whoever picks it up knows
what was decided, why it waits, what it will need from the write side and what must be decided first. It is
not ready to implement. It is finished when the open decisions below are answered by the person, the
answers are written into this bead, and the implementation beads for the nightly call exist, each written
whole (what changes for the user, outcome, context, criteria, tests, blast radius) and each depending on
the write side being complete.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database*
(`finwise.db`, created by `finwise serve --db`) is where everything the person authors is kept. *The
journal* is the record that database keeps of every change: author, method, instant and effects, so every
change can be undone. *The rules* are `internal/classrules`: for a transaction never evaluated before, they
apply the establishment's default line, or the line of at least the configured minimum of the person's own
examples when one line leads by the configured threshold, or else make the transaction *pending* with a
reason. *The queue* is the weekly review's list of pending transactions. *The model* here is a call to a
large language model made from the app's side once a night, after the collector has refreshed the ledger.
*The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend of the design prototype (`web/src/api/fake/`); the things the
model is meant to produce are present in it as seeded data with no rule behind them.

**What the person decided.** The nightly model call is not part of the write side (decision of
2026-11-21: "pode ser A"). The write side ends with an app that is complete by hand and by rule; the model is
the plan after it. What was given up by deciding that: the model inside the write side, which would have
meant choosing a provider and a model at once and an outbound dependency in every verification.

**What the write side leaves ready for it** (the points the model plan builds on):

- The suggestion on a pending transaction is nullable: `suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification` may
  all be absent, because without a model "Estabelecimento novo" has nothing to suggest and the queue must
  still work. The interface already handles a pending item with no suggestion, no confidence and no "the
  model had suggested", and keeps "accept" disabled until a line is chosen. A model would fill them.
- The journal's author is one of three: `person` (an HTTP session), `rule` (the ingest) and `model`, which is
  reserved for this call and used by nothing yet. The journal is never trimmed, so it is the record of what
  the model did and what the person corrected afterwards.
- The pending reasons are three, all produced by rules. The interview that fed the write side named a fourth,
  a *value out of pattern*, which needs a judgment the write side does not invent; it arrives with the
  model.
- `belowThreshold` on a transaction stays false until the model exists: it is about the model's confidence
  only, never about a rule's.
- The three settings that govern the rules (threshold 50 to 99, minimum of examples 1 to 50, closing day)
  act only on transactions evaluated after the change; the rules run once per transaction and never again,
  so taking a rule's line back does not bring it back the next night. How the model's pass relates to that
  rule (is a transaction the rules left pending offered to the model once, and when) is open.
- Calibration is answered as the contract has it today: five bands (`CalibrationBand`: from, to,
  `correctionPercent`, null for a band no classification fell in) with no measured value, and a suggested
  threshold that is null. Lines applied by rule never count as the model's. The figure is "how often the
  person corrected the model among classifications whose confidence fell in a band"; the journal holds
  what is needed to compute it (a change by `model`, and a later change by `person` to the same unit).
- The month's report (`ReportSection` of the closing view, each `ReportParagraph` with text, an optional
  `proposalId` and `sent`) is empty. A paragraph's `proposalId` names a change it suggests; `sent` says the
  change already waits for approval.
- Cap proposals and approvals: `review.propose`, `review.approve` and `review.refuse` are write methods that
  answer null (nothing produces a proposal until the model or the command-line interface does). The
  contract's `ApprovalRequest` (`id`, `title`, `reason`) is "a change the model proposed that waits for a yes
  or a no". The flow is shared with the command-line interface for agents (see the tracking bead for it).
- A subscription's `alternatives` (sentences the model wrote about cheaper plans, empty when it found none)
  is empty.
- The handlers are meant to be callable outside HTTP, so the nightly call can use them without a network
  hop (the same need the command-line interface has).

**Why it waits.** A provider and a model are not chosen, and the person decided not to carry that choice
or its outbound dependency into the work that makes the app complete.

**What the model call will need to respect** (rules of the write side that stay true): money is integer
cents and no float may appear in the money path; every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered
constant; the files of `internal/api` log nothing and read the clock only from the request, so a call made
at night supplies its own clock and its own author; nothing authored is ever rewritten silently, so what the
model changes is a change in the journal with author `model` that can be undone and is refused as stale if
overwritten since. A real ledger is a person's whole financial history: no value from it is ever printed,
logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request, and what a model is sent is a separate
decision (below).

## What must be decided first
Each of these is decided by the person who uses the app, since it decides what the app does with their
money and where their data goes.

1. **Which provider and which model** the nightly call uses, and where its credential lives.
2. **What is sent out.** Which fields of which transactions leave the machine (description, amount, day,
   establishment key, the person's own previous decisions as examples), and what never does. The
   establishment key can be a document number. This is the decision most likely to change the design.
3. **What the model may do alone and what it may only propose.** Whether it only fills the suggestion of a
   pending transaction (the person still accepts), or may apply a line itself above some confidence, and
   whether a model-applied line counts toward the budget at once. This is shared with the command-line
   interface's decision about what an agent may do without approval.
4. **When it runs and what a failure does.** After the collector's nightly refresh, on a schedule the
   packaging work of step 4 provides; and what the app shows when a night's call failed or the provider was
   unreachable (the rules keep working either way).
5. **The fourth reason.** What "a value out of pattern" means, as a rule the person can state, and what the
   queue says for it.
6. **The report and the proposals.** What the month's report contains, which of its paragraphs may carry a
   proposal, and which proposals exist (cap changes were named); what "alternatives" for a subscription
   means; and what makes a change a proposal rather than a suggestion.
7. **Calibration.** How the measured correction rate by band and a suggested threshold are computed from
   the journal, over how many classifications a band is judged, and whether the suggested threshold is only
   shown or ever applied.
8. **How it is verified.** A verification that depends on a provider is an outbound dependency in every
   run; decide what is proved with a recorded or invented model answer, what is checked against the real
   ledger under the rule that no value of it is printed, and what is only judged by the person.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every item of "What must be decided first" has an answer written into this bead by the person, or is
struck out with the reason.
- [ ] The implementation beads exist, each written to the standard (self-contained, with criteria a
command or an observation can check), each depending on the write side's last piece, and none states a
provider or a model that the person has not chosen.
- [ ] This bead changes no code: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` before and after, and no test is added, so there
is none to see failing.
- [ ] Done when: the decisions are recorded in this bead, the implementation beads are written and ready, and
the subject cannot be mistaken for finished (closing this bead does not mean the model exists).

## Tests
None: nothing is implemented here. The implementation beads carry the tests; the points they need to
cover are those the context lists (suggestion nullable end to end; author `model` in the journal; undo of a
model's change; calibration from the journal; no value in any log).

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none now (this bead edits only the tracker). When implemented, expect: `internal/classrules`
(or a package beside it) for the contract between rules and model, `internal/authored` (the author is
already in the journal), `internal/api` (the five methods named above and the closing view's report),
`cmd/finwise` (a command that runs the call), the settings screen's calibration read, and the contract
manifest if a type changes.
**Reads only:** `internal/classrules/`, `internal/ingest/`, `internal/authored/`,
`internal/api/review*.go`, `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/review-closing.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/subscriptions.ts`

The radius cannot be stated in a few lines until the decisions are made, which is what keeps this a
tracking bead.

title: Add `finwise backup`, a checked copy that never replaces a file, and show the last backup in the settings
description:
## What changes for the user
Once the app keeps what a person types, that one file is the only copy of months of decisions about
their money, and nothing today can copy it safely: copying the file by hand while the app is running
can produce a copy that looks whole and is missing the latest changes. The settings screen already
has a line "Último backup:", and it always shows a dash. After this lands there is one command that
takes a complete, checked copy while the app keeps running and never writes over a copy that is
already there, and the settings line says when the last one was taken ("hoje às 02:15", or the date).
If this were wrong the person would find out on the worst day: a backup that cannot be restored, or
one that silently replaced the last good copy.

## Outcome
`finwise backup --db <file> --to <file>` writes a consistent copy of the app's database: it
recognises the source by its first hundred bytes before touching it and treats a missing or empty one
as an error, copies with `VACUUM INTO` to a temporary file beside the destination, checks the copy,
publishes it with an operation that cannot replace a file, and then records the instant in the source
database. A destination that exists, or appears meanwhile, is refused and untouched; no temporary
file outlives a failure; and if the instant cannot be recorded the copy just published is removed, so
a backup and its record exist together or not at all. `settings.overview` answers that instant as
`lastBackup`, in Brazil time, and null while no backup has run or no database is configured.

## Context
finwise is a personal finance app for one person. The **ledger** is a SQLite snapshot that a separate
collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. The **app's own database**,
`finwise.db`, holds everything the person authors, and `internal/authored` is the only package that
executes SQL against it. The collector can always fetch the ledger again; what is in `finwise.db`
exists nowhere else, which is why it needs a backup of its own.

**What exists when this starts.** Two pieces of earlier work have landed; read the code as it is,
since file and function names are whatever that work chose.

- The work that creates the database (finwise-9h2): `internal/authored` recognises a file by its first
  hundred bytes before writing to it, opens it with fixed connection settings (`foreign_keys(1)`,
  `busy_timeout(5000)`, `synchronous(FULL)`, `journal_mode(WAL)`, immediate write transactions),
  applies migrations, keeps every statement as a registered constant that a test prepares against the
  migrated schema, and created the table `meta(key, value)`, which holds the month the database was
  created in and is where the instant of the last backup goes. `finwise serve --db` keeps the database
  open for the life of the server. The clock is a required part of the configuration, and
  `environment` in `cmd/finwise/main.go` carries it: the host's in `main`, a fixed one in a test.
- The work that gives every handler a view of each store per request, and makes the clock required
  and guarded in the API (finwise-jzw): a read handler's third parameter, today a `*ledger.Reader`
  (`ReadHandler` in `internal/api/reads.go`), is one value carrying a view of the ledger and a view of
  the app's database, the latter inside one read-only transaction opened for the request. Without
  `--db` that view is an empty one that answers nothing, so read code has one path.

**Recognition, as `serve` does it, with one exception.** Recognition does not open the file as a
database: it reads the file's first hundred bytes, which must be the header of an SQLite file carrying
the application id finwise stamps, `0x46494E57` (decimal 1179209303; bytes 68 to 71 of the header, big
endian). Any other file, the collector's snapshot included, is refused with its bytes untouched and no
file created beside it. Use the package's recognition, do not write a second one. The exception: for
`serve` a file that does not exist or is empty is a new database, which it creates; here a missing or
empty file is an error and is never created. A mistyped path must not leave a database behind, nor fix
the month a person "started" in it. This command also never runs a migration.

**The copy.** After recognition the command writes a consistent copy, in this order:

1. `VACUUM INTO` a uniquely named temporary file in the destination's directory. The same directory
   is what makes the last step possible; `VACUUM INTO` reads one consistent state of the source even
   while the server is writing to it, and it refuses a file that already holds anything.
2. Check the temporary file: its application id, and `PRAGMA integrity_check`.
3. Publish it with an operation that cannot replace a file: a hard link to the destination name, then
   removing the temporary name. A rename would replace whatever is at the destination; a link fails
   when the name is taken, which is the whole reason it is used.
4. On success, record the instant, from the injected clock, in the source database, as UTC in
   RFC 3339. If that record cannot be written, remove the copy just published and fail.

A destination that exists before, or appears meanwhile, is refused and untouched; every failure
removes only this command's temporary file. The one file besides the temporary one that the command
may ever remove is the copy it has itself just published, in the one case of step 4: a backup and its
record exist together or not at all. It never removes or replaces a file it did not publish in this
run. A plain file copy of a running database is not supported, because it can miss the write-ahead
log; the nightly backup of the later packaging work calls this command.

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| a backup's destination exists or appears meanwhile | refused; the destination and the database are untouched; no temporary file is left |
| `--db` points at a file that is not ours | refused; file untouched, no side file created |
| `--db` is missing or empty | an error; the file is not created |
| the instant cannot be recorded after the copy was published | the published copy is removed; the command fails |

All SQL here (`VACUUM INTO`, the two checks of the copy, the write to `meta`) is executed by
`internal/authored` through registered constants; `cmd/finwise` parses the flags, calls it and
reports. `VACUUM` cannot run inside a transaction. The check of the copy must not leave a `-wal`,
`-shm` or `-journal` file beside the published destination.

**The command line.** `run` in `cmd/finwise/main.go` knows `serve` and `hash-pin` and prints
`usage: finwise serve | hash-pin` in two places; `backup` joins both. The existing exit constants are
`exitFailure` (1) and `exitUsage` (2); `runServe` prints `finwise: <error>` to standard error. The
source is resolved the way `serve` resolves it, the flag `--db` first and then `FINWISE_DB`
(`firstNonEmpty` in `cmd/finwise/serve.go`), so the nightly job can run in the server's own
environment; `--to` is a flag only. Both a source and a destination are required. A message names a
path and a fixed reason, never the content of a
file: a raw SQLite error can quote a value, so errors carry fixed sentences, as
`UnreadableSnapshotError` in `internal/ledger/open.go` does.

**The settings read.** The instant recorded is what the settings screen's "last backup" shows, in
Brazil time like the last sync. Today `dataSettingsOf` (`internal/api/settings_data.go`) fills
`LastSync` as `momentWire{Day: string(brday.DayOf(finished)), Time: clockTimeOf(finished)}` and never
fills `LastBackup`; its comment says "This backend makes no backup, so there is none to show", and
`TestTheSettingsReportTheLastCompleteRunAndNoBackup` (`settings_test.go`) expects null.
`dataSettingsWire` in `settings.go` already has the field, and the contract already types it
(`DataSettings.lastBackup: Moment | null`, "Null when no backup has run", in
`web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`; `Moment` is a day and a time). The instant is stored as UTC in
RFC 3339 and shown in Brazil time: it is read through the request's view of the app's database and
written on the wire the same way as the last sync, the Brazil day and the time as `HH:MM`. With no
instant recorded, or no database configured, it stays null.

Nothing changes in `web/`: `web/src/screens/config/DataSection.vue` already prints
"Último backup: hoje às 02:15" for today, "Último backup: em 26/11 às 02:15" for another day and
"Último backup: —" for null, and its tests (`config.test.ts`, `web/src/test/first-run-fields.test.ts`)
already cover the three. The golden files `internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/settings.overview.json`
and `full/settings.overview.json` are answered without a database and keep `"lastBackup": null`. Do
not add a `readCase{…}` literal for a state with a backup: `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts` scans
every `_test.go` file of `internal/api` for those literals and requires each to have a golden file in
`empty/`. The read with a recorded instant is a test of its own.

**Left to the implementer.** No criterion below leaves a number or a representation open. What is
free is mechanism: the key under which the instant sits in `meta`, which is the package's, since
nothing outside the package reads `meta` by key; how a test makes a destination appear between the
checks and the publication (a hook, or two functions the test calls in turn), as long as the file
really is created after the destination was found free and before the link; and how a test makes the
record of the instant fail after the publication, as long as the copy really was published first.

**Privacy and conventions.** A backup is a whole copy of what a person authored. No test here touches
a real ledger or a real database: sources are created in temporary directories with invented
content, and the "collector's snapshot" of the refusal test is the invented one `ledgertest.New`
builds. The command prints paths and fixed sentences only. Work happens in the worktree it was given
and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a
session, a work item or a plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in
the money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant. Interface text
is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; a design value in a component comes from a
token (no component is touched here). `internal/authored` and `internal/api` log nothing here, and
`internal/api` reads the clock only from the request, never from the host.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `finwise backup --db <db> --to <dest>` over a database created by the package exits 0. `<dest>`
then carries application id 1179209303, answers `ok` to `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and holds the same
rows of `schema_migrations` and the same creation month as the source.
- [ ] After a success the destination's directory has gained exactly one entry, `<dest>`: no temporary
file and no `-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal` beside it.
- [ ] After a success with the clock at 2026-12-01T01:30:00Z, the instant stored in the source is the
RFC 3339 text `2026-12-01T01:30:00Z`, and `settings.overview` over that database answers
`"lastBackup": {"day":"2026-11-30","time":"22:30"}`. A second backup with the clock at
2026-12-02T05:15:00Z makes it `{"day":"2026-12-02","time":"02:15"}`.
- [ ] `settings.overview` answers `"lastBackup": null` over a database in which no backup was
recorded, and without a database. `git diff` shows no change under `internal/api/testdata/golden/`.
- [ ] A destination that exists before the command runs: the exit is non-zero, the destination's
SHA-256 is equal before and after, the source's SHA-256 is equal before and after, no instant is
recorded, and the destination's directory listing is equal before and after.
- [ ] A destination created after the command found the name free and before it publishes: the exit is
non-zero, the file that appeared is byte-identical afterwards, no instant is recorded, and the only
new entry in the directory is the file that appeared.
- [ ] Each failure the tests can force after the temporary file exists (the copy's check failing, the
link failing) leaves no temporary file.
- [ ] When the record of the instant fails after the copy was published (forced by the test), the exit
is non-zero, the published copy is gone, no instant is recorded, and the destination's directory
listing is equal to what it was before the command.
- [ ] Given as `--db`, each of these is refused with a non-zero exit, its SHA-256 and its directory
listing equal before and after, and no destination created: a foreign database in write-ahead mode;
an invented collector snapshot built by `ledgertest`; a database with one table and application id 1;
a text file that is not a database.
- [ ] A `--db` that does not exist is an error and is not created. A zero-byte `--db` is an error, is
still zero bytes afterwards, and leaves nothing in the destination's directory.
- [ ] A copy taken while another connection commits transactions of two rows each, in a loop, passes
both checks and holds an even number of those rows.
- [ ] A backup changes nothing in the source but the one recorded instant: `schema_migrations`, the
creation month and every other row read the same before and after.
- [ ] `FINWISE_DB` supplies the source when `--db` is absent, and the flag wins when both are given.
With neither, or without `--to`, the command exits with the usage status and touches no file; no
variable stands in for `--to`. `finwise` with no argument names `backup` in its usage line.
- [ ] A sentinel string stored in the source (invented, for example as a `method` in `changes`) appears
in neither stream of the command, on success and on every refusal above.
- [ ] Every statement added to `internal/authored` is a registered constant: the package's
registration and preparation tests pass with them and fail when one is left out.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, and the report names the break used for each: the link
replaced by a rename (a destination that exists, and one that appears, are both replaced); the removal
of the temporary file dropped; the instant recorded before the publication (a refusal then shows an
instant); the published copy left in place when the record of the instant fails; the check of the
copy skipped; the database opened the way `serve` opens it (a missing or empty `--db` becomes a
database); the settings read left at null.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, a copy taken during a write passes its checks, the
settings read shows the recorded instant, and a destination that exists or appears is not replaced.

## Tests
- Integration, `cmd/finwise`, in a new `backup_test.go` that uses the existing `runCommand` of
`finwise_test.go` with the injected clock, over temporary directories: the success and what the
directory holds after it; the source taken from `FINWISE_DB` and the flag winning over it; the usage
errors; the refusals of a source that is not ours, missing or empty, each with hashes and directory
listings; the sentinel in the output.
- Unit, `internal/authored`, over temporary files: the destination that exists; the destination that
appears between the checks and the publication; no temporary file after each forced failure; the
record of the instant failing after the publication, and the copy removed with it; the instant
recorded only on success, as RFC 3339 in UTC, and replaced by the next backup; the source otherwise
unchanged.
- Unit, `internal/authored`, two connections on one temporary file: the copy taken during a loop of
committed writes.
- Unit, `internal/api`, over the invented full ledger of `fixtures_test.go` and a temporary database:
`settings.overview` with an instant recorded on each side of midnight in Brazil, with none recorded,
and with no database.
- Golden: `settings.overview` over the two fixture ledgers, unchanged.
- Unit, source scans: the new statements registered and prepared.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `cmd/finwise/backup.go`, `cmd/finwise/backup_test.go`, `cmd/finwise/main.go`,
`internal/authored/`, `internal/api/settings_data.go`, `internal/api/settings.go`,
`internal/api/settings_test.go`
**Reads only:** `cmd/finwise/finwise_test.go`, `cmd/finwise/serve.go`, `internal/authored/migrations/`,
`internal/api/reads.go`, `internal/api/now.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`,
`internal/ledger/ledgertest/`, `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`,
`web/src/screens/config/DataSection.vue`, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`, `bin/ci`

A new command file and its line in `main.go`; in `internal/authored` the copy, its checks, the
publication, and the write and read of one `meta` value; in `internal/api` the one field of the
settings read. About six code files, most of them small, but in three packages, which is what makes it
`size:L` on the scale. No migration is added (`meta` exists), nothing in `web/` changes, and no golden
file changes.

## Recovery path
A backup that should not have been taken is undone by deleting the destination file. The command
itself never replaces a file, and the only copy it ever removes is the one it has just published when
it cannot record the instant. The instant it recorded stays in the database and only says when a copy
was last taken; the next backup replaces it. To restore the database from a backup: stop
the server; check the copy (`PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok`, the application id is
1179209303); put it in place of the database with no `-wal` or `-shm` file beside it; start the
server. A restore does not set the creation month again: the copy carries the one it was taken with.
close_reason: finwise backup --db <database> --to <file> writes a checked copy (VACUUM INTO a temporary name, application id and integrity_check on a connection that reports CHECK constraints, published by a link that never replaces a file) and records its instant in UTC in the source; a failed record withdraws only the copy it published. settings.overview answers the last backup as a Brazil day and time, null before the first. bin/ci green on the branch merged with main. Review: six independent mutations; three survived at first and two of them were defects (a copy violating a CHECK was published; a file that took the destination's name after the publication was deleted), now fixed with regression tests; the third (UTC) has a test. The implementer's seventeen breaks each failed a test. Found on the way and filed separately: a relative path to either store does not open.

title: Read pluggy-sync's snapshot through typed read-only queries
description:
## What changes for the user
Today everything finwise shows is an invented dataset; none of it is the person's own money. This is the first piece that reads the real ledger the collector writes every night. Nothing looks different on screen once it lands, but the app gains a tested way to ask that ledger for accounts, transactions, card bills, savings pots, investments and the state of the last synchronisation, and it refuses a ledger whose format it does not know instead of showing wrong numbers.

## Outcome
A Go module at the repository root (`github.com/gabrielassisxyz/finwise`) with a package that opens pluggy-sync's snapshot file strictly read-only for each call, pins its schema version, and answers typed queries over the documented surface only. It ships with the fixture builder every later Go test uses, a test that prepares every query against the real schema, an opt-in test over a real snapshot that reports counts only, and the Go toolchain joined to the gate and to CI.

## Context
finwise has no backend yet. `web/` is a Vue interface running on an in-memory stand-in. The backend will be one Go binary; this bead starts it and contains no HTTP.

**The ledger.** pluggy-sync is the separate, public collector that pulls bank data into SQLite every night. Beside its live database it publishes `pluggy-snapshot.db`: a verified copy written to a temporary file and swapped in by an atomic rename, mode 0600, journal mode `delete`. A reader uses the snapshot and never the live file. Nothing promises what an open handle sees across a swap, so the reader opens read-only, runs its query and closes, on every call.

**Version.** `PRAGMA user_version` is 1 today. The collector promises nothing to readers about it, so the reader accepts exactly 1 and returns a typed error for anything else, before any query runs.

**Surface.** Only this is stable: the nine current-state tables (`items`, `accounts`, `transactions`, `bills`, `investments`, `investment_transactions`, `consents`, `identities`, `categories`), the views listed in pluggy-sync's README, `daily_sightings` (used by a README query) and `runs`. Anything else is internal to the collector and must not be queried.

**What exists now.** On every current-state table a row is current when `state = 'present' AND ambiguous_run IS NULL`.

**The clean list of transactions** is a README query, not a view: the predicate above, joined to `document_coverage` with `covered = 1`, minus every `PENDING` row whose id appears in `pending_posted_candidates.pending_id` (the collector's heuristic pairing of a pending row with the posted row that replaced it). Copy the query and cite the README lines in a comment beside it; the README of the checkout at dispatch has it near lines 287-296.

**Transactions.** Columns are `id, account_id, date, description, amount, currency, type, category, raw`. Everything else lives in the `raw` JSON: `status` (`PENDING` or `POSTED`), `operationType`, `amountInAccountCurrency`, `currencyCode`, `descriptionRaw`, `paymentData` (`paymentMethod`, and `payer` and `receiver`, each with `name` and `documentNumber.value`) and `creditCardMetadata` (`cardNumber`, `billId`, `installmentNumber`, `totalInstallments`, `purchaseDate`, `billForecastDate`, `feeType`, `payeeMCC`). The `merchant` column is null on every row. `date` is a UTC timestamp on every row.

**Accounts and bills.** `accounts.type` is `BANK` or `CREDIT`. A card's limit, available limit, closing and due dates are in `accounts.raw.creditData`. The bank behind an account is told by `accounts.name` or the first segment of `accounts.raw.bankData.transferNumber`; the connector name is the same for every bank. `bills` has `due_date`, `closing_date`, `total_amount`, `minimum_payment`.

**Pots.** `reserved_balance_history` has one row per reserve entry of an account's latest sighting of a day. A pot's key is `reserve_id`, valid only when `stable_identity = 1`; names repeat across pots. The latest balance of each pot is the README query `reserves_as_of` (near lines 239-258); nothing is carried forward from an earlier day.

**Investments.** `investment_history` has one row per investment per day with `amount_gross`, `taxes`, `taxes2`, `amount_net`, `rate`, `due_date`, `status`. `amountOriginal` is never summed.

**Synchronisation.** The last sync is `max(finished_at)` over `runs` with `outcome = 'complete'`; a later run may be `partial`. A connection is in trouble when `items.status != 'UPDATED'`, `execution_status != 'SUCCESS'`, or its last update is older than 48 hours. `consents.expires_at` and `revoked_at` are null in practice; the expiry is `items.raw.consentExpiresAt`.

**Money and days.** Amounts arrive as floating point out of JSON. The reader converts every amount to integer cents (round half away from zero) at its boundary, so no caller ever adds floats. A period is given in Brazil days and converted to UTC bounds inside the reader, because a row at 02:30 UTC on the 1st belongs to the last day of the previous month in America/Sao_Paulo.

**Scope.** The reader returns rows faithfully and interprets nothing: what kind a transaction is, the sign convention of the app, taxes folded into purchases and the card's bill rules belong to later beads. Its types must still carry every field named above, parsed, so those beads never touch SQL.

**Privacy, the rule above all others.** The ledger is a real person's complete financial history and this repository is public. A real snapshot may be opened read-only to check schema, JSON keys and counts. No value from it is ever printed, copied, logged, committed or pasted. Every fixture and every test uses invented literals.

**Decided, with what lost.** `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, keeps one static binary) over the cgo driver. Reopening per call over a long-lived handle, because of the rename. Copying README queries with a citation over views added to the collector, which would change its schema version and need a release there; that is revisited once the queries have proven themselves.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `go test ./...` passes from the repository root with no environment variable set and writes nothing outside the tests' temporary directories.
- [ ] A fixture whose `user_version` is 2 yields the typed unsupported-version error from every query and no rows.
- [ ] The snapshot is opened read-only: a test attempts a write through the same open path and it fails, and the fixture file's SHA-256 is identical before and after running every query.
- [ ] A test replaces the fixture file by rename between two calls and the second call returns the new content.
- [ ] The clean list, over a fixture holding one row of each case (state not `present`, `ambiguous_run` set, not covered, `PENDING` with a posted pair, `PENDING` without a pair, `POSTED`), returns exactly the unpaired pending row, the posted row and the posted half of the pair.
- [ ] A transaction dated `2026-03-01T02:30:00Z` is returned for February 2026 and not for March 2026.
- [ ] `19.99` becomes 1999 cents, `-0.005` becomes -1, and a sum of one thousand rows of `0.10` is exactly 10000.
- [ ] The consent expiry is read from `items.raw.consentExpiresAt`; a fixture with `consents.expires_at` null and that key set returns the key's value.
- [ ] `internal/ledger/testdata/ledger-schema-v1.sql` is the collector's real schema, a test asserts it contains no `INSERT`, and a test prepares every query of the package against a database built from it. Renaming one selected column in any query makes that test fail.
- [ ] A test skipped unless `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set runs every query over that file and logs row counts only.
- [ ] `bin/ci` runs `gofmt -l` (failing on any output), `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build ./...`, and still ends with `CI green.`; the workflow installs the Go version named in `go.mod`; every existing step is unchanged.
- [ ] `go.mod` requires `modernc.org/sqlite` and nothing else directly.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` describes the Go side under "Stack & Commands" and states the real-ledger rule under "Tests".
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` on the branch and the opt-in run over a real snapshot completes with counts and no error.

## Tests
- Unit: cents conversion and rounding; Brazil-day and month bounds, including the daylight-free UTC-3 offset at month and year ends.
- Unit over synthetic fixtures: one test per query, each asserting the exact rows returned for a fixture that also holds rows that must be excluded.
- Unit: version refusal, read-only open, file hash unchanged, rename between calls.
- Golden: the schema file against every prepared query.
- Integration, opt-in: the whole query set over a real snapshot, counts only.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `internal/ledger/`, `internal/money/`, `internal/brday/`, `bin/ci`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/contract/`

Three small Go packages, all new: `internal/ledger` (the reader, its `ledgertest` fixture builder exported for other packages' tests, and its `testdata`), `internal/money` (integer cents) and `internal/brday` (a day and a month in Brazil time). The gate and the workflow gain Go steps and keep every existing one. Nothing under `web/` changes.
close_reason: internal/ledger opens the snapshot read-only on every call (mode=ro plus query_only), pins user_version 1 with a typed error, and answers accounts, the clean list, bills, pots, investments, identities and the sync state; internal/money holds integer cents and internal/brday gives Brazil days as UTC bounds. Every statement lives in one registry that a test prepares against the collector's real schema. bin/ci: CI green with the four Go steps. The opt-in run over a real snapshot completed with counts and no error. Correction to the bead text: the transactions table has no merchant column at all, rather than a column that is always null.

title: Leave one lookup helper of each kind for the transaction writes and remove the type nothing produces
description:
## Outcome
The writes that name transactions share one set of helpers: one function that looks one transaction up
and refuses an id the list does not show, one that reads an id and a text from the arguments, and one
that resolves a selection of several ids. The type `readOnlyError`, which nothing produces, is gone.
Nothing a person or a client can observe changes: every answer, refusal, recorded effect and index row is
as before.

## Context
**Why.** The write handlers of `internal/api` were written by several pieces of work running side by
side, and three of them each brought their own copy of the same helpers. The copies are correct; the cost
is that a rule about looking a transaction up now has to be changed in up to three places, and the work
that makes a lookup refuse a snapshot the ingest has not taken in touches exactly these call sites. This
item is done after that work, on the code it leaves.

**The terms.** A *write* is a method of the API that changes what the person authored. A write that names
a transaction resolves it with `lookupTarget` (`internal/api/transaction_target.go`), which finds the
listed transaction for a provider id and gives it its key in the app's index (`indexListed`); *found* is
false for an id the list does not show. A *refusal* is the answer `refused` with a reason; `not_found` is
the reason for an item that no longer exists. A *selection* is several ids sent by one bulk write, which
is all or nothing: every id is found before anything is written.

**What is duplicated, read line by line.**
- `countedTarget` (`transaction_count_writes.go`) and `targetNamedBy` (`transaction_tag_writes.go`) have
  identical bodies: `lookupTarget`, the lookup's error passed through, `refuse(reasonNotFound)` when not
  found. `countedTarget` is called in `transaction_count_writes.go` and
  `transaction_reimbursement_writes.go`, and by name in four test files
  (`transaction_count_writes_test.go`, `transaction_reimbursement_writes_test.go`,
  `transaction_reimbursement_step_undo_test.go`, `reimbursement_candidates_test.go`); `targetNamedBy`
  is called in `transaction_tag_writes.go` and `establishment_writes.go`, and by one test that keeps
  calling it. A third copy of the same refusal is written inline in `setReason`
  (`transaction_history_writes.go`). These lists were read on 2026-11-23 and other work adds tests:
  take the callers from the code.
- Three writes call `lookupTarget` directly and answer null, not a refusal, for an id the list does not
  show: `setLine`, `confirmLine` (`transaction_line_writes.go`) and `undoHistoryStep`
  (`transaction_history_writes.go`). They are not copies and stay as they are.
- `twoTextArguments` (`transaction_line_writes.go`, three callers) and `idAndText`
  (`transaction_tag_writes.go`, twelve callers in five files) both refuse anything but two arguments and
  read each as text. Their one difference: when the second argument is not a text, the first returns the
  first text with the error and the second returns two empty texts. No caller reads the texts when there
  is an error.
- Three functions resolve a selection, each with one caller: `targetsNamedBy` for `addTagToMany`,
  `everyListed` for `excludeMany`, `findManyListed` for `setLineForMany`. They differ in ways the callers
  and the tests depend on:
  - *How the ledger is read.* `targetsNamedBy` interprets the whole ledger in one pass (`listedLedger`).
    `everyListed` calls the single lookup's read once per id, which reads the ledger's rows again for each
    id. `findManyListed` reads the rows once and interprets each month once.
  - *An id the list does not show.* The first two refuse `not_found` themselves; `findManyListed` answers
    a boolean and its caller refuses.
  - *Indexing.* `targetsNamedBy` indexes every row itself, after every id is found, and answers targets
    with their keys; the other two answer listed rows and their callers index while they write.
  - *Repeated ids.* The first two take each id once, the first occurrence; `findManyListed` leaves that to
    its caller, which passes `distinct(ids)`.
  - *The order of refusals in the line write.* `setLineForMany` must refuse an unknown id before a month
    that lacks the line, whatever their order in the selection.
- `readOnlyError` (`errors.go`) is a type a handler returned to decline an input while part of the app was
  read-only. No handler returns it any more. What is left is the type, its case in `classify` and one case
  of `TestHandlerErrorsAreMappedByClassWhateverTheMethod` (`refusal_test.go`). The error kind `read_only`
  itself stays: the router answers it directly for a server without a database of its own and for a
  method with no handler (`serveChange` in `writes.go`).

**What a single resolver has to keep.** Every id found before anything is indexed or written; each id
once, in the order given, first occurrence; `not_found` for the whole call when one id is not listed, with
nothing recorded and no index row added; for the line write, the unknown id refused before the missing
line; the rows found being the ones the single lookup finds, which
`TestTheSelectionFindsAndIndexesWhatTheSingleLookupDoes` pins for the whole-ledger pass. That test calls
`targetsNamedBy` by name: its call becomes the single resolver followed by the indexing the tag write
does, and what it asserts stays. The shape that
fits all three callers is a resolver that answers the listed rows and leaves indexing to the caller; which
of the two efficient readings it uses is the implementer's, as long as the ledger's rows are read once per
call.

**What the work this item waited for left.** `indexListed` now takes the request's ledger view and
refuses to index from a snapshot whose projected run is not the run the ingest took in last, with an
error the router recognises by identity (`errSnapshotNotTakenIn` in `transaction_target.go`): the router
then has the snapshot taken in and tries the write once more. A helper of this item passes every error
of the lookup and of `indexListed` through exactly as it got it. Wrapped so that `errors.Is` cannot see
through it, or turned into a refusal, that error would end the write instead of retrying it.
`TestABulkWriteOverTheNextSnapshotFindsThePostedRowUnderThePendingRowsKey` and the other tests of
`take_in_sequences_test.go` and `take_in_router_test.go` pin this for a selection and pass unchanged.

**Tests that pin the behaviour**, all in `internal/api`: for the tag selection,
`TestABulkTagTagsEachTransactionOnceAndItsUndoRemovesOnlyWhatItAdded`,
`TestABulkTagWithAnUnknownIDRefusesTheWholeCallAndTouchesNothing`,
`TestABulkWriteLeavesNothingEvenWhenItsCallerKeepsTheChange` and
`TestTheSelectionFindsAndIndexesWhatTheSingleLookupDoes`; for the exclusion,
`TestASelectionTakesTheReasonOnceOnEachOfItsTransactions`,
`TestOneUnknownIDRefusesTheWholeSelectionAndChangesNoTableOrTheIndex`,
`TestASelectionIsFoundWholeBeforeAnyOfItIsWritten` and
`TestUndoingASelectionGivesTheMonthsListBackAsItWas`; for the lines, `TestSetLineForManyIsAllOrNothing`;
and the write cases of the conformance suite with their committed effects files.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `countedTarget` and `twoTextArguments` no longer exist, their callers use the one remaining function
of each pair, and `setReason` uses the lookup helper in place of its inline copy.
- [ ] `setLine`, `confirmLine` and `undoHistoryStep` still answer null for an id the list does not show;
their tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] One function resolves a selection for `addTagToMany`, `excludeMany` and `setLineForMany`;
`targetsNamedBy`, `everyListed` and `findManyListed` no longer exist as three.
- [ ] That function reads the ledger's rows once per call, shown by a test that counts the readings for a
selection of three ids in two months.
- [ ] Every test named in the Context passes with no change to what it asserts; a test whose only change
is the name of a helper it calls counts as unchanged.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/` changes: `git diff --stat` over that directory is
empty.
- [ ] `readOnlyError`, its case in `classify` and its case in `refusal_test.go` are removed, and a server
without a database of its own still answers `read_only` for a write, shown by the existing test of it
passing unchanged.
- [ ] The diff adds no exported name and holds only the files this item lists as edited; of the test
files, only `transaction_count_writes_test.go` and `refusal_test.go` change beyond the call of a helper
whose name goes away.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`.
- [ ] Done when: one helper of each kind is left, every pinned test and every golden file is as it was,
and the dead type is gone.

## Tests
- Unit, in `internal/api/transaction_count_writes_test.go`: the readings of the ledger counted for one
selection. `reimbursement_candidates_test.go` already counts readings of the whole ledger by taking the
reading as a function, which is one way to count without an exported name.
- Integration, existing: the tests named in the Context and the write cases of the conformance suite,
passing without a change to their assertions.
- Golden: none moves.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/transaction_count_writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_tag_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_history_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_reimbursement_writes.go`, `internal/api/establishment_writes.go`,
`internal/api/errors.go`, `internal/api/refusal_test.go`, `internal/api/transaction_count_writes_test.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_tag_writes_test.go`, `internal/api/transaction_reimbursement_writes_test.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_reimbursement_step_undo_test.go`, `internal/api/reimbursement_candidates_test.go`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/transaction_target.go`, `internal/api/settings_counterpart_writes.go`,
`internal/api/writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_line_writes_test.go`,
`internal/api/take_in_sequences_test.go`, `internal/api/take_in_router_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/`, `bin/ci`

Seven source files of one package and six test files, four of which change only where they call a helper
by a name that goes away. No store function, no contract type and nothing of
the interface is touched. The lookup itself (`lookupTarget`, `indexListed`) is read and not edited: it
belongs to the work this item waits for.

## Recovery path
Nothing stored changes. Reverting the pull request brings the copies back and nothing else.
close_reason: One helper of each kind is left for the writes that name transactions: targetNamedBy refuses an id the list does not show, idAndText reads an id and a text, and listedSelection resolves a selection, reading the ledger's rows once per call and leaving indexing to its caller; the copies and the error type nothing produced are removed. Verified by the gate on the branch after main was merged in, by no golden file moving, by every pinned test passing with its assertions unchanged, by two new tests (the readings counted; every bulk write finding its whole selection before it indexes any), by the author's twelve deliberate breaks and by four more in review: three killed by a named test, one judged to change no answer. One answer changes and is said in the pull request: an empty selection over a missing snapshot now answers ledger_unavailable from the bulk exclusion too.

title: Let the person choose a pot's bucket and the budget lines it feeds, and count every pot where its bucket says in the pots list, a pot's page, the settings, the net worth, its chart and the home screen
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every savings pot counts where the bank's own word puts it: a reserve is reserved money and an
investment is invested, and the settings screen's bucket menu and its "Editar" of the budget lines a pot
feeds both answer that the app is read-only. A pot the person keeps as their everyday money cannot be
counted as available, and no pot can say which budget lines it pays for. After this lands the person
chooses a pot's bucket (Disponível, Reservado or Investido) and the budget lines it feeds, both are kept
after a restart and can be taken back, and the pots screen, a pot's page, the settings, the Patrimônio
screen with its chart, and the net worth on the home screen all count that pot where the person put it,
including a third group, "Disponível", on the pots screen. The bucket is a label of today: changing it
moves that pot in every month of the chart, since no history of buckets is kept. A pot the bank cannot
identify from one day to the next refuses both choices with a sentence that says why. What the person
would notice if this were wrong: the net worth's parts no longer adding to the same total, the chart's
current month disagreeing with the cards above it, a pot counted twice or in no part at all, or a line
linked to a pot that the settings do not show.

## Outcome
`settings.setPotBucket` and `settings.toggleLinkedLine` have handlers: each refuses a pot the bank does
not identify stably (`unstable_pot`) and a pot the ledger does not have (`not_found`), the second
resolves the line's name in the current month's budget (`unknown_line` otherwise) and moves a line that
another pot has, and each writes through the pots' store as one recorded change that `changes.undo` takes
back exactly. Every read that places a pot uses its effective bucket, the one the person chose or else the
bank's default: `savingsPots.list` (grouped reserved, invested, available, in that order),
`savingsPots.detail`, the pots of `settings.overview`, `netWorth.overview` with its buckets and every
point of its chart, and the net worth of `home.summary`. The settings overview and a pot's page show the
lines linked to each pot by their name in the current month's budget. On a server without the app's
database every answer is byte for byte what it is today.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite snapshot that a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, and the file may be swapped
under it at any time. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, owned by the Go package `internal/authored`,
where everything the person authors is kept; the server has one only when started with `--db`, and
without it every write answers `read_only`, as today. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under
`web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it is the only existing statement of how writes
behave, and its behaviour is the rule here except where this text says the server departs from it. *The
manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, the generated description of every API method (route,
class, argument and result schemas, error envelope). *The recorder* is the layer of `internal/authored`
through which every change to the app's database is written; *the journal* is what it writes; *undo* is
the inverse of a change's recorded effects. *A pot* is a savings pot or an investment as the pots
screens list it; its id is `reserve:<account>/<reserveId>` for a bank reserve whose identity the bank
keeps, `investment:<id>` for an investment, and `slot:<account>/<n>` for a reserve whose identity the
bank does not keep, in which case `<n>` is only its place among that account's unidentified reserves on
the latest day and names a different pot from one day to the next (`internal/api/pots_model.go`). *A
bucket* is where a pot's money counts in the net worth: `Disponível`, `Reservado` or `Investido`. *A
budget line* has an integer id minted by the app's database and a name that belongs to a budget
version; *the budget in force for a month* is the latest version starting at or before it. *The current
month* is the Brazil month of the instant in the request's context. *A golden file* is the committed, exact
answer of one call over an invented fixture. *The gate* is `bin/ci`.

**What earlier work provides.** None of it is in the repository when this text is written; each piece is
delivered before this bead starts, and its interfaces are to be read in the code as that work left them.

- The pots' store (finwise-rju: the tables that keep a pot's bucket and its linked lines): migration
  `0005_pots` adds `pot_settings(pot_id, bucket)`, an attribute table of optional facts keyed by the pot's
  id as the API answers it, `bucket` one of the three or null for "the read side's default", and
  `pot_lines(line_id, pot_id)`, `line_id` referencing `lines` and unique, so a line is linked to at most
  one pot; the database itself refuses a line linked twice and a bucket outside the three. Store functions
  in `internal/authored` set or clear a pot's bucket (setting the stored bucket again records no effect)
  and toggle a link for a line and a pot (remove it from this pot, move it from another pot in the same
  change, or add it; undo of a move puts the line back where it was), through the recorder; reads answer
  a pot's stored bucket, the lines of a pot (in a deterministic order) and the pot of a line, on the
  authored view, the empty view answering none. `authoredtest` has builders for both. Nothing there
  deletes a link except the person's toggle.
- The recorder and undo (finwise-wi4): every change to the app's database is written through it;
  `changes.undo` is refused with `refused` / `stale_change` when a later change still in force touched the
  same unit.
- The views (finwise-jzw): a handler gets one value carrying a view of each store for the request; the ledger
  view is one handle and one read-only transaction, so every ledger query of a request sees one snapshot;
  the authored view is one read-only transaction, empty on a server without `--db`. Each slice adds the
  reads of the tables it owns.
- The `refused` kind (finwise-our): `{"error":{"kind":"refused","reason":"<reason>"}}`, HTTP 409, with a
  reason from a closed list; the sentences live in the interface (finwise-diw: the interface learns the
  reasons and their sentences).
- Write dispatch (finwise-2s5): a registered write, on a server with the app's database, has its arguments
  validated against the manifest (a `Bucket` outside the three is `bad_request` before the handler runs),
  then runs inside one immediate transaction with a recorder holding one open change (author `person`,
  the qualified method, the instant, the Brazil day); the dispatcher commits, any failure rolls back and
  answers `internal`. A write whose result cannot be null and that changes nothing records an *empty
  change* and answers its id. `writesWithoutHandler` names the writes still without a handler.
  `ledger_unavailable` is answered by a write as by a read, through the same classifier, when the
  snapshot it needs is missing.
- The write conformance harness (finwise-fst): recorded-change cases whose effects match a golden file under
  `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/` and whose undo returns a canonical dump of every journaled table
  to the one taken before; one refusal case per reason, each expecting 409, its reason, a body that
  validates against the manifest's error schema, and no table changed; a list in a test file names the
  reasons with no producer yet, and the slice that first produces one removes it and adds its case.
  `authoredtest` builds invented authored states; `authoredReadCases` are reads over the full invented
  ledger with an invented authored state, golden under `testdata/golden/full-authored/`, of a type of
  their own so the interface's equality test does not find them.
- The budget's tables (finwise-ef7: the budget stored by month with stable line ids): `lines(id, builtin)`
  with the built-in fees line `Tarifas e juros`, budget versions and their lines with names owned by each
  version, and one function for "the lines a month's budget has" that resolves a name to an id in a
  month, the fees line included whenever that month's budget has at least one line.
**What the code is today (each point read in the file named).**

- `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`: `setPotBucket(potId: string, bucket: Bucket)` and
  `toggleLinkedLine(potId: string, line: string)` ("Links the line to the pot, or unlinks it when it was
  linked"), both `Promise<ChangeResult>`, never null. `SettingsPot` is `{id, name, bank, cdiPercent,
  bucket: Bucket | null, linkedLines: string[]}`. `web/src/api/contract/savings-pots.ts`: `Bucket` is
  `'Disponível' | 'Reservado' | 'Investido'`; `SavingsPotRow.bucket` and `SavingsPotGroup.bucket` may be
  null; `PotLinkedLine` is `{name, share: number | null}`, "`share` is its part of the balance when several
  lines share the pot". `web/src/api/contract/net-worth.ts`: `NetWorthBucket.bucket` is a `Bucket`.
- `internal/api/pots_model.go`: `bucketReserved` and `bucketInvested` and the comment "A pot's bucket is
  the bank's own word for what it is until the person assigns one". `entryOf` gives every reserve entry
  `bucketReserved`; `investmentEntryOf` (`pots_investments.go`) gives every investment `bucketInvested`;
  `bucketAvailable` (`Disponível`) is in `accounts.go`. `loadPots(ctx, reader, withYield)` builds the
  entries: reserve entries (a stable one is kept when it is gone, as closed; an unstable one that is gone
  is dropped), then investments, of which `withoutBackedInvestments` drops those the ledger shows back a
  connection's reserves, so they are not counted twice. `withYield` false skips the slow yield work, as
  `readSettingsOverview` and `readHomeSummary` already ask.
- `internal/api/pots.go`: `(*potsView).groups` lists only `bucketReserved` and `bucketInvested`, in that
  order, each with its subtotal, a group with no pot left out; within a group the entries' order
  (`sortedEntries`: bank, then name, then id). `rowOf` answers `entry.bucket`.
- `internal/api/pots_detail.go`: `detailOf` answers `Bucket: entry.bucket` and `LinkedLines: []any{}`
  ("the budget lines a pot feeds are the person's to author, so they are the contract's empty value");
  `accountSideDetail` answers a bank account's unclaimed movements under the account's id, with bucket
  `Disponível`; it is not a pot.
- `internal/api/settings.go`: `settingsPotsOf` lists the open pots "in the order and the bucket the pots
  screen gives them", with `LinkedLines: []string{}`.
- `internal/api/net_worth.go`: `partsOf` adds the bank accounts' balances to available and each entry's
  balance to the part its bucket names (the `bucketAvailable` case exists already and is never reached);

  a closed entry with nothing in it. `home.summary` (`home.go`) answers its net worth from the same
  `partsOf`.
- `internal/api/net_worth_chart.go`: `pointOf` builds each month's point at its end: per bank account

  `view.investmentDays` at its latest day up to then, to invested. So the chart fixes each pot's bucket by
  its source and never asks a pot for its bucket.
- Tests that pin today's answers: `TestEveryPotNamesItsBucketAsTheBankSaysIt` (`pots_test.go`),
  `TestAReserveEntryIsReservedAndAnInvestmentIsInvested` and
  `TestTheCurrentMonthsPointIsTheNetWorthShownAboveIt` (`net_worth_test.go`),
  `TestTheHomeNetWorthIsTheOneTheNetWorthScreenShows` (`home_test.go`),
  `TestEachPotOfTheSettingsHasTheBucketTheSavingsPotsListGivesIt` and
  `TestTheSettingsLeaveOutAClosedPotAndKeepBothBucketsOfTheFullLedger` (`settings_test.go`). On a server

- The full invented ledger (`internal/api/fixtures_test.go`, `fixtures_savings_test.go`) has the pots

  50.00), `investment:inv-it-1` (7000.00), `investment:inv-nu-1` (3000.00) and `investment:inv-nu-2`
  (closed). Its net worth is 14135.46: available 2059.66, reserved 2075.80, invested 10000.00; its chart
  has points for 2026-01, 2026-02 and 2026-03, the last equal to those parts.
- The stand-in: `web/src/api/fake/settings.ts` (`setPotBucket` sets the pot's bucket and
  `toggleLinkedLine` adds or removes a name in the pot's list, both recording a change even for a pot
  that does not exist, neither refusing anything, and a line may sit in two pots; a toggle also forgets
  the pot's seeded split of its balance between lines, `lineShares`), `savings-rules.ts` (`groupByBucket`
  with the order Reservado, Investido, Disponível, then the pots with no bucket; `linkedLines`),
  `savings-pots.ts`, `net-worth.ts`, and `settings.test.ts` ("moves the net worth when a pot gets a bucket,

  unlinked one").
- The interface: `web/src/screens/config/PotsSection.vue` sends `setPotBucket(pot.id, bucket)` from the
  bucket menu and `toggleLinkedLine(pot.id, line)` with a name picked from the line menu, then bumps the
  revision counter, which makes the settings screen fetch its overview again. No file under `web/`
  changes in this work.

**Which pot a write may name.** Both writes resolve the pot through the same pots read the API answers
them with, in the request's ledger snapshot and without the yield (`loadPots` with `withYield` false):

- an id with the prefix `slot:` is refused with `refused` / `unstable_pot`, whatever the ledger lists
  under it today, because that id names a different pot tomorrow;
- an id that is not one of the pots that read lists, closed ones included, is refused with `refused` /
  `not_found`: an unknown id, an investment left out because the ledger shows it backs the reserves (it is
  not listed), and a bank account's id even where `savingsPots.detail` answers its account side;
- a closed pot is a pot the ledger has: both writes accept it;
- with the snapshot missing the write answers `ledger_unavailable` and records nothing.

The result cannot be null, so an unknown target is a refusal and not a null answer. A refusal changes no
table and adds no row to the journal.

**`setPotBucket(potId, bucket)`.** It stores the bucket for the pot; the pot then counts there in every
read below. Setting the bucket the pot already has stored records an empty change. Whether choosing the
bucket equal to the read side's default stores it or clears the row is the implementer's: every answer is
the same either way, and the effects golden file pins the choice. Undo brings back the bucket before,
and so the default for a pot that had none stored.

**`toggleLinkedLine(potId, line)`.** The line is named by its name and has no month of its own, so it is
resolved in the budget in force for the current month, the fees line included when that budget has at
least one line; a name that budget does not have (including one only an earlier version of the budget
has, and the empty name) is refused with `refused` / `unknown_line`. The link is stored by line id. If
the line is linked to this pot, the link is removed; if it is linked to another pot, it moves to this one
in the same change; otherwise it is added. Undo restores the link as it was, on the pot it was on. Which
of the pot's checks and the line's check comes first is the implementer's, pinned by a test. Only a
provision or reserve line's link has an effect elsewhere (the budget's balance cell and the payday's
transfers, below); any other line the current month's budget has may be linked, as in the stand-in.

**What the reads answer.**

- *The effective bucket* of a pot is the bucket stored for it, else the read side's default (a reserve is
  `Reservado`, an investment `Investido`). A `slot:` pot always has the default. No read answers a null
  bucket.
- `savingsPots.list({includeClosed})`: the groups in the stand-in's order, `Reservado`, `Investido`,
  `Disponível`, each the pots of that effective bucket in the order the entries have today, with its
  subtotal; a group with no pot shown is left out; a closed pot is shown only with `includeClosed`.
- `savingsPots.detail(id)`: `bucket` is the effective bucket; `linkedLines` lists the lines linked to the
  pot, each `{name, share: null}`. The share of a pot's balance per line is deferred work (a pot that
  several lines share has no split until a later plan), so it is always null; the stand-in's seeded
  `lineShares` have no source here. The account side of `accountSideDetail` is unchanged. The pot's
  contribution state is another slice's (finwise-66k: the payday's transfers, which also give a pot's page its
  contribution) and is not touched here.
- `settings.overview().pots`: the open pots as today, each with its effective bucket and `linkedLines`,
  the names of its linked lines.
- A linked line is shown by the name the current month's budget gives it, so a rename shows at once. A
  link whose line the current month's budget no longer has is not shown, and its row stays: a budget save
  never clears what names a line without belonging to a month, because a save for a later month must not
  touch the current one (finwise-oib: a save clears only the transactions' references). The order of the names
  is the implementer's, deterministic and pinned by a test (the order the links were made needs a
  position column; the line menu's order of the current month needs none).
- `netWorth.overview`: `partsOf` and `bucketsOf` place each pot by its effective bucket; under
  `Disponível` the bank accounts come first and then the pots in that bucket. The total is still the sum
  of the three parts, which is unchanged by any bucket.
- The chart: every point places each pot by its effective bucket, pot by pot. A reserve row of the
  balance history counts in the bucket of the pot it belongs to (a stable row's pot id is
  `reserve:<account>/<reserveId>`; a row whose identity the bank does not keep counts as `Reservado`, the
  default, since no write can reach it), and an investment's days count in that investment's bucket. A
  bucket is a label of today: changing it relabels every past point of the chart, and no history of
  buckets is kept. The current month's point still equals the parts shown above it.
- `home.summary`'s `netWorth` follows, because it reads the same parts.
- Without `--db` the authored view is empty: every pot has its default and no link, and every answer is
  byte for byte what it is today.

**Why, and what lost.** A pot is identified by the ledger's id, and a `slot:` id changes between days, so
a write to one is refused rather than stored against a pot it will not name tomorrow. Rejected: storing
it and letting it apply to whatever pot holds that slot next. Links are by line id and resolved in the
current month, because a pot's link has no month of its own. Rejected: validating against the
transaction's month (there is none) or joining by name, which would let a renamed line drop its pot. A
line belongs to at most one pot, so linking it elsewhere moves it. Rejected: the stand-in's freedom to
put one line in two pots, which would count its planned amount into two transfers. Pot targets ("Rainy
Funds") have no control in this plan: the budget's Rainy Funds group is answered empty and no pot shows a
target.

**Where this departs from the stand-in on purpose,** each pinned by a test that the final report names:
an unknown pot and a `slot:` pot are refused (the stand-in records a change for anything); an unknown
line is refused and a line is linked by id, resolved in the current month (the stand-in stores any
name); a line linked to another pot moves (the stand-in lets it sit in two); there is never a pot with no
bucket and never a split of a balance between lines; the chart relabels its past points.

**Failure paths that touch this work.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing while writing | the write answers `ledger_unavailable`; nothing is recorded |
| the snapshot is swapped during a request | the request finishes on the snapshot it opened |
| a write fails halfway, or waits out the lock | one transaction: nothing of it is kept; `internal` |
| an undo meets a later change of the same pot or line | `refused` / `stale_change`; nothing is restored |
| a pot closes or leaves the ledger | its row in `pot_settings` and its links stay; nothing is deleted |
| a linked line is renamed or removed from the current month's budget | the link holds by id; a rename shows the new name, a removal hides the link |

**Known next users, not built here,** which read the store's lookups directly: the budget's view joins a
provision or reserve line to the pot it is linked to, never to a pot of the same name (finwise-jsx: the
budget's arithmetic on the server); the payday derives one transfer per pot that has linked provision or
reserve lines and treats a line linked to a closed pot, or to one the ledger no longer has, as linked to
none (finwise-66k). The screens that show these answers fetch again when something was written (finwise-xu2:
the net worth screen, the pots list and a pot's page refetching on a new revision).

**Left to the implementer** (what makes this bead `spec:open`), each with what constrains it: whether a
bucket equal to the default is stored or clears the row; the order of the linked names; the order of the checks; how the
chart's reserve rows find their pot; the names of new files.

**Privacy and conventions.** Nothing here needs a real ledger. A real ledger is a person's whole financial
history and this repository is public: fixtures are invented, and no value from a real snapshot (an
amount, a description, a name, a document, an id) is ever printed, logged or copied into a file, a
commit, a bead or a pull request. Work in your own git worktree, on your own branch, and stop at local
commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a
plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; a test
already forbids floats in `internal/api` and covers `internal/authored`. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is
English; this work adds no interface text. A design value in a component comes from a token; this work
touches no component. Register the two handlers in a registration function of this slice's own
file, so the sibling settings slices do not edit the same lines; `settings.go` is edited only in
`settingsPotsOf`. New files in `internal/api` log nothing: the request log holds the verb, the route, the
status, the duration and the error kind, never an argument, a body, a pot id or a line's name.

## Acceptance criteria

The harness and the gate
