title: Take a new snapshot in before a write looks a transaction up, so a write never moves the index ahead of the ingest
description:
## What changes for the user
The app learns about new bank data in two ways: a background step that runs every few minutes, and
whatever the person happens to touch on screen. Today, if the person changes a transaction in the minutes
after new bank data arrived and before the background step ran, two things can go wrong, and nothing on
screen says so. A card purchase that was pending and has now been posted by the bank can lose the line,
the tags and the note the person gave it while it was pending: the posted purchase shows up empty, as if
never seen. And a purchase whose date the bank moved into another month can leave the app in a state in
which every "Desfazer", of anything, answers "Isso já foi alterado depois e não pode mais ser desfeito."
until the next time a budget is saved. After this lands, whenever the person changes a transaction the
app first takes the new bank data in properly, so the posted purchase keeps what was said about the
pending one, undo keeps working, and the change the person made can itself be undone.

## Outcome
A write that looks a transaction up never reads a snapshot the ingest has not taken in. When it finds
that it would, nothing of it is recorded, the server runs the ingest over the new snapshot, and the write
is tried once more over fresh views. If the snapshot still is not the one taken in, the write is answered
as a failure and nothing is recorded. Only the ingest moves the index of transactions forward to a new
snapshot; a write's lookup leaves a known transaction's index row as the ingest left it.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger snapshot* is an SQLite file
that a separate collector fills from the banks, usually once a night, and replaces by renaming a new file
over the old one; the app only reads it. Each collection is *a run* with a growing id, and the snapshot
records which run its current state belongs to, *the projected run* (`(*View).ProjectedRun` in
`internal/ledger/sync.go`). *The app's database* keeps what the person authors. It holds *the index*
(`tx_index`): one row per transaction the app has met, under a key of the app's own (`TxKey`) that
everything authored about the transaction hangs on, with the transaction's day and whether the bank still
calls it pending. The index is not journaled. *The journal* records every other change so it can be
undone; a change has an author, `person` or `rule`. *The ingest* (`internal/ingest`, `ingest.Run`) takes
a snapshot in as one change by `rule`: it refreshes the index rows of the transactions the ledger lists;
it *pairs* a pending row that vanished with the posted row that replaced it, which has a different id
from the bank, so that the posted row takes the pending row's key; it clears, for a transaction whose
month moved, its references to budget lines the new month lacks; and it evaluates new transactions. It
then records the run it took in (`RecordIngestedRun`, read back by `LastIngestedRun`, in
`internal/authored/meta.go`). The server runs it at start in a goroutine, on a timer (ten minutes by
default), after a budget save, and by the command `finwise ingest`.

**How a write reaches the index.** Every write of the API that names a transaction resolves it through
`indexListed` in `internal/api/transaction_target.go`, the only caller of
`(*Recorder).IndexTransaction` in that package. Called for a transaction the index knows, it overwrites
the index row with the facts of the snapshot the request reads; for one it has never met, it mints a new
key. It does this from whatever snapshot the request reads, taken in or not. The request's ledger view is
opened lazily, at its first query, and stays on that one file for the whole request.

**The two defects, read in the code and not yet reproduced by a test.**
1. *What was authored on a pending purchase is left behind.* The pairing only considers posted rows the
index has never met (`newPosted` in `internal/ingest/pairing.go`; the test
`TestAPostedRowTheIndexAlreadyHoldsIsNeverPaired` pins it for a row the ingest itself indexed). When a
write looks the posted row up before the ingest pairs it, the lookup mints a new, empty key for it. The
ingest then skips it, the pending row's key keeps the line, tags and note and is listed by nothing, and
the rules evaluate the posted row as a new transaction. Nearly every card purchase goes from pending to
posted, so every night's snapshot offers this.
2. *Every undo is refused.* After each undo a check (`noStrayLineReferences` in
`internal/authored/line_references.go`) reads the whole index and refuses the undo if any transaction
points at a budget line that the budget of its month, by the index's day, lacks. The ingest clears such
references for the transactions whose month it sees move, by comparing the index's day with the listed
day (`refreshAndPair` in `internal/ingest/pairing.go`). When a write's lookup has already moved the
index's day, the ingest sees no move and clears nothing, on that run or any later one; only a budget save
clears, over the whole index. Until then every undo, and every step taken back from a transaction's
history, is refused with the sentence for a stale change. A transaction in that state is not dropped from
any total: the figures read it as uncategorised.

Both have one root: a write reads a snapshot the ingest has not taken in, and moves the index without
doing what the ingest does. The window is the time between the collector replacing the snapshot and the
next run of the ingest, plus the first moments after the server starts, while the first run is still
going.

**What was decided, and what lost.**
- *The ingest goes first; the lookup does not learn to pair or to clear.* Clearing inside the lookup was
  considered: it fixes the second defect only, records the clearing inside the person's own change (so
  that undoing that one write is refused), and leaves the first defect, whose fix is to run the pairing
  before the lookup anyway.
- *The rule is enforced at the door, inside the write's own change.* Inside `indexListed`, before the
  index is touched: the projected run of the snapshot the request reads must equal the run taken in last.
  Read there, under the write lock the change holds, the comparison cannot go stale: the view stays on
  its file and no other writer can record a newer run. A step before every write was rejected: it would
  make a write that names no transaction (a setting) open the snapshot and fail when the snapshot is
  missing, and it would leave a gap when the snapshot is replaced between that step and the lookup.
- *One take-in, one retry.* When the comparison fails, the change is abandoned with nothing recorded, the
  router asks the server to run the ingest, opens fresh views and runs the handler once more. A handler
  has no effect outside its change, so running it again is safe; what the router does after a commit runs
  once, after the attempt that committed. If the comparison fails again, the write is answered `internal`
  and nothing is recorded. Going on without the take-in was rejected: it reopens both defects.
- *The take-in runs outside the write's change.* A change begun inside another's transaction would wait
  for a lock its own caller holds (the comment above `serveJournal` in `internal/api/writes.go` says the
  same of journal methods), so the first attempt is rolled back before the ingest is called.
- *A snapshot with no projected run is unavailable, not a server error.* A lookup that cannot learn the
  run because the snapshot records none answers `ledger_unavailable`, as a missing snapshot does today;
  `classify` in `internal/api/errors.go` has no case for that error yet and would answer `internal`.
- *No refusal reason is added.* The closed list of reasons, the interface and the stand-in backend are
  not touched: the person reads the sentences that exist for `internal` and `ledger_unavailable`.

**What the server offers for this.** The router gets what it calls after a budget save through
`api.Config.AfterBudgetSaved` (`internal/api/router.go`), built in `cmd/finwise/serve.go` from the
server's ingester (`cmd/finwise/ingest.go`): `internal/api` does not call the ingest itself. The same
shape serves the take-in: a second function on `api.Config`, which unlike the first returns its error.
Every recorded write passes through `serveWrite` and every journal method (`changes.undo`,
`transactions.applyLineToEstablishment`, the second of which indexes every purchase it moves) through
`serveJournal`, both in `internal/api/writes.go`. Runs of the ingest are not serialised by a lock of
their own: each is one change, the database admits one writer, and the run decides again under that lock
whether the snapshot was already taken in (`stopsAt` in `internal/ingest/run.go`). A snapshot older than
the run taken in is never taken in. A run for the triggers that stop at a run already taken in returns
after opening the snapshot and two small reads, without reading the ledger's rows. A run is logged as its
trigger and counts, or its trigger and the kind of its failure; tests of `cmd/finwise`
(`requireOnlyCountsAndKinds`, `triggerNames`) fail for anything else.

**Tests that exist, and what they lack.** No test sends a write across a replaced snapshot. The ingest's
tests have a harness that writes the next night's snapshot over the ledger path (`world.night` in
`internal/ingest/harness_test.go`), and `cmd/finwise` has `inventedNight` and `startServerWith`, which
start the real server over a snapshot and a database. The router's tests build an environment from an
`api.Config` with options (`newTestEnv`, `newCaseEnv`, `newCaseEnvCalling`). The conformance suite of the
writes runs over a scratch database on which no ingest ever ran, so under the new rule its environments
have to declare the fixture's run as taken in; a helper of the store's test package does that, and no
committed golden file should move.

**No repair is owed.** Nobody uses a database fed by writes yet, so there is none to mend. A database
that already holds a line reference its month lacks is cleared by the next budget save, as today.

## Steps to Reproduce
Both are sequences over invented data; neither exists as a test today.

*The pending purchase.*
1. A snapshot lists a pending card purchase. The ingest takes it in. The person puts it on a line, gives
   it a tag and a note.
2. The collector writes the next snapshot: the pending row is gone and a posted row with another id, the
   same account, amount and establishment, is listed.
3. Before any run of the ingest over that snapshot, the person adds a tag to the posted row
   (`transactions.addTag`).
4. The ingest runs.
5. Expected: the posted row shows the line, the first tag and the note, with the new tag. Actual: it
   shows the new tag alone, the index holds two keys, and the first key keeps the line, the tag and the
   note.

*The moved month.*
1. Two months have budgets; the earlier one lacks a line the later one has. A purchase dated in the later
   month is on that line. An unrelated change is recorded (a note on another transaction).
2. The collector writes the next snapshot with the purchase dated in the earlier month.
3. Before any run of the ingest over that snapshot, the person sets a note on the purchase
   (`transactions.setNote`).
4. The ingest runs, any number of times.
5. The person undoes the unrelated change (`changes.undo`).
6. Expected: the undo is accepted. Actual: it is refused with `stale_change`, and stays refused until a
   budget is saved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each sequence above exists as a test that drives the writes through the router with the take-in
wired to the real ingest, was seen failing on the code as it stands, and passes: in the first the posted
row has the pending row's key and shows the line, both tags and the note; in the second the unrelated
undo is accepted and the purchase has no line.
- [ ] In both, the journal holds one change of the method `ingest.run` by `rule` for the new snapshot,
recorded before the person's change, and undoing the person's change is accepted and takes back only what
that write did.
- [ ] After the ingest took a snapshot in, a write that looks up a transaction the index knows leaves that
transaction's index row byte for byte as the ingest left it.
- [ ] A write over a snapshot already taken in calls the take-in zero times, shown by a counting function
in its place.
- [ ] A write that names no transaction (`settings.setThreshold`) calls the take-in zero times and is
answered as today when the snapshot is missing.
- [ ] With a take-in that does nothing, and with one that fails, a write that looks a transaction up over
a snapshot not taken in is answered `internal`, the handler having run at most twice, and the journal and
the index are as they were before the request.
- [ ] With no take-in configured, the same write is answered `internal` and records nothing.
- [ ] A lookup over a snapshot that records no projected run is answered `ledger_unavailable` and records
nothing.
- [ ] The same holds for a bulk write (`transactions.addTagToMany` over a selection that includes the
posted row of the first sequence) and for the journal method `transactions.applyLineToEstablishment`: each
ends with the posted row under the pending row's key.
- [ ] A test fails for a call of `IndexTransaction` in any source file of the API's package other than
inside `indexListed`, in `internal/api/transaction_target.go`.
- [ ] The take-in's run is logged with a trigger name of its own, `write`, and counts only; the tests of
`cmd/finwise/ingest_test.go` that restrict the log's content pass with that name added.
- [ ] One test in `cmd/finwise/serve_ingest_test.go` starts the real server with a timer interval long
enough never to fire,
replaces the snapshot while it runs, posts a write on the posted row, and finds the answer 200 and the
posted row under the pending row's key.
- [ ] Each rule was seen failing once, by breaking it on purpose, and the pull request names the test that
failed for each: the comparison of runs removed; the retry removed; the take-in called inside the write's
change; the write going on when the second comparison fails; the comparison made before the change is
opened instead of inside it.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/` changes: `git diff --stat` over that directory is
empty.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` says, in the paragraph on the ingest, that it also runs before a write that looks a
transaction up over a snapshot not yet taken in, and, in the paragraph on handlers, that a lookup refuses
to index from such a snapshot.
- [ ] How long a write waits for a take-in over a real ledger is measured by the review, not by the
implementer, three times, and written in the pull request as a duration and nothing else of that ledger.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`.
- [ ] Done when: both sequences pass as tests through the router and one through the real server, a write
whose snapshot cannot be taken in records nothing, and no golden file moved.

## Tests
- Integration, in `internal/api`: the two sequences through the router with the real ingest as the
take-in, over two successive invented snapshots; the bulk write and the journal method; the failing, the
idle and the absent take-in; the snapshot with no projected run.
- Unit, in `internal/api`: the comparison at the door (equal runs, a newer snapshot, an older snapshot, no
run taken in yet); the counting take-in for a snapshot already taken in and for a write that names no
transaction.
- Unit, source-level, in `internal/api`: no call of `IndexTransaction` outside `indexListed`.
- Unit, in `internal/ingest`: the new trigger stops at a run already taken in.
- End to end, in `cmd/finwise`: the real server, a snapshot replaced while it runs, one write, the
database read afterwards; the log's shape with the new trigger.
- Golden: none moves; the conformance suite passes with its environments declaring the fixture's run as
taken in.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/transaction_target.go`, `internal/api/writes.go`, `internal/api/router.go`,
`internal/api/errors.go`, `internal/ingest/run.go`, `cmd/finwise/ingest.go`, `cmd/finwise/serve.go`,
`internal/authored/authoredtest/`, `internal/api/transaction_target_test.go`,
`internal/api/helpers_test.go`, `internal/api/write_runner_test.go`, `cmd/finwise/ingest_test.go`,
`cmd/finwise/serve_ingest_test.go`, `AGENTS.md`, and, only if `indexListed` has to be handed the request's
views to make the comparison, the files that call it: `internal/api/transaction_tag_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_count_writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_reimbursement_writes.go`, `internal/api/review_accept.go`,
`internal/api/subscriptions_writes.go`
**Reads only:** `internal/ingest/pairing.go`, `internal/ingest/harness_test.go`,
`internal/authored/meta.go`, `internal/authored/transaction_index.go`,
`internal/authored/line_references.go`, `internal/ledger/sync.go`, `internal/ledger/view.go`,
`internal/ledger/ledgertest/`, `internal/api/after_budget_save_test.go`, `internal/api/views_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/`, `bin/ci`, `internal/api/` (every source file, read by the test that
looks for a call of `IndexTransaction`), `cmd/finwise/` (where the test over the real server is added)

Seven code files in three packages (the router and its lookup, the ingest's triggers, the server's
wiring), a helper in the store's test package, new test files beside them and two sentences of the
briefing: `size:L` by the number of packages, although the change at each place is small. It stops at the
door of the index: the pairing, the clearing, the undo engine and its check, the contract, the interface
and the stand-in backend are not edited. It is not split, because the comparison without the take-in
turns both defects into refused writes and the take-in without the comparison fixes neither.

## Recovery path
No stored row changes shape and nothing is migrated. Reverting the pull request brings back the two
defects and nothing else. A database touched while the change was in place needs nothing: what the ingest
took in before a write is what it would have taken in on its next run.
close_reason: A write that looks a transaction up refuses to index from a snapshot whose projected run is not the run the ingest took in last: the write keeps nothing, the server runs the ingest with a trigger of its own (logged as write), and the write is tried once more over fresh views; a take-in that fails, is not configured or leaves the snapshot still not taken in ends the write as internal with nothing recorded. For a key the index already gives, the lookup writes nothing. Verified by the gate on the branch after main was merged in; by both reproductions as tests through the router with the real ingest, seen failing on the earlier code; by the same for a bulk write and for the journal method; by one test over the real server with the snapshot replaced while it runs; by the author's thirteen deliberate breaks and four more in review, each killed by a named test; and by the opt-in tests over a real ledger, where a take-in adds well under a second. No golden file moved. One criterion is met differently: a write over a snapshot that records no projected run answers not_found, since such a snapshot lists no transaction, while the door itself answers ledger_unavailable.

title: Work out the budget's figures on the server in integer cents, for the month's budget and for a draft, and weigh a scenario against the month by line id
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, over their real bank data, the budget screen shows five empty groups and nothing else: whatever
budget the person keeps, no line says how much was spent on it, the income is zero and the investment
rate is a dash; pressing "Editar budget" and changing any amount ends the edit at once with the message
that the app is read-only, and the scenarios screen sends the person back to the budget the moment it
opens. After this lands the budget screen shows, for the month on screen, what was received on each
income line, what was spent on each fixed and variable line and what is left of it, which variable line
went over its cap, the balance of the savings pot a provision or a reserve is linked to, the fees the
banks charged, what is left to invest and its share of the income. While editing, every change is
weighed at once, with a renamed line keeping what was spent on it and a new line starting at nothing;
the scenarios screen says how much a scenario would invest and which of its amounts differ from the
month's budget; and opening a line lists the places that make it up, biggest first. If this were wrong
the person would see a total that does not add up to the purchases behind it, a line that loses its
spending when renamed, a pot balance shown under a line that is not linked to that pot, or a scenario
that marks an untouched amount as changed.

## Outcome
The pure package `internal/budgetrules` gains `View` and `ScenarioImpact`, which compute every figure of
`BudgetView` and `ScenarioImpact` in integer cents from plain values: the groups of a budget with each
line's id, name, amount and flag; what each line id received or spent in the month, from the
dispositions; the balance of the pot each line is linked to; whether the month is closed; and the
investment "made". `budget.view(month)` answers the budget in force for the month from the app's
database, `budget.view(month, draft)` answers the same figures for a draft, with its arguments validated
against the manifest before the handler runs, `budget.evaluateScenario(month, draft)` has a handler, and
`budget.establishments(month, line)` groups the month's contributions to a line by establishment. On a
server without the app's database `budget.view` without a draft and `budget.establishments` answer exactly
what they answer today, and no golden file under `full/` or `empty/` changes.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite snapshot that a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, through `internal/ledger`.
*The app's database* is `finwise.db`, owned by the Go package `internal/authored`, where everything the
person authors is kept (a budget, a transaction's line, a link between a budget line and a pot); the
server has one only when started with `--db`. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under
`web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it and its tests are the only existing statement
of how the budget's figures behave, and its behaviour is the rule wherever this text does not say
otherwise. *The contract* is the TypeScript interface `FinwiseApi` under `web/src/api/contract/`; *the
manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it, versioned and never edited by hand,
which gives Go each method's route, class (`read`, `evaluate`, `write`, `session`) and the schemas of its
arguments and result. *A budget* is a list of versions, each valid from a month on; the budget in force
for a month is the latest version at or before it, and a month before the first version uses the first.
It has five groups a person edits, by key: income (`rec`), fixed (`fix`), variable (`var`), provisions
(`prov`, money set aside every month for a bill that comes once in a while) and reserves (`res`, money set
aside for something wanted). *A line* has an integer id minted once in the app's database, a name that
belongs to the budget version, an amount in cents and an optional flag such as "Não garantida". *The fees
line* is the built-in line "Tarifas e juros": it belongs to no group and no document and has a fixed id.
*A draft* is a budget document the person is still editing; it is sent to be weighed and never stored by
this work. *A pot* is what the pots screens list: a reserve entry of a bank account (id
`reserve:<account>/<reserveId>`), an investment (id `investment:<id>`) or, when the bank does not keep an
entry's identity stable, a slot (id `slot:<account>/<n>`). *A month* is `YYYY-MM` and *a day*
`YYYY-MM-DD`, both in Brazil time (`internal/brday`); "the current month" is the Brazil month of the
instant in the request's context, never the host's clock. *A golden file* is the committed, exact answer
of one call over an invented fixture. *The gate* is `bin/ci`, the exact checks CI runs.

**What earlier work provides.** None of the following is in the repository when this text is written;

- The transactions' tables, the dispositions and the merged reads ({{T1}}): the migration
  `0003_transactions` with `tx_index`, `tx_ids` and `tx_state` (a transaction's line, split parts,
  exclusion, refund and its line, reimbursement and its linked credit, pending review), and
  `budgetrules.Dispose`, the function that says what a transaction counts for. It takes one listed
  transaction with its authored state merged in (joined in Go by the transaction's key, inside one request
  that sees one snapshot of each store) and answers its disposition and the amounts it adds to which line
  ids. Amounts are magnitudes in integer cents; the first condition that matches wins:

  | # | disposition | condition | adds |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | unconverted | the ledger has no value in reais for it | nothing |
  | 2 | movement | a movement between own accounts or a bill payment | nothing |
  | 3 | excluded | excluded with a reason | nothing |
  | 4 | waiting | pending review | nothing |
  | 5 | split | a debit with two or more parts | each part with a line adds its amount to that line; the rest is unassigned |
  | 6 | fee | a fee row, charge or discount, on no line (posted, as the existing fees rule says) or put on the fees line by the person | a charge adds to the fees line; the credit that discounts it takes off |
  | 7 | reimbursement | a credit linked to a purchase | no line; the smaller of its amount and the purchase's is applied inside the purchase |
  | 8 | refund | a credit that is a refund | takes its amount off its refund line; with no refund line, nothing |
  | 9 | income | a credit on a line of the income group | adds its amount to that line (received) |
  | 10 | other credit | any other credit | nothing |
  | 11 | on a line | a debit with a line | adds its amount less the applied reimbursement |
  | 12 | uncategorised | a debit with no line | nothing |

  A row the bank still reports as pending is listed and counts like any other; only the fee rule keeps
  counting posted fee rows alone. The package already exists when this starts, created by that work.
- The pots' links ({{S2}}): the migration `0005_pots` with `pot_lines(line_id, pot_id)`, a line linked to
  at most one pot, and the authored view's read of it; the write that toggles a link (refused for a
  `slot:` pot, whose id changes between days, and `not_found` for a pot the ledger does not have).

**The decisions this work carries, with what lost.**

- Spending is looked up by line id, never by name: a draft's renamed line keeps its spending and a line
  the draft has just added (no id) has none. Lost: the stand-in's join by name, under which renaming a
  line silently drops its history from every total.
- Spending and income received are summed from the ledger for the month asked, by Brazil day, through the
  dispositions. Lost: the stand-in's seeded baseline, which has no rule behind it and no rule at all for
  income received.
- A provision or reserve line's pot is the pot the line is linked to in `pot_lines`, never a pot of the
  same name. Lost: the join by name, under which renaming a line or a pot silently moves a balance.
- `ScenarioImpact` compares each scenario line with the line of the same id in the budget of the month
  asked, instead of by position; a line without an id is changed. Lost: comparing by position, which marks
  every line after an inserted one as changed and compares a moved line with its neighbour.
- Every percentage the server computes is a whole number rounded half up, as the existing reads already
  answer `fill` and `progress`. Lost: the stand-in's fractions (a bar of 77.0 for 308 of 400 happens to be
  whole; 290 of 900 would be 32.22).
- A draft being edited is not validated beyond its shape: an empty or repeated name, a name equal to the
  fees line's and an id that names no line are all weighed as typed. Only the save validates ({{B2}}).
- Pot targets (Rainy Funds) get no control in this plan of work, a decision of the person: the Rainy Funds
  group is answered empty.
- The investment's "made" follows the month's "Investimento" transfer of the payday review, which does
  not exist yet ({{V5}}: the payday transfers derived from the budget and marked by month). Until then it
  is answered as not made.
- The next charge of a provision has no source yet: it is answered as the contract's "no date".

**The figures.** Every amount is integer cents (`money.Cents`) from the budget's `cents` column and the
dispositions to the wire, where `api.Reais` writes it. The only divisions are the two percentages, rule
(P). `View` is a pure function of plain values: it opens nothing, knows no HTTP and reads no clock, as
`internal/txrules`, `internal/cardrules` and `internal/potrules` do today. Its inputs, for a month M:

- `G`: the groups of the budget in force for M (or of the draft), each line with its id (absent for a
  draft's new line), its name, its amount `a ≥ 0` and its flag;
- `F(id)`: for every line id, the sum of what `Dispose` adds to that id over the transactions the API
  lists whose Brazil day is in M, signed as the table says (a refund takes off, an income credit adds to
  its income line). The transactions of M are read as `feesOfMonth` reads them today, widened by the tax
  pairing window and cut back to M, so a purchase is placed exactly as the list shows it. `F` of an id
  nothing touched, and of a line without id, is 0;
- `P(id)`: for a line id linked in `pot_lines`, the pot's balance now, as `loadPots` builds it (`potEntry.
  balance`; the pots are needed for the balance alone, so they are loaded without the yield, as `home.go`
  does), counted only while the ledger lists that pot now and the pot is open; otherwise absent. The
  balance is today's whatever month is asked, as in the stand-in. The same rule, "a link counts only while
  its pot is listed and open", is the one the payday transfers will use ({{V5}}), so it is one function;
- `closed`: whether M has a row in `closed_months`;
- `made`: the amount the investment line shows as made. This work always supplies 0; it is an input so
  that the payday work ({{V5}}) can feed it (the residual once the month's "Investimento" transfer is
  marked, or when the month is closed) without changing `View`.

Numbered, each in cents:

1. `T(k) = Σ a(l)` over the lines of group k, for each of the five keys. A group a draft leaves out has
   no lines and `T = 0`.
2. `income = T(rec)`.
3. `outgoing = T(fix) + T(var) + T(prov) + T(res)`.
4. `investment = income − outgoing`. It can be negative.
5. `allocated = outgoing + investment`, as the stand-in computes it (it equals `income` by construction,
   and a test says so).
6. `rate = null` when `income = 0`; otherwise `round½↑(investment × 100 / income)`, by rule (P). This is
   also `investmentRate` and the third cell of the investment line. The residual (4) and the rate (6) are
   functions of their own that `View` calls, because the payday review and the net worth's investment rate
   ({{V5}}) take them "exactly as the budget view answers them".
7. Rule (P), whole percent rounded half up: for `x = n × 100 / d` with `d > 0`, `round½↑(x) = ⌊(200·n + d)
   / (2·d)⌋`, with a floor division, not Go's `/`, which truncates toward zero and gives the wrong answer
   for a negative `n`. Half goes toward positive infinity, as JavaScript's `Math.round`: 12.5 → 13, −12.5
   → −12, −184.67 → −185. One function, in `internal/budgetrules`, serves every percentage of this work
   and of the work after it (the weekly fill, the contribution's progress).
8. `share(part, whole) = 0` when `whole = 0`; otherwise `round½↑(part × 100 / whole)` held between 0 and
   100. The upper bound is the stand-in's `Math.min(100, …)`; the lower bound is the contract's ("`bar` is
   the share of the amount reached, 0 to 100"), which a negative `part` (refunds larger than the purchases
   on a line) would otherwise break; the stand-in has no lower bound and answers a negative bar there.
9. An income line l: cells `[money a(l), money F(l), none]`; marks `[{text: flag, tone: "neutral"}]` when
   it has a flag, else `[]`; `over` false; `bar` null; `expandable` true.
10. A fixed or variable line l: `done = F(l)`, `left = a(l) − done`, `over = left < 0` (strictly above
    the amount). Cells `[money a(l), money done, difference left]`; `expandable` true. A fixed line: marks
    `[]`, `bar` null. A variable line: marks `[{text: "Estourou", tone: "bad"}]` when `over`, else `[]`;
    `bar = share(done, a(l))`.
11. `potCell(l) = money P(l)` when `P(l)` is present, else `none` (the stand-in answers money 0 for a line
    with no pot of its name; here a line with no counted link has no balance to show).
12. A provision line l: cells `[money a(l), potCell(l), next-charge null]`, the contract's
    `{"type":"next-charge","charge":null}`; marks `[]`, `over` false, `bar` null, `expandable` false.
13. A reserve line l: cells `[money a(l), potCell(l), money F(l)]`; marks `[]`, `over` false, `bar` null,
    `expandable` true.
14. An editable group k: `subtotal = T(k)`; `subtotalSpent = Σ F(l)` over its lines for `fix` and `var`
    (0.00 when it has no line), `null` for the other three; `over = (k = var) ∧ subtotalSpent > T(var)`,
    strictly; its lines in the version's (or the draft's) order within the group.
15. Rainy Funds: `{key: "rf", name: "Rainy Funds", subtotal: 0.00, subtotalSpent: null, over: false,
    lines: []}`.
16. Fees: `fees = F(fees line)`. Group `{key: "tar", name: "Tarifas e juros", subtotal: fees,
    subtotalSpent: null, over: false}` with one line "Tarifas e juros", cells `[money fees, none, none]`,
    marks `[]`, `over` false, `bar` null, `expandable` true. The fees line counts by rule in every month,
    with or without a budget. With nothing authored this equals today's `spentOnFees` for the month.
17. Investment: group `{key: "inv", name: "Investimento", subtotal: investment, subtotalSpent: null, over:
    investment < 0}` with one line "Investimento", cells `[money investment, money made, percent rate]`,
    `over = investment < 0`, marks `[{text: "Budget maior que a receita", tone: "bad"}]` when over, else
    `[]`, `bar` null, `expandable` false.
18. The view: `{month: M, closed, income, allocated, investmentRate: rate, groups}`, the groups in the
    order `rec`, `fix`, `var`, `prov`, `res`, `rf`, `tar`, `inv`, the five editable ones always present,
    with the fixed names the server owns, whatever names or order a draft sends.

Both new texts, "Estourou" and "Budget maior que a receita", are the stand-in's and go to `messages.go`.

**The scenario's impact** (`budgetrules.ScenarioImpact`), for a month M and a draft S:

19. `current = {investment: investment(C), rate: rate(C)}` by (4) and (6), where C is the budget in force
    for M. A month with no version has no lines: `{0.00, null}`.
20. `scenario = {investment: investment(S), rate: rate(S)}`.
21. `difference = investment(S) − investment(C)`.
22. `changed[g][i]`, for every group g of S in the order it was sent and every line i of it in the order
    sent (the screen draws it by those positions): `true` when the line has no id, or C has no line with
    that id, or that line's amount in C is not `a(S, g, i)`; `false` otherwise. Only the amount is
    compared: a renamed or moved line with the same id and amount is not changed.

An evaluation reads nothing from the ledger, so it answers when the snapshot is missing.

**The establishments of a line** (`budget.establishments(month, name)`):

23. The name is resolved in the budget in force for the month: "Tarifas e juros" is the fees line in any
    month, as the view shows it in any month; any other name is the line that version gives that name. A
    name the month's budget does not have answers `[]`.
24. A transaction listed in the month is in the list when `Dispose` reports at least one addition to that
    line id, even of zero; it adds the sum of its additions to that id (two parts of one split on the
    line add together) and counts once.
25. Grouped by establishment key (`txrules.Transaction.EstablishmentKey`, `doc:`, `name:` or `text:`; a
    person has one too): `amount = Σ` of its transactions' sums, signed (a refund takes off), `count` the
    number of its transactions, `name` the name to show for the key. Order: `amount` descending, then
    `key` ascending.
26. Invariant: the amounts of a line's establishments add up to `F(line)`, the figure the view shows for
    that line in the same month, and the counts to the number of transactions that add to it.

The name to show is the nickname when the person gave the key one, else the name the list shows for the
newest of those transactions. One function answers the name to show for an establishment key, delivered
with the nicknames ({{T3}}: tags, notes, nicknames, default lines). If it exists when this work starts,
call it; if not, answer the ledger's name and leave a call site that work can bring under its function.

**`budget.view` with a draft, and its arguments.** The router validates `budget.view`'s arguments against
its argument schema in the manifest before the handler runs, as it does for every write and evaluation
with a handler, and only for this read: every other read keeps its own decoding. So over HTTP the drafts
`0` and `"x"`, a group key outside the five, a line with a field the contract does not have and a line
without `amount` are 400 `bad_request` with the handler not called; `null` and an empty array `[]` (a
document with no groups) pass. The handler then parses what a schema cannot say: the month
(`bad_request` for `2026-13`), each amount through `Reais` (`bad_request` for a negative amount, one beyond
one billion reais, or `1e400`). Then it builds the view of the draft with (1) to (18), reading from the app's
database only the closed month and the links, and from the ledger the month's transactions and the pots.
It stores nothing: a read runs in a read-only transaction.

On a server without the app's database `budget.view` is still a read, so a draft is weighed against an
empty authored view (no line has spending, no link exists) and answered; `budget.evaluateScenario` is of
class `evaluate` and keeps answering `read_only` there, before its body is read. Over the interface this
means: on a server without `--db` the edit mode of the budget no longer ends at the first change, and
saving keeps answering `read_only`, which keeps the edit as today; the scenarios screen keeps returning to
the budget.

**What the stand-in does that is not ported** (each pinned by a test named in the report of the work):
the seeded spending baseline and its freeze outside the current month; the join by name of spending, pots
and the scenario's comparison; the pot's next charge; the Rainy Funds built from pots named "RF ..."
with a target; the investment counted as made in a closed month (it arrives with the transfers); the
fractional bars; `cleanDraft`'s zero for an amount that is not a number, which has no wire form (JSON has
no `NaN`, and a `null` amount is refused by the schema); the establishments' order on a tie, which the
stand-in leaves to insertion.

**The cost of an evaluation.** The interface asks for a draft's figures after every change, with no
debounce, so one evaluation is one ledger read of the month widened by the pairing window, one load of the
pots without yield and a few authored reads. Its time on a real ledger is measured by the review, not by
this work, and recorded on the pull request beside the time of `budget.evaluateScenario`; whether a
debounce is then needed in the interface is the review's decision, and this work adds none. Reading the
whole ledger on every call is accepted for now and is deferred work that will read this measurement.

**Failure paths that touch this work.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing | `budget.view` (with or without a draft) and `budget.establishments` answer 503 `ledger_unavailable`; `budget.evaluateScenario` answers, as it reads no ledger |
| the snapshot is swapped during a request | the request finishes on the snapshot its ledger view opened |
| a save commits while a view is being computed | the view's authored read is wholly before or wholly after it |
| a line is renamed, reordered or moved between groups | its id holds, and so do its spending and its pot |
| a line is linked to a pot the ledger no longer lists, or to a closed pot | its balance cell is `none` |
| a draft sends a negative amount | 400 `bad_request`; the interface shows the failed evaluation as a failed read, and every further change of that draft fails the same way until the amount is fixed |
| a server without the app's database | `budget.view` and `budget.establishments` answer as today; a draft is weighed against nothing authored; `budget.evaluateScenario` answers `read_only` |

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. A real
snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from it (amount, description, name, document, id) is ever
printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the
person running the test and goes into no file; a test that touches a real ledger runs only when
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. Fixtures are invented. The review's timing of an evaluation on a
real ledger records durations only, never a figure the evaluation answered. A line's name and an
establishment's name are the person's own words: new files of `internal/api` log nothing, and the request
log keeps to verb, route, status, duration and error kind.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional
Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit message. Money is
integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; the test that forbids floats covers
`internal/api` and the rule packages. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant
of `internal/authored`, the only package that executes SQL against `finwise.db`; this work should need no
new one beyond what {{B2}} and {{S2}} added, and any it adds is registered and prepared by the existing
test. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English. A design value in a component
comes from a token; this work changes no component. A read handler's conformance case is in
`authoredReadCases` when it needs authored data, never in `readCases` in the shape the interface's
equality test scans for: that test compares a case with the stand-in over an empty ledger, and the
stand-in answers money 0 where the server answers `none` for a line with no pot. A golden file changes only
with `go test ./internal/api -run TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile -update`, which refuses to run while
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set, and every changed golden file is read before it is committed.

title: Show a line an agent proposes for a pending transaction as the weekly queue's suggestion
description:
## What changes for the user
Every week the person goes through the queue of transactions the app could not place on a budget line
by itself: a new shop, a PIX to someone, a purchase the rules were not sure of. For each one the app
shows its own suggestion, if it has any, and the person accepts it or picks another line. An agent
reading the same queue often knows better (it read the receipt in the person's mail, or it knows that
this PIX is the rent), but today all it can do is say so in the terminal. After this lands the agent
proposes a line for a transaction that waits in the queue, and the queue itself shows that line as the
suggestion, with the agent's reason under it, where the person was going to look anyway. The person
answers exactly as today: "Aceitar" puts the transaction on that line as their own decision, "Escolher
outra linha" puts it elsewhere, and the agent reads which one happened. If it were wrong, the person
would see a suggestion in the queue that is not the one the panel of the same transaction shows, or a
transaction put on a line they never accepted.

## Outcome
A proposal of `transactions.setLine` for a transaction waiting for review is stored as the queue's
suggestion for it, not as a card proposal. Wherever the app shows or accepts that transaction's
suggestion (the weekly queue, the transaction list, the transaction panel, `transactions.confirmLine`),
it is the proposed line, with no confidence and the agent's reason as the justification. Settling the
review closes the proposal in the same transaction: approved when the person put it on the proposed
line, refused when they chose another, stale when the rules or something else settled it.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *A transaction waiting for review* is
one the app's database keeps a review for and the ledger lists, in a month whose budget has a line:
`pendingTransactions` in `internal/api/pending.go` is the one definition, and the weekly queue
(`readQueue` in `internal/api/review_queue.go`) lists exactly those. Its review is kept in `tx_state`
(`internal/authored/migrations/0003_transactions.sql`): `pending_reason`, `pending_line_id` (the rule's
suggestion, a line id that survives a rename) and `pending_confidence`. The contract's `PendingReview`
(`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`) carries `reason`, `suggestion` (a line name), `confidence` and
`justification` (null until something explains a suggestion); `pendingOf` in
`internal/api/transactions_authored.go` builds it for the list and the queue, and `justificationOf` in
`internal/api/transaction_detail.go` answers the panel's `justification`. The queue's card
(`web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`) already shows `Sugestão da IA: <line>` and, under it, the
justification when there is one. *Accepting* is `review.acceptPending` (`internal/api/review_accept.go`),
the person's own change, which settles the review through `(*Recorder).SettleLine`
(`internal/authored/transaction_lines.go`), the function every write that puts a transaction on a line
calls, the ingest's rules included. *A proposal*, *the token*, `review.submitProposal`, the `proposals`
table, `review.proposals` and the closed union `ProposedChange` are the previous item's: an agent with the
token submits a change of a closed list with a reason and its name; the server checks it by running the
method's handler in a change it rolls back, and stores it, outside the journal, until the person answers.

**What the person decided, and what lost.** A line proposed for a transaction still pending shows in the
weekly queue itself, as the suggested line with the agent's reason, and the person accepts it or picks
another; accepting stays the person's own change, as accepting the rule's suggestion is today. Lost:
putting it on the approvals card, where forty line proposals become forty loose sentences away from their
transactions.

**What the code forces, decided here, with what lost.**
- *`transactions.setLine(id, line)` joins the union.* Submitted for a transaction waiting for review, it
  is checked as every proposal is (an unknown line is answered `unknown_line`, an unknown transaction
  null), titled `Pôr N em L` (the previous item's notation: `N` the transaction's shown name and
  amount, `L` the line), and stored with a row in a new table. Submitted for a transaction that does not
  wait for review, it is answered `read_only` and stores nothing, until the item of the difference view
  makes it a card proposal. Lost: storing it on the card now (that item is where its view of before and
  after is built).
- *Storage.* Migration `0010_queue_proposals.sql` creates `queue_proposals (proposal_id INTEGER PRIMARY
  KEY REFERENCES proposals (id), tx_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tx_index (tx_key), line_id INTEGER
  NOT NULL REFERENCES lines (id))`, with an index on `tx_key`. The line is kept by id, resolved when the
  proposal is checked, so a rename of the line does not lose it, as `pending_line_id` does not. The table
  is named in `notJournaledTables` for the reason the `proposals` table is. `review.weekly`'s approvals
  leave out every proposal that has a row here.
- *One suggestion per transaction.* A new queue proposal for a transaction that already has one waiting
  closes the earlier as stale, with `staleReason` null, in the transaction that stores the new one. Lost:
  refusing the second (the agent could not correct itself before the person answers).
- *One function says what a review suggests,* and every place that shows or accepts it calls it: the
  waiting queue proposal's line when there is one and the transaction's month names it, with
  `confidence` null and `justification` the proposal's reason; otherwise the rule's suggestion, as today.
  `pendingOf` and `justificationOf` show it; `confirmLine` (`internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`)
  accepts it for a transaction waiting for review; `answeredStep` in `internal/api/review_accept.go`
  compares the answer with it, so accepting the agent's line writes `Você aceitou <line>`. Lost: the queue
  alone (the panel of the same transaction would show and confirm another line than the queue).
- *Settling closes it, in the store.* `SettleLine` closes the waiting queue proposal of its key, in the
  transaction of the change that settles it: approved, with that change's id, when the line is the
  proposal's, whoever the author; refused, with no text, when the author is `person` and the line is
  another; stale, with `staleReason` null, when the author is `rule` or `model` and the line is another.
  The author `rule` reaches a waiting transaction through "all purchases here"
  (`transactions.applyLineToEstablishment`, whose moves are settled by `rule`, line 302 of
  `internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`); the ingest applies its rules once to a new transaction and
  never settles one already waiting. `LinkReimbursement`
  (`internal/authored/transaction_reimbursement.go`), which settles the review of the credit it links,
  closes the credit's as stale. So the outcome is right however the review was settled: the queue, the
  panel, a bulk line change, "all purchases here" or the ingest. Undoing that change brings the review
  back and leaves the proposal closed, since proposals are not journaled; the queue then shows the rule's
  suggestion again. Lost: closing it only from `review.acceptPending` (a review settled from the panel
  would leave a proposal waiting for a transaction that no longer waits).
- *Nothing of the interface changes.* The queue's card already shows a suggestion with a justification,
  and the contract's `PendingReview` keeps its fields.

**Decided by the person on 2026-11-23.** The queue keeps its label, `Sugestão da IA: <line>`, for an
agent's line as for the rule's, with the agent's reason under it. Lost: `Sugestão de <name>`, which would
add a field to the contract's `PendingReview` and change the queue's text. A stale queue proposal is not
answered with a refusal, since nothing is approved in the queue: it closes as stale with `staleReason`
null, and the refusal reason `proposal_stale` added by the item before is not involved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The manifest's union of `review.submitProposal` gains `transactions.setLine`, and
  `npm --prefix web run contract:check` passes.
- [ ] Submitting `transactions.setLine` for a transaction waiting for review stores a waiting proposal
  with a row in `queue_proposals`, records no change and leaves every journaled table as it was; it does
  not appear in `review.weekly`'s approvals.
- [ ] The queue item, the transaction in `transactions.list` and `transactions.detail` of that
  transaction show the proposed line as `suggestion`, `confidence` null and the proposal's reason as
  `justification`; with no queue proposal they answer as today, and no existing golden file moves.
- [ ] Submitting it with a line the transaction's month lacks is answered `unknown_line` and stores
  nothing; for a transaction that does not wait for review it is answered 403 `read_only` and stores
  nothing.
- [ ] A second proposal for the same transaction closes the first as stale and is the one the queue
  shows.
- [ ] `review.acceptPending` with the proposed line records the person's change (author `person`, method
  `review.acceptPending`), writes the step `Você aceitou <line>`, and closes the proposal as approved with
  that change's id; with another line it closes it as refused with no text.
- [ ] `transactions.confirmLine` on that transaction puts it on the proposed line and closes the proposal
  as approved; `transactions.setLine` from the panel to another line closes it as refused.
- [ ] "All purchases here" applied from another purchase of the same establishment closes the proposal
  as approved when it moves the transaction to the proposed line and as stale when it moves it to
  another; linking that credit as a reimbursement closes it as stale.
- [ ] Undoing the accept brings the review back with the rule's suggestion and leaves the proposal
  approved.
- [ ] `queue_proposals` is in `notJournaledTables`, `TestEveryTableOfTheSchemaIsJournaledOrDeliberatelyNot`
  passes, and the list of tables in `cmd/finwise/database_test.go` names it.
- [ ] Each rule was seen failing once by breaking it on purpose, and the pull request names the test that
  failed for each: the panel showing the rule's suggestion while the queue shows the agent's; settling
  from the panel leaving the proposal waiting; the earlier proposal left waiting beside the new one.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` says, in the paragraph on the proposals, that a line proposed for a transaction waiting
  for review is the queue's suggestion and how settling it closes it.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`.
- [ ] Done when: a line an agent proposes for a pending transaction is what the queue suggests, with the
  agent's reason, and the person's answer in the queue is the agent's outcome.

## Tests
- Unit, in `internal/authored`: the migration; `SettleLine` by `person` on the proposed line, by `person`
  on another, by `rule` on the proposed line and on another; `LinkReimbursement` on the credit; an undo
  leaving the proposal closed; one waiting suggestion per transaction.
- Integration, in `internal/api`, through the router: submission for a waiting transaction, an unknown
  line and a transaction that does not wait; the queue, the list and the panel; accept with the line and
  with another; `confirmLine`; the panel's `setLine`; "all purchases here" from a sibling purchase.
- Golden: new cases over the invented authored state with a queue proposal for `review.weekly` and for
  `transactions.detail` of the pending transaction; a write case for the submission and one for the accept
  after it. No existing file moves.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/authored/migrations/0010_queue_proposals.sql`, `internal/authored/proposals.go`,
`internal/authored/proposals_test.go`, `internal/authored/transaction_lines.go`,
`internal/authored/transaction_reimbursement.go`, `internal/authored/statements.go`,
`internal/authored/registry.go`, `internal/authored/journal_guard_test.go`,
`internal/api/review_approvals.go`, `internal/api/proposal_titles.go`, `internal/api/messages.go`,
`internal/api/transactions_authored.go`, `internal/api/transaction_detail.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`, `internal/api/review_accept.go`,
`internal/api/review_approvals_test.go`, `internal/api/authored_conformance_test.go`,
`internal/api/write_conformance_test.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/proposed-change.test.ts`, `cmd/finwise/database_test.go`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/pending.go`, `internal/api/review_queue.go`, `internal/ingest/evaluation.go`,
`internal/authored/transaction_ingest.go`, `internal/authored/migrations/0003_transactions.sql`,
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`, `bin/ci`

A migration and two store functions in `internal/authored`, the one function of the suggestion and its
four callers in `internal/api`, one member of the contract's union: `size:L` by the schema change. The
interface, the stand-in and the parity states are not touched.

## Recovery path
The migration only adds a table; the runner copies the database to `<name>.before-<UTC timestamp>`
before applying it. Reverting the merge commit on a database that recorded `0010_queue_proposals` stops
the start (a recorded migration the binary does not carry): restore that copy, or keep the binary that
carries it. Accepts made meanwhile are the person's own changes and stay undoable.

title: Bring the app's database up to date with a snapshot in one function: refresh the index, carry a pending charge's work to its posted row, and classify each new transaction by rule once
description:
## What changes for the user
Today nothing the banks send at night reaches the person's month: a new purchase sits uncategorised until
they find it in the list, the weekly queue never asks about anything real, and a purchase they put on a
line while the bank still showed it as pending would lose that line the moment the bank posts it, because
the bank gives the posted charge a new identity. This work is the step that takes a night's records in.
Every new transaction from the month the person began using the app goes on its line by rule when the
person has already shown where that shop belongs, and is put in the queue otherwise; a charge the bank
posts under a new identity keeps everything the person did to it while it was pending; a rule's choice the
person takes back stays taken back; a change of the confidence threshold acts only on purchases that
arrive after it; older history is never pushed into the queue. Nothing runs it yet on its own (starting
the server, a timer, a save of the budget and a command will call it, in separate work), so on its own the
person sees nothing. What they would notice if it were wrong: a category lost when a charge posts, the
same purchase asked about twice, a correction overwritten overnight, a queue flooded with years of old
purchases, or a purchase asked about in a month that has no budget to answer it with.

## Outcome
A new package, `internal/ingest`, holds one function, `ingest.Run`, that brings `finwise.db` up to date with
the ledger's current snapshot in five steps: it reads the collector's projected run and the listed
transactions from one ledger view, refreshes the index, pairs a vanished bank-pending transaction with the
posted one that replaced it, evaluates every new transaction from the tracking start month on whose month
has a budget with at least one line (applying `classrules.Decide` only where neither the person nor a rule
has decided yet), records what it changed as one change by `rule`, and records the run. It is told why it
was called (a timer tick or the start, which stop when the run is the one already taken in, or a budget
change or the command, which go on), returns counts only, and logs nothing. `internal/authored` gains the
registered statements and functions it needs. An opt-in test runs it over a real ledger against a scratch
database and reports counts only.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite file,
`pluggy-snapshot.db`, that a separate program, *the collector* (pluggy-sync), fills from the banks every
night and replaces by an atomic rename; each such file is *a snapshot*, and the app only reads it
(`internal/ledger`). *A listed transaction* is one the API lists: the collector's clean list after the
transaction rules (`internal/txrules`) folded tax rows under their purchases and took the movements of
savings pots out. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, owned by `internal/authored`, the only package
that executes SQL against it. *The index* is `tx_index(tx_key, account_id, day, cents, establishment_key,
bank_pending, first_run, last_run, evaluated)` with `tx_ids(provider_id, tx_key)`: what the app's database
remembers about the transactions it has evaluated or the person has touched. `tx_key` is minted there and
`tx_ids` maps every provider id seen to it. The two tables record observations, not decisions, so they are
not journaled; an undo never removes an index row, and no amount shown or summed ever comes from the
index. *The journal* is the record of every change to authored data: each change has an author (`person`,
`rule` or `model`) and can be undone by the inverse of its effects. *The tracking start month* is the
Brazil month in which `finwise.db` was created, set once at creation from the injected clock and never
again. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype
runs on; it has no ingest and plays no part here.

**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

- The app asks about uncategorised transactions from the month in which `finwise.db` is first created.
  Earlier transactions are never put in the queue; they can still be categorised by hand or reached by
  "all purchases here". Decided by the person, 2026-11-21. What lost: all history in the queue on day one;
  a month chosen by hand.
- The rules run once per transaction, and a change of threshold or minimum of examples acts only on
  transactions evaluated after it. Why: a setting must not silently rewrite the queue or lines already
  applied. What lost: a retroactive pass on every settings change.
- `finwise.db` gives each transaction its own key and maps the provider's ids to it. Why: a pending row is
  replaced by a posted row under a new id; with a key of its own, carrying the person's work across is one
  mapping row instead of rewriting every table. What lost: the provider's id as the key.
- Ledger rows and authored rows are joined in Go, by key, never in SQL. What lost: `ATTACH`; copying the
  ledger into `finwise.db`.
- "Pending" everywhere means pending in `finwise.db`, listed by the ledger now, and in a month whose budget
  has at least one line. So a pending row that vanished is in no queue and no count while it stays
  unlisted, and nothing ever has to be deleted to keep the queue honest.

**What the code is today (each point read in the file named).**

- `internal/ledger/view.go`: `(*Reader).View()` gives one handle and one read-only transaction on the
  snapshot, opened by the first query and kept for every later one, so the queries of one view agree even
  when the collector renames a new file over it meanwhile; `Close` releases it.
- `internal/ledger/testdata/ledger-schema-v1.sql`: the view `pending_posted_candidates` pairs a `PENDING`
  row with a `POSTED` row only while both are present, on the same account, amount, currency, description
  and date, and does not promise one to one; `queryCleanTransactions` (`internal/ledger/queries.go`) hides
  a pending row that has such a pair. So when the bank posts a charge, its pending row leaves the list and
  a posted row with a new id appears.
- `internal/ledger/ledgertest/`: `MarkRemoved` (`rows.go`) turns a current row into one the collector no
  longer sees; `NewAt` builds a fixture at a chosen path, so a test can build the next night's snapshot
  beside the first and rename it over it, as the collector does (`renameOver` in
  `internal/ledger/view_test.go` does exactly that).
- `internal/txrules`: `Interpret(rows, Reference)` lists every row in exactly one place (the list, under a
  purchase as its tax, or the pot movements) and its `Tally` says so; a listed `Transaction` carries `ID`,
  `AccountID`, `Day` (Brazil), `Amount` (signed cents), `Unconverted`, `EstablishmentKey`, `Person`,
  `Movement` (`OwnTransfer`, `BillPayment` or none), `Refund`, `Fee` and `Posted` (false while the bank
  reports it `PENDING`). `internal/api` interprets the whole ledger in one pass for anything that spans
  months (`wholeLedger` in `shell.go`, `transaction_detail.go`) and refuses an answer whose tally does not
  place every row (`checkPlaced` in `transactions_period.go`). The ingest cannot import `internal/api`
  (that package will call it), so it builds the same interpretation itself: the accounts and identities of
  the same view as the reference, the whole clean list, `txrules.Interpret`, and the same tally check.
- `internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`: `TestOnlyTheRequestLogWritesAnything` fails when any file of
  `internal/api` other than `logging.go` and `router.go` imports `log` or `log/slog` or prints. The ingest
  follows the same rule: it returns counts, and only `cmd/finwise` logs them (separate work). An error
  from the ledger reader may carry a row id in its text, so only its kind is ever logged, never its
  message.

**What earlier work provides.** Each is delivered before this bead starts; read its interfaces in the code
as that work left them.

- The app's database (finwise-9h2) and the recorder (finwise-wi4): `internal/authored` opens `finwise.db` with
  immediate write transactions and read-only ones, keeps every statement a registered constant under
  test, offers the tracking start month as a read, and holds `meta(key, value)`, which this work uses for
  the last ingested run through functions of the package, never by key. The recorder holds one immediate
  transaction and one open change with an author, a method, the instant and the Brazil day; the change's
  row is written with its first effect, so a recorder that records nothing leaves no trace.
- The projected run (finwise-j4z): `View.ProjectedRun`, the collector run that produced the snapshot's current
  rows, answered from the same view as the rows; a snapshot without the row answers a typed error; and
  `ledgertest` can add runs and advance the projection.
- The rules (finwise-9gz): `classrules.Decide`, which answers for one never-evaluated transaction leave,
  nothing to store (a fee), apply a line by rule, or pending with "Baixa confiança" (a suggestion and a
  confidence), "PIX para pessoa sem apelido" or "Estabelecimento novo" (neither), filtering the candidate
  examples it is given; and `classrules.Pair`, which matches vanished bank-pending index rows with
  never-seen posted rows on the same account, cents and establishment key, the posted day zero to five days
  after, counting only matches that are one to one on both sides.
- The transactions' store (finwise-jw2): the migration `0003_transactions` with the index, `tx_state(tx_key,
  line_id, classified_by, confidence, pending_reason, pending_line_id, pending_confidence, ask_reason,
  exclusion, …)`, `tx_split_parts`, `establishments(key, nickname, default_line_id)` and
  `history_steps`; the store function that creates or refreshes a transaction's index row; and the
  `authoredtest` builders of those tables. `first_run` and `last_run` stay null until this work fills
  them.
- The classifier settings' store (finwise-11u): the threshold and the minimum of examples, read with their
  defaults.
- The budget (finwise-ef7): budget versions by month and one function of "the lines a month's budget has" (the
  fees line among them whenever the budget has any line), so a rule never applies a line a menu would not
  offer.
- The clearing of line references (finwise-oib): one function of `internal/authored` that takes an open
  recorder and a scope (every indexed transaction, or a given list of transaction keys) and clears, in that
  change, each transaction's references to lines the budget of its index row's month lacks (its own line
  with who and confidence, a split part's line, a refund's line, a pending suggestion with its confidence;
  the "why" question closed; the transaction itself stays).
- The line writes and history (finwise-yfu): the function that writes a history step of a change, and
  `undoHistoryStep`, through which a line applied by rule is taken back like any other step; for a step of
  a change that touched many transactions, only that transaction's units are restored.

**`ingest.Run`, the five steps.**

1. In one ledger view, take `ProjectedRun` and the rows: the whole ledger interpreted in one pass as above,
   with a tally that must place every row, or the run fails as a read does. On a timer tick or at start,
   stop here when the run is the one recorded in `meta`; a call made because a budget changed, or by the
   command, goes on. The ledger is read before the write lock is taken, so the lock is held only for steps
   2 to 5. The view is closed when the run ends.
2. Open one immediate transaction on `finwise.db`, through the recorder, author `rule`, with the instant
   and the Brazil day from the injected clock. The method recorded on the change is a fixed name that is
   not a method of the contract (so nothing that counts changes by method, such as the answers given
   through the queue, ever counts it); the name is the implementer's.
3. Refresh the index rows of the listed transactions already in it: day, cents, establishment key, whether
   the bank still reports it pending, and the run it was last listed in (`last_run`; `first_run` is the run
   that first indexed it). Then pair: the vanished rows are the bank-pending index rows whose provider ids
   the ledger no longer lists (whenever they vanished); the new rows are the listed posted transactions
   whose provider id is not in `tx_ids`; `classrules.Pair` matches them. For each pair, map the posted id
   to the pending row's key in `tx_ids` and give the index row the posted row's day and amount, no longer
   bank-pending; everything the person or a rule did to the pending row now belongs to the posted one,
   with no authored row rewritten. When the posted row falls in a different month, the references its new
   month's budget lacks are cleared as a budget save clears them, by the clearing function scoped to the
   paired keys (finwise-oib), in this run's change. An index row that the ledger stopped listing in this run and
   found no pair is counted once, in this run.
4. For every listed transaction dated on or after the tracking start month that was never evaluated and
   whose month's budget has at least one line: index it and mark it evaluated; apply `Decide` only when it
   has neither a line nor a pending review, so the rules never touch what the person already decided in
   the minutes before a tick. That check, and every read of authored data `Decide` needs, happens inside
   the transaction of step 2. A transaction whose month has no budget yet, or a budget with no line, stays
   unevaluated and unindexed, so the queue never holds something that cannot be answered.
5. If anything authored changed, record it as one change by `rule`; with nothing to record, no change is
   written. Record the run in `meta` and commit.

What `Decide` is given for one transaction (the ingest fills its plain input): from the interpreted row,
whether it is a movement between own accounts or a bill payment, unconverted, a credit, a refund by the
ledger's rule, a fee row, and whether the other side is a person; from `finwise.db`, the establishment's
nickname and default line (`establishments`), the line ids the budget of the transaction's month has
(finwise-ef7), the threshold and the minimum (finwise-11u), and the candidate examples: the indexed transactions of
the same establishment key that have a line, each with its line id, its day, who put it there, whether it
is excluded and whether it is split. What the ingest writes for each answer, through the recorder:

- apply: `tx_state` gets the line, who = the rule (the wire's `Regra`), no confidence, nothing pending, no
  "why" question; and the history step "Regra classificou como <linha>" with the name the line has in the
  budget of the transaction's month, on this change (finwise-yfu's step writer). It can be taken back like any
  other step.
- pending: `pending_reason` is the reason, `pending_line_id` and `pending_confidence` the suggestion and
  its confidence, or null for the two reasons that have none.
- leave, nothing to store: nothing authored. The transaction is still marked evaluated.

**Two callers at once.** Every step is idempotent, so two callers at once are safe: the second waits for
the first one's transaction (the immediate write lock) and finds nothing left to do. For that to hold, the
second decides from what it reads inside its own transaction: the run recorded in `meta`, the evaluated
flags, the mapped ids, whether a transaction already has a line or a pending review. A caller that read an
older snapshot than the run the first one recorded must not move the index or `meta` backwards; how it
detects that is the implementer's. A write of the person that arrives while the ingest holds the lock waits
for it (the five-second busy timeout of the app's database) and is its own change; one that commits before
the ingest takes the lock is seen by step 4.

**Never again, and only forward.** An evaluated transaction is never evaluated again: taking a rule's line
back (its history step undone) does not bring it back the next night, because `evaluated` is in the index,
which undo does not touch. Changing the threshold or the minimum of examples acts only on transactions
evaluated after the change, with no retroactive pass: what was applied stays applied, what is pending stays
pending with its suggestion and confidence. A paired posted row inherits its pending row's key and its
evaluated flag.

**A pending row that vanishes without a one-to-one match** keeps its authored rows and its index row;
nothing is deleted. It is counted unpaired once, in the run the ledger stopped listing it. While the ledger
does not list it, it is in no queue and no count (the queue and the counts are later work (finwise-rf3: the
weekly queue and `review.acceptPending`), and they look only at listed transactions); if it is listed
again, it comes back as it was, and it is not evaluated again. A vanished pending row can still be paired
in a later run, when its posted row first appears within the window. A pending row that was never indexed
(never evaluated, never touched by the person) is not an index row: its posted replacement is a new
transaction like any other. A posted row the index has already seen is never a pairing candidate.

**When the bank rewords a row** so its establishment key changes: a transaction already evaluated keeps what
it has, and its index row takes the new key in step 3; later rows under the new key are a new establishment
and go to the queue, with only the examples of the new key; nothing authored is lost. Grouping keys is
deferred.

**Counts.** `Run` returns counts only: indexed (the transactions step 4 marked evaluated in this run),
paired, unpaired, applied by rule, pending per reason (the three reasons), and whether it stopped at step
1. In a run, every transaction marked evaluated ends in exactly one of applied, pending, left, nothing to
store, or already decided by the person. `internal/ingest` imports no logger and prints nothing; a source
test says so, as `TestOnlyTheRequestLogWritesAnything` does for `internal/api`.

**Failures.** A failure (the snapshot missing, a file that is not a database, a version the reader does not
know, no projection row, the rules not placing every row, a database error, the lock timing out) changes
nothing: the transaction of step 2 rolls back, or was never opened. It is returned as an error of a closed
set of kinds that distinguishes at least "the snapshot is unavailable" (missing, unreadable, an unknown
version, no projection row) from anything else, so a caller can log the kind without the message and try
again on the next tick.

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing when the ingest runs | nothing changes; reported by kind; tried again on the next tick |
| a pending row with authored data is posted under a new id | the ingest maps the new id to the same key when the match is one to one; otherwise the rows stay, out of every queue and count, and the ingest counts them once |
| a transaction disappears from the ledger | its authored rows and its index entry stay; nothing is deleted; it is in no count until listed again |
| the bank rewords a row so its establishment key changes | a transaction already evaluated keeps what it has, and its index row takes the new key; later rows under the new key are a new establishment and go to the queue; nothing authored is lost |
| a tab and the ingest write at once | writes queue; each is its own change; an undo that lost the race is refused |
| two callers run the ingest together | every step is idempotent; the later one finds nothing to do |

**The proof on a real ledger, and the privacy rule.** A real ledger is a person's whole financial history
and this repository is public. A real snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from it (amount,
description, name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull
request; a count may be shown to the person running the test and goes into no file and no pull request;
the test runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file, and otherwise skips. Fixtures are invented.
The test runs the ingest against a scratch `finwise.db` in `t.TempDir()`, never against the person's own
database. That scratch database holds real values as soon as the ingest runs (the index carries account
ids, establishment keys and amounts), so it stays in the temporary directory, is removed with it, and
nothing of it is printed. The clock is injected: an instant in the Brazil month of the ledger's latest
listed transaction, so the tracking start month is that month. The test compares in memory and fails with
fixed sentences; on success it logs counts only. The steps: run as the command with no budget (every
count is zero); save an invented budget for that month with invented line names through the budget's
store; run as after a budget change and log the counts; check that indexed equals the number of listed
transactions dated in or after the start month (counted in memory from the same interpretation), that
applied by rule and "Baixa confiança" are 0 (a database where nobody has put anything on a line has no
default line and no example), that no index row is dated before the start month, and that the evaluated
transactions add up across the outcomes; run as a timer tick (it stops at step 1); run as the command (no
row is added to `changes`, and the canonical dump of the journaled tables is equal). Its failure path is
read in review.

**Privacy and conventions, beyond the above.** Work happens in a worktree and ends at local commits:
atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a work item or a plan in
a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; the float guard and
the `time.Now` guard already cover `internal/ingest` from its first file (finwise-po6, finwise-jzw: the source tests
