**Where the server departs from the stand-in on purpose.** Typed refusals instead of thrown errors; the
envelope carries a reason. The stand-in throws a plain `Error`; nothing in it changes here. The test
that pins this slice's part is the envelope test of `manifest.test.ts`.

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. Nothing
in this slice touches a ledger, real or invented; no value from a real snapshot (amount, description,
name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic,
Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit
message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant (this slice runs none). Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese
and everything else is English; a design value in a component comes from a token (this slice touches no
component). The manifest is generated, never edited by hand.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `API_ERROR_KINDS` holds the six older wire kinds, `refused` and `network`; the list of reasons
holds exactly the nine of the table, in that order; `npm --prefix web run typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run contract:check` passes, and the diff of `internal/contract/contract.json`
against the commit this work started from shows only the error envelope and the definitions it needs.
- [ ] In `manifest.test.ts`, the manifest's `error` schema accepts `{error:{kind}}` for each of the six
older wire kinds and `{error:{kind:"refused",reason}}` for each of the nine reasons, and rejects
`{error:{kind:"refused"}}`, `{error:{kind:"refused",reason:"nope"}}`,
`{error:{kind:"refused",reason:"stale_change",detail:"x"}}`,
`{error:{kind:"read_only",reason:"month_closed"}}`, `{error:{kind:"network"}}` and `{kind:"read_only"}`.
- [ ] `internal/contract` hands out an argument schema for each of the 82 methods; a test compiles all
82 with the schema library the conformance tests already use, and for `budget.save` accepts
`["2026-03",[{"key":"rec","name":"Receita","lines":[{"name":"Salário","amount":8000}]}]]` and rejects
the same array with `amount` as a string, with an extra field on the line, and with a third element.
- [ ] `internal/contract` hands out the nine reasons in the order of the table, read from the manifest
and not written a second time in Go; a test compares them with the table above.
- [ ] `parse` refuses a manifest whose method has no argument schema and one in which the reasons cannot
be found, in the style of `TestParseRefusesWhatItDoesNotUnderstand`.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api`, `web/src/api/http/`, `web/src/api/fake/` or `web/src/api/failures.ts`
is changed, and `go test ./...` and `npm --prefix web test` pass.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against its own deliberate break, named in the final
report: the envelope test against a `reason` allowed on every kind and against `refused` with an
optional reason; the reasons test against a reason removed from the TypeScript list without
regenerating; the schema test against definitions left out of what Go hands out.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` with the manifest current, and an envelope with a reason on
another kind, or `refused` without one, does not validate against the manifest.

## Tests
- Unit (vitest, `web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts`), over the generated manifest: the envelopes the
  error schema accepts and rejects.
- Unit (`internal/contract/contract_test.go`), over the embedded manifest: an argument schema for every
  method; all 82 compile; the `budget.save` vectors; the nine reasons in order.
- Table (`internal/contract/contract_test.go`), over hand-written manifests: what `parse` refuses.
- The gate's own checks: the manifest is current; the types check.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/api/contract/errors.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts`,
`web/scripts/contract-manifest.mjs`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `internal/contract/contract.go`,
`internal/contract/contract_test.go`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/http/client.ts`, `web/src/api/http/failure.ts`, `web/src/api/failures.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/changes.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/classification.ts`,
`internal/api/conformance_test.go`, `internal/api/errors.go`, `internal/api/router.go`, `go.mod`,
`bin/ci`

Two small modules: the contract's error type with its test and generated manifest, and the Go package
that reads the manifest. Three code files at most (`errors.ts`, `contract.go`, and the generator only if
it cannot express the union), two test files and one generated file. The HTTP client, the failure
handler, the stand-in and every file of `internal/api` are read and left as they are: what the interface
does with a refusal and how the server answers one are other slices'. `go.mod` gains no requirement: the
schema library is already there, and here only a test uses it. Only `bin/ci` proves the whole, because
the change spans the TypeScript types, the generated manifest and Go.
close_reason: The contract and the manifest carry a refused kind whose envelope always holds one reason of a closed list of nine, as a closed union (no other kind may carry a reason, refused may not omit one); internal/contract hands out every method's argument schema as a document that compiles alone, and the reasons in the contract's order read from the manifest. bin/ci green on the branch merged with main; hosted check passed. Review: three independent mutations (last reason dropped, argument schema emptied, definitions not followed transitively) each failed a test; the implementer's nine breaks each failed one too. Nothing answers refused or validates arguments yet.

title: Let an agent propose a change and the person approve or refuse it on the weekly review's card
description:
## What changes for the user
Once an agent can read the person's finance data, the next thing it notices is what should change: a
purchase that should not count, a tag missing on the month's trip, a reimbursement nobody linked, a
subscription that should be marked for cancelling. Today it can only say so in the terminal, and the
person retypes each change into the app. The approvals card of the weekly review, "Aguardando seu ok",
exists but is always empty, and its buttons do nothing. After this lands the agent proposes a change
with a reason, and the person finds it on that card, worded by the app, with the agent's reason and the
name it goes by. "Aprovar" makes the change exactly as the screen would, and it can be undone like any
other; "Recusar" leaves everything as it was and lets the person say why, which the agent reads back
with the outcome of each of its proposals. A proposal nobody answers waits; one whose target has changed
in the meantime is not applied. If it were wrong, the person would find a change they never approved,
an approval applied twice, or a proposal applied over something they had changed since.

## Outcome
An agent holding the token submits a proposal of one of a closed list of changes with
`finwise agent propose`, and lists its proposals with their outcome with `finwise agent proposals`. The
proposal is stored in the app's database, outside the journal, and shown on the approvals card while it
waits. Approving runs the proposed method's own handler inside a change journaled under the author
`model`, once; a target changed since the proposal answers the new refusal reason `proposal_stale`
and closes it as stale.
Refusing closes it with the person's optional reason and changes nothing else.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person: a Go server over a read-only snapshot
of the person's bank data and a Vue interface. *The app's database* (`finwise.db`, `internal/authored`)
holds what the person authors; only that package executes SQL, every statement is a constant registered
in `allStatements` (`internal/authored/statements.go`), and migrations live in
`internal/authored/migrations/` (the last is `0008_session.sql`). *The journal* (`changes`,
`change_effects`) records each change with its author (`person`, `rule` or `model`; `Author` in
`internal/authored/journal.go`), its method, its instant and its effects, so that `changes.undo` can take
it back; a table written through the journal is registered in `productionTables`, and a table
deliberately kept out of it is named in `notJournaledTables` (`internal/authored/registry.go`), which
`TestEveryTableOfTheSchemaIsJournaledOrDeliberatelyNot` and
`TestTheTablesDeliberatelyNotJournaledAreTheNamedOnes` (`internal/authored/journal_guard_test.go`) check.
*A change* is opened by `(*Database).Change(ctx, ChangeFacts{Author, Method, At}, func(*Recorder) error)`
(`internal/authored/recorder.go`); a handler that records no effect and asks no id leaves no row. *The
contract* is the API's list of methods, written as TypeScript types under `web/src/api/contract/`,
classified in `web/src/api/contract/classification.ts` and generated into
`internal/contract/contract.json` by `npm --prefix web run contract`; the manifest refuses any schema
that accepts anything (`findEmptySchemas` in `web/scripts/contract-manifest.mjs`). *A write handler*
(`WriteHandler`, `internal/api/writes.go`) runs inside a change the router opened with the author
`person` (`recordWrite`); *a journal handler* (`JournalHandler`, registered with `RegisterJournal`) opens
its own transactions through the `Journal` interface, as `changes.undo` does; both are wrapped by
`withSnapshotTakenIn`, which takes a new ledger snapshot in and retries once when a lookup finds the
snapshot not taken in. *The agent's token* and `finwise agent read` come from the item this one depends
on: a request carrying the token is answered for the reads and refused `read_only` for anything else.
*The stand-in* (`web/src/api/fake/`) is the in-memory backend that answers with the design prototype's
dataset; *parity* (`npm --prefix web run parity`, `web/scripts/parity/states.mjs`) measures every ported
screen state against the prototype's screenshots.

**What exists today.** `review.approve`, `review.refuse` and `review.propose` are registered and answer
null (`internal/api/review_approvals.go`); `review.weekly` answers `approvals: []` (`internal/api/review.go`).
The card is `web/src/screens/revisao/ApprovalsCard.vue`, inside `WeeklyTab.vue`; it shows
`ApprovalRequest` (`id`, `title`, `reason`, in `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`), toasts
`Aprovado: <title>.` with "Desfazer", and toasts `Recusado. Nada foi alterado.` with "Desfazer" too. The
stand-in seeds three waiting proposals (`web/src/api/fake/review-data.ts`), whose titles are the design's
model for wording: `Subir o teto de Delivery de R$ 200 para R$ 250`, `Marcar como "não conta": Estorno
de anuidade R$ 120,00`, `Mudar status de Revista digital para Cancelar`; and its history step for an
approved exclusion reads `IA marcou como não conta (você aprovou)` (`web/src/api/fake/review.ts`).

**What the person decided, and what lost.**
- An agent never writes directly: it reads and proposes. In the first version it may propose what
  belongs to a transaction (line, tags, note, with the bulk and whole-establishment variants), budget,
  subscriptions, exclusions, splits and reimbursements; closing a month, the PIN and the settings are
  out of its reach. There is nothing to configure: the list is fixed in the server. Lost: read only;
  direct writes for some classes; only line, tag and note; everything but the PIN.
- A proposal stores the method, its arguments and the reason the agent wrote. The app, not the agent,
  words what will happen. Approving runs the same handler the screen uses, with its refusals, and the
  app applies the change, never the proposer.
- A change applied from an approved proposal is journaled under the author `model` and carries the
  name its proposer gave; the person reads that it was proposed by that name and approved by them, and
  undoes it as any change.
- A refusal closes the proposal and may carry a reason the person writes, which the agent reads. A
  proposal nobody answers stays, with no expiry. When what it would change has changed, approving
  answers a refusal and the proposal closes as stale. Lost: a refusal with no reason; expiry after a
  number of days.
- *Decided by the person on 2026-11-23, after the drafts were written:*
  - A refusal cannot be undone: answering is not a recorded change, so the toast after "Recusar" offers
    no "Desfazer". Lost: journaling refusals (the proposals' rows would be journaled, and undoing a
    refusal would reopen a proposal the agent was already told was refused).
  - The wording is the one written below: the table of titles, `· proposto por <proposer>` on the card,
    and the history note `Proposto por <proposer> · você aprovou`; the card's empty sentence is
    unchanged. Lost: other wordings.
  - The refusal reason is typed in a field that opens after "Recusar". Lost: a field always visible under
    each request (it would move the measured weekly state and need a design).
  - A stale approval answers a refusal reason of its own, `proposal_stale`, with the sentence "Isso mudou
    depois da proposta. Nada foi alterado.", and `stale_change` keeps what it already means (undoing or
    extending a change). Lost: reusing `stale_change`, whose sentence, "Isso já foi alterado depois e
    não pode mais ser desfeito.", speaks of undoing and would tell the person something false about an
    approval.
  - The establishment's default line for future purchases (`transactions.setDefaultLine`) is the
    whole-establishment variant of a line an agent may propose; past purchases are moved only by an
    explicit selection (the bulk line change of the difference view's item). Lost: proposing "all
    purchases here", which extends an earlier change by its id.
  - "Aprovar tudo" approves only the proposals one sentence describes and leaves waiting, untouched,
    every proposal that needs the difference view; it is built in that view's item.
- No screen lists answered proposals in this version; that is a later item (`finwise-moo`, a list of
  answered proposals with the undo of each approved one). The agent reads outcomes through its command.

**This item carries the proposals one sentence can describe:** tags, note, exclusions, splits,
reimbursements, subscriptions and an establishment's default line. A line proposed for a transaction
waiting for review goes to the weekly queue, in the next item; a budget, a line for a transaction already
on one and the bulk line change need a view of the values before and after, in the item after it, which
waits for a design.

**What the code forces, decided here, with what lost.**
- *A new method, `review.submitProposal`, not `review.propose`.* `review.propose(id)` already has a
  meaning: it takes the id of a change the month's report suggested and puts it on the card, called by
  the report's button (`sendSuggestion` in `web/src/screens/revisao/useClosingActions.ts`), and it stays
  as it is, answering null, until the nightly model produces report suggestions (`finwise-6cp`). The
  token opens `review.submitProposal` and the reads; `review.approve` and `review.refuse` stay the
  person's. Lost: changing `review.propose`'s signature (it would break the report's flow for a method
  the agent does not share with it).
- *The list is a closed union in the contract.* `ProposalDraft` is `{ change: ProposedChange; reason:
  string; proposer: string }`, and `ProposedChange` has one member per proposable method, `{ method:
  '<domain>.<name>'; arguments: [<the method's own parameter types>] }`. The manifest then validates a
  proposal's arguments at the door like any other write's, and the list of decision 6 is readable in one
  place. A compile-time check fails when a member's arguments are not assignable to its method's
  parameters. Lost: `arguments: unknown[]` (the manifest refuses an unconstrained schema) and a JSON
  string (it would reach the handler unchecked).
- *The members of this item*, with the title the server writes for each. `N` is the transaction as the
  card names it, its shown name and the absolute amount as the review's sentences write it (`reaisText`
  in `internal/api/messages.go`, e.g. `Padaria Sol R$ 12,90`); `E` an establishment's shown name; `S` a
  subscription's name; `L` a line's name; `T` a tag as stored, with its `#`; `n` a count; quoted text is
  the argument itself.

  | member | title |
  | --- | --- |
  | `transactions.addTag(id, tag)` | `Adicionar T a N` |
  | `transactions.removeTag(id, tag)` | `Tirar T de N` |
  | `transactions.addTagToMany(ids, tag)` | `Adicionar T a n transações` (one id: `Adicionar T a N`) |
  | `transactions.addFixedTag(id, tag)` | `Adicionar T a todas as compras em E` |
  | `transactions.removeFixedTag(id, tag)` | `Tirar T de todas as compras em E` |
  | `transactions.setNote(id, note)` | `Anotar em N: "note"`; a blank note: `Apagar a nota de N` |
  | `transactions.setDefaultLine(id, line)` | `Pôr as próximas compras em E em L` |
  | `transactions.setExcluded(id, false)` | `Voltar a contar N` |
  | `transactions.setExclusionReason(id, reason)` | `Mudar o motivo de "não conta" de N para "reason"` |
  | `transactions.excludeMany(ids, reason)` | `Marcar como "não conta": N` (several: `Marcar n transações como "não conta"`) |
  | `transactions.setSplit(id, parts)` | `Dividir N: L R$ x, L R$ y` (a part with no line: `sem linha`); null: `Desfazer a divisão de N` |
  | `transactions.setReimbursable(id, on)` | `Marcar N como reembolsável` / `Desmarcar o reembolso de N` |
  | `transactions.setExpectedReimbursement(id, amount)` | `Esperar R$ x de reembolso por N`; null: `Tirar o reembolso esperado de N` |
  | `transactions.linkReimbursement(id, creditId)` | `Ligar o PIX de <the credit's name> R$ x a N` |
  | `transactions.unlinkReimbursement(id)` | `Desligar o PIX de N` |
  | `subscriptions.create(transactionId)` | `Criar assinatura de N` |
  | `subscriptions.setStatus(id, status)` | `Mudar status de S para <status>` |
  | `subscriptions.setLine(id, line)` | `Pôr a assinatura S em L` |
  | `subscriptions.setReviewDate(id, day)` | `Revisar S em <dd/mm/aaaa>` |
  | `subscriptions.setNote(id, note)` | `Anotar em S: "note"`; a blank note: `Apagar a nota de S` |

  The sentences live in `internal/api/messages.go`, with the server's other Portuguese text.
  `transactions.setExcluded` is a member only with `false`: turning it on takes effect only once a reason
  is given, which `excludeMany` does in one call. Left out, each for a reason of the code:
  `subscriptions.acceptSuggestion` and `rejectSuggestion` take no argument and act on whatever suggestion
  is open when they run, which may not be the one the agent saw (`subscriptions.create` names its
  purchase); `transactions.applyLineToEstablishment` extends an earlier change by its id and cannot be
  stored ahead of it; `review.keepSubscription` and `review.cancelSubscription` are steps of the month's
  closing (`subscriptions.setStatus` makes the same change); refunds, nicknames, a line's reason,
  `confirmLine`, `undoHistoryStep`, every `settings.*`, every closing method, `session.*` and
  `changes.undo` are outside the decided list.
- *Submitting checks the proposal against the state as it is.* `review.submitProposal` is a journal
  handler. It opens a change under `model` with the proposed method, runs that method's registered
  write handler over the request's ledger view and the change's recorder, words the title from what it
  read, notes the id of the newest change in the journal (0 for none), and rolls the change back
  whatever happened. A refusal of the handler is answered as it is and nothing is stored; a handler that
  recorded no effect (the change is already true) is answered null and nothing is stored; otherwise the
  proposal is inserted, in a transaction of its own, and answered `{ proposalId, title }`. The proposer is
  trimmed and must be 1 to 40 characters, the reason 1 to 500; anything else is `bad_request`. Lost:
  storing whatever arrives (the person would meet proposals that can never apply, and the agent would
  learn it only from a refusal days later).
- *Storage.* Migration `0009_proposals.sql` creates `proposals`: an id that is never reused, the
  instant submitted, the proposer, the method, the arguments as a JSON array, the reason, the title,
  `based_on` (the newest change id at submission), the outcome (`waiting`, `approved`, `refused`,
  `stale`), the instant answered, the person's refusal text, the refusal reason that closed a stale one,
  and the id of the change an approval made; CHECKs keep the answered columns consistent with the
  outcome. The table is named in `notJournaledTables` with the reason "a request and its answer; what an
  approval applies is journaled as a change of its own": answering is not itself a journaled change, and
  undoing an approved change leaves its proposal approved, as the index of transactions is not journaled
  either. The proposer's name lives on this row, which names the change it made; the journal's `changes`
  table is not altered. Lost: a `proposer` column on `changes` (it would repeat this row and touch the
  journal's table for one author).
- *Approving.* `review.approve(id)` becomes a journal handler. It reads the waiting proposal, opens a
  change with `ChangeFacts{Author: model, Method: <the proposed method>, At: <the request's instant>}`,
  checks again inside that change that the proposal still waits (two approvals at once apply it once;
  the second answers null), runs the proposed method's handler, and then refuses with `proposal_stale`
  when the change recorded no effect, or when any change after `based_on` that is still in force has an
  effect on a unit this change has an effect on, the unit as the undo engine counts it (`overlaps` in
  `internal/authored/journal.go`). Otherwise it adds, on each transaction the method names by id, a
  history note `Proposto por <proposer> · você aprovou`, marks the proposal approved with the change's
  id in the same transaction, and answers `{ changeId, title }` (`Approved`). A refusal, the handler's or
  `proposal_stale`, rolls the change back, closes the proposal as stale with that reason in a transaction
  of its own, and is answered as the refusal, so the person reads its sentence. A handler's own
  refusal (`not_found`, `unknown_line`, `month_closed`, `split_with_reimbursement` and the rest) is
  answered with its own reason, which is also the more precise one. Any other failure
  (`internal`, `ledger_unavailable`) leaves it waiting. The change's method is the proposed one, so every
  query keyed by method treats it as that write. The handlers' own attributions are not touched: a step
  they write still reads `Você ...`, since the person approved it. Lost: the method `review.approve` on
  the change (it would hide what the change did from every query keyed by method); applying over a
  changed target (it would silently overwrite what the person did since).
- *Refusing.* `review.refuse(id, reason)` gains the reason, blank allowed, at most 500 characters. It
  closes a waiting proposal as refused with the reason, records no change, and answers `{ title }`
  (`RefusedProposal`), or null when nothing by that id waits. It is not a recorded change, so it has no
  undo: the card's toast after it offers no "Desfazer". Lost: a journaled refusal (the proposals' rows
  would have to be journaled, and undoing a refusal would bring back a proposal the agent was already
  told was refused).
- *The card in this item.* `ApprovalRequest` gains `proposer: string | null` (null for what no agent
  proposed, such as the stand-in's seeded proposals), and `review.weekly` lists every waiting proposal,
  oldest first. The card adds `· proposto por <proposer>` after the reason when there is a proposer.
  "Recusar" opens, under the request, a text field (`Por quê? (opcional)`, at most 500 characters) with
  "Recusar" to confirm and "Cancelar"; the toast is `Recusado. Nada foi alterado.` with no action. A null
  answer to approve or refuse makes the card fetch again. The states the parity measures do not change,
  because the seeded proposals have no proposer and no measured state presses "Recusar". The card's
  "Aprovar tudo" is in the item of the difference view: on the prototype's dataset it would change the
  measured state `revisao-semanal`, so it needs a design, as that item already does.
- *The new reason reaches every copy of the closed list.* `proposal_stale` is added, after
  `split_with_reimbursement`, to `REFUSAL_REASONS` (`web/src/api/contract/errors.ts`, the contract's
  `RefusalReason`), to `REFUSAL_SENTENCES` (`web/src/api/failures.ts`) with "Isso mudou depois da
  proposta. Nada foi alterado.", to `refusalReasons` and its constants (`internal/api/errors.go`), to the
  tests that pin the list (`internal/contract/contract_test.go`, `web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts`,
  `web/src/api/failures.test.ts`, `web/src/api/refusal-reasons.test.ts`) and to the table of refusals in
  `AGENTS.md`. Its producer is approval: a write case that expects the refusal with that reason is what
  `TestEveryReasonOfTheClosedListIsCasedOrNamedAsWithoutAProducer` (`internal/api/write_runner_test.go`)
  requires, so `reasonsWithoutProducer` (`internal/api/write_conformance_test.go`) stays empty. The
  stand-in produces it too: its `approve` rejects a seeded proposal whose effect would change nothing (the
  subscription already holds the status, the transaction is already excluded with that reason, the line
  already has that cap) with `ApiFailure('refused', { reason: 'proposal_stale' })` (`web/src/api/http/failure.ts`)
  and closes it as stale.
- *The agent's list.* `review.proposals()` is a read, open to the token like every read: every proposal,
  newest first, as `ProposalRecord` (`id`, `title`, `change`, `reason`, `proposer`, `submittedAt`,
  `outcome`, `answeredAt`, `refusal` (the person's text or null), `staleReason` (the refusal that closed
  a stale one, or null), `changeId`, and `undone`, true once that change was undone). Instants are UTC
  with milliseconds, as the journal writes them. It answers `[]` on a server without `--db` and needs no
  snapshot.
- *The stand-in.* `submitProposal` answers null (no agent talks to the stand-in: the command reaches only
  the real server), `proposals()` lists the seeded proposals with their outcome, and `refuse(id, reason)`
  keeps the reason. Lost: wording and applying the twenty members in TypeScript a second time for a
  caller that never exists in prototype mode.
- *The command's verbs.* `finwise agent propose --reason <text> --name <name> <method>
  <json-arguments>` (the name falls back to `FINWISE_AGENT_NAME`; the flag wins) and `finwise agent
  proposals`, with the exit statuses and the fixed sentences of `finwise agent read`. A method that is
  not a member is a usage error that lists the members, read from the server's own list in the same
  binary; a test pins that list to the manifest's union.
- *Conformance.* The write harness (`internal/api/write_conformance_test.go`) gains a mode for a write
  that answers without a journaled change: the answer validates, the journal gains no row, every
  journaled table is as it was, and the rows of `proposals` equal the case's golden file. Submitting and
  refusing are of that mode; approving is a recorded change, whose cases first submit through `before`.

**Respect, as everywhere.** Money is integer cents, and no source file of `internal/api` or
`internal/authored` touches a float; the files of `internal/api` log nothing and read the clock only from
the request; no command output and no log line holds a value from the ledger the person did not ask to
see. `AfterBudgetSaved` is not concerned here: no member of this item saves a budget.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The manifest lists `review.submitProposal` (write) and `review.proposals` (read); the argument
  schema of `review.submitProposal` accepts exactly the twenty members of the table, `findEmptySchemas`
  finds nothing, and `npm --prefix web run contract:check` passes.
- [ ] Changing one member's argument tuple so it is no longer assignable to its method's parameters makes
  `npm --prefix web run typecheck` fail; a Go test fails when the server's list of members differs from
  the manifest's.
- [ ] With the token, `review.submitProposal` is answered and `review.approve` and `review.refuse` are
  answered 403 `read_only`; a method outside the union, such as `review.closeMonth` or
  `settings.setThreshold`, is answered 400 `bad_request` and stores nothing.
- [ ] For every member, a submission over the invented ledger stores one waiting proposal with the title
  of the table, and leaves every journaled table and the journal as they were; a submission the handler
  refuses is answered with that refusal and stores nothing; one that would change nothing is answered
  null and stores nothing.
- [ ] `review.weekly` lists the waiting proposals oldest first with their proposer; with none it answers
  `approvals: []`, and no existing golden file moves.
- [ ] Approving a waiting proposal records one change with author `model` and the proposed method,
  answers its id and title, adds the history note on each transaction the method names, and marks the
  proposal approved with that change's id; undoing that change restores every journaled table and leaves
  the proposal approved, with `undone: true` in `review.proposals`.
- [ ] Two approvals of one proposal sent at once record one change; the other answers null.
- [ ] A proposal whose target a later change in force has changed (a note set by the person after a
  `setNote` proposal; a split set by the person after a `setSplit` proposal; the same tag added by the
  person after an `addTag` proposal, which leaves the approval nothing to do) is answered 409
  `proposal_stale`, records no change and closes as stale with `staleReason: "proposal_stale"`; after that later change is undone, a
  new proposal of the same change is approved.
- [ ] A proposal whose handler refuses at approval (its transaction no longer listed) is answered with
  that refusal, `not_found`, and closes as stale with it; one whose approval fails with `internal` or
  `ledger_unavailable` stays waiting.
- [ ] Refusing with a reason closes the proposal as refused with that text, records no change, answers
  its title, and leaves every journaled table as it was; refusing a proposal that does not wait answers
  null.
- [ ] `proposal_stale` is in `REFUSAL_REASONS`, `REFUSAL_SENTENCES` (with "Isso mudou depois da proposta.
  Nada foi alterado."), the Go `refusalReasons`, the manifest's `RefusalReason`, the tests that pin the
  list and the table of refusals in `AGENTS.md`; a write case expects it from `review.approve`, so
  `TestEveryReasonOfTheClosedListIsCasedOrNamedAsWithoutAProducer` passes with `reasonsWithoutProducer`
  empty; `stale_change` is answered by no approval.
- [ ] On the weekly tab, an approval answered `proposal_stale` (the stand-in's approval of a seeded
  proposal whose effect already holds) shows "Isso mudou depois da proposta. Nada foi alterado." once and
  the card no longer lists the proposal.
- [ ] `review.proposals` answers every proposal newest first with the fields of `ProposalRecord`; it
  answers `[]` on a server without `--db` and with the snapshot missing.
- [ ] Without the app's database, `review.submitProposal` is answered `read_only` before its body is
  read, as the other writes are.
- [ ] The card shows `· proposto por <proposer>` for a proposal that has one and nothing for one that
  has none; "Recusar" opens the field, the confirmation sends the typed reason, and the toast reads
  `Recusado. Nada foi alterado.` with no action; a null answer makes the card fetch again.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` passes for `revisao-semanal`, `revisao-aprovacao-aprovada` and
  `revisao-semanal-tablet` with no limit raised, and its output is in the pull request.
- [ ] The write series over the invented ledger (`TestTheWriteSeriesHoldsOverTheInventedLedger`) passes
  with a step that submits a proposal, one that approves it and one that refuses another, and the count
  of methods it records changes through rises by one, for `review.approve`.
- [ ] The end-to-end test in `cmd/finwise/agent_test.go` over the real server and an invented snapshot: `finwise agent
  propose` an `addTag`, see it in `review.weekly` with a session, approve it, see it approved with its
  change id in `finwise agent proposals`, undo the change, see `undone: true`; propose a `setNote`,
  refuse it with a reason, read the reason back; no line on standard error contains the token,
  `ledgerSentinel` or any of `leakedValues`.
- [ ] Each rule was seen failing once by breaking it on purpose, and the pull request names the test that
  failed for each: the second check that the proposal still waits; the staleness comparison; the dry run's
  rollback; the author `model`; the refusal leaving the journal untouched.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` documents the proposals (the table and why it is not journaled, the members, the
  staleness rule, the command's two verbs, the token's access to `review.submitProposal`) and gains the
  row `proposal_stale` | approving a proposal when what it would change has changed since it was
  submitted, or already holds | Isso mudou depois da proposta. Nada foi alterado. in the table of
  refusals.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`.
- [ ] Done when: an agent proposes a change from its terminal, the person approves or refuses it on the
  weekly review's card, the change is applied once under `model` and can be undone, and the agent reads
  the outcome.

## Tests
- Unit, in `internal/authored`: the migration; the table's CHECKs refusing an inconsistent row; insert,
  claim inside a change, close as approved, refused and stale; the overlap of a change's effects with the
  effects in force since a change id; an undo leaving a proposal as it was.
- Integration, in `internal/api`, through the router: each member submitted, refused at submission and
  idle at submission; the token's access; approval, the concurrent approval, staleness by a later change
  and by a refusal, a failure that leaves it waiting; refusal; the list; a server without `--db`; a
  submission and an approval across a snapshot not taken in.
- Golden: `review.proposals` in `readCases` over both ledgers (`[]`); new cases over the invented authored
  state for `review.proposals` with one proposal of each outcome and for `review.weekly` with waiting
  proposals; write cases for submission, approval and refusal. No existing file moves.
- Unit, in `web/src/api/`: the new reason in the pinned lists and its sentence shown once on screen
  (`refusal-reasons.test.ts`, `failures.test.ts`).
- Compile-fail, in `web/src/api/contract/`: every member assignable to its method's parameters.
- Unit, screen, in `web/src/screens/revisao/`: the proposer's mention, the refusal field and its toast, the
  refetch on null, over the stand-in.
- Regression, visual (parity): the three weekly states above, unchanged.
- End-to-end, in `cmd/finwise`: the sequence of the criterion, extending the end-to-end read test of the item before.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/authored/migrations/0009_proposals.sql`, `internal/authored/proposals.go`,
`internal/authored/proposals_test.go`, `internal/authored/statements.go`, `internal/authored/registry.go`,
`internal/authored/journal_guard_test.go`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/proposals.go`,
`internal/api/review_approvals.go`, `internal/api/proposal_titles.go`, `internal/api/messages.go`,
`internal/api/review.go`, `internal/api/writes.go`, `internal/api/router.go`,
`internal/api/review_approvals_test.go`, `internal/api/review_warnings_test.go`,
`internal/api/review_warnings_write_cases_test.go`, `internal/api/write_conformance_test.go`,
`internal/api/write_runner_test.go`, `internal/api/write_walk_test.go`, `internal/api/conformance_test.go`,
`internal/api/authored_conformance_test.go`, `internal/api/realsnapshot_writes_series_test.go`,
`internal/api/realsnapshot_writes_checks_test.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/classification.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/proposed-change.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/review.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review-model.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review-rules.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/review-data.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review.test.ts`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/ApprovalsCard.vue`, `web/src/screens/revisao/useReviewActions.ts`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/weekly.test.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/errors.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts`, `web/src/api/failures.ts`, `web/src/api/failures.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/refusal-reasons.test.ts`, `internal/api/errors.go`, `internal/contract/contract_test.go`,
`cmd/finwise/agent.go`, `cmd/finwise/agent_test.go`,
`cmd/finwise/database_test.go`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `internal/authored/journal.go`, `internal/authored/recorder.go`,
`internal/authored/undo.go`, `internal/api/transaction_tag_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_count_writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_reimbursement_writes.go`,
`internal/api/establishment_writes.go`, `internal/api/subscriptions_writes.go`,
`internal/api/transaction_target.go`, `internal/api/changes.go`, `internal/api/errors.go`,
`internal/api/reads.go`, `web/src/api/http/failure.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/WeeklyTab.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/useClosingActions.ts`, `web/scripts/contract-manifest.mjs`,
`web/scripts/parity/states.mjs`, `design/README.md`, `bin/ci`

A schema change, two handlers and a read in `internal/api`, the contract and its manifest, the stand-in,
one card and two verbs of the command: `size:L`. It is one item because the contract types are shared by
every part, and the card cannot be backed without the storage nor the storage be useful without the card.
The handlers of the proposed methods are called, never edited.

## Recovery path
The migration only adds a table. A database migrated by it is copied first to `<name>.before-<UTC
timestamp>` by the migration runner, as for every migration. Reverting the merge commit leaves the table
in a database that recorded `0009_proposals`, and the server then refuses to start, because the runner
stops on a recorded migration the binary does not carry: restore the copy taken before the migration, or
keep running a binary that carries it. Changes approved while it ran are ordinary changes of the journal
and stay undoable.

title: Decide by rule what to do with a new transaction, pair a vanished pending charge with its posted one, and let a pending review carry no suggestion
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the app never asks the person about anything real: the weekly queue of "Pendências" holds only the
prototype's invented examples, each one with a line the model is said to suggest and a percentage of
confidence, and no rule exists that would put a new purchase on the line the person always uses for that
shop. This work writes down that rule, so that later the app can do it: a purchase from a shop the person
has told it about goes on its line by itself, one it is unsure of is asked about with its best guess, and
one it has never seen is asked about plainly, as "Estabelecimento novo" or "PIX para pessoa sem apelido",
with no guess at all. It also makes every screen ready for that last case. A pending transaction with no
guess shows "Pendente" in its line pill, its reason where a percentage used to be, no "Confirmar" in the
panel, and in the queue no invented suggestion and an "Aceitar" button that stays disabled until the
person picks a line, so nothing is ever sent without one. What the person would notice if this were
wrong: a purchase put on the wrong line without being asked, a confident guess offered where the app knew
nothing, the word "null" in a sentence, or a queue answer saved with no line.

## Outcome
A new package, `internal/classrules`, holds two pure functions. `Decide` takes one transaction that was
never evaluated, what the app's database knows about its establishment, the examples the person made, the
lines of the transaction's month and the two classifier settings, and answers exactly one of: leave it,
nothing to store (a fee), apply a line by rule, or pending with one of three reasons and either a suggested
line with its confidence or no suggestion at all. `Pair` takes the bank-pending transactions the ledger
stopped listing and the posted transactions never seen before, and answers the pairs that match one to one.
Neither is called by anything yet. In the contract, `PendingReview.suggestion`, `confidence` and
`justification` become nullable, the manifest is regenerated, the Go wire type follows, and every place of
the interface that shows a pending transaction has a tested state for a pending review without a
suggestion.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite snapshot that a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database* is
`finwise.db`, owned by the Go package `internal/authored`, where everything the person authors is kept.
*The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on;
it is the only existing statement of how writes behave, and it has no classifier at all: every pending
review in its dataset is invented, with a suggestion, a confidence and a justification. *The contract* is
the TypeScript interface `FinwiseApi` (`web/src/api/contract/`); *the manifest* is
`internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it by `npm --prefix web run contract`, versioned, never
edited by hand, and checked current by the gate. *A pending review* (`PendingReview` in
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`) is a transaction waiting for the person to choose its budget line.
*The queue* is the list of pending reviews in the weekly review ("Pendências"). *An establishment key* is
the key `internal/txrules` gives the other side of a row (`EstablishmentKey`, prefixed `doc:`, `name:` or
`text:`; `counterpart.go`); it may be a document number and is never logged. *A budget line* has an
integer id minted by the app's database; its name belongs to each budget version. *The month's budget* is
the budget version in force for a month. *The fees line* is the built-in line "Tarifas e juros", in no
group, which a month's budget has whenever it has at least one line. *The gate* is `bin/ci`.

**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

- The nightly model call is not part of this work, nor of the plan of which it is part: the app ends
  complete by hand and by rule, and the model is later work. What lost: a model now, which meant choosing
  a provider and an outbound dependency in every verification.
- A transaction without a suggestion can be pending: `suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification`
  become nullable. Why: without a model, "new establishment" has nothing to suggest, and the queue must
  still work. What lost: waiting for the model; inventing a suggestion.
- The rules run once per transaction, and a change of the threshold or the minimum of examples acts only
  on transactions evaluated after it. Why: a setting must not silently rewrite the queue or lines already
  applied. What lost: a retroactive pass on every settings change. This is enforced by the ingest, the
  one function that brings the app's database up to date with a new snapshot of the ledger and calls these
  rules for each transaction it has never evaluated ({{R2}}); `Decide` is pure and uses the values it is
  given.
- "Pending" everywhere means pending in the app's database and listed by the ledger now, in a month whose
  budget has at least one line. That is the queue's and the counts' business ({{V1}}); here it explains
  why `Pair` exists: a pending charge that the bank replaces with a posted one under a new id must not
  leave the person's work behind.
- Where the server departs from the stand-in on purpose, a test pins it: here, a pending review can have
  no suggestion, which the stand-in's data never has.

**What earlier work provides.** None of the following is in the repository when this text is written; each
is delivered before this bead starts, and its interfaces are to be read in the code as that work left
them.

- The transactions' tables, the index and the merged reads ({{T1}}): the migration `0003_transactions`
  with `tx_state(tx_key, line_id, classified_by, confidence, pending_reason, pending_line_id,
  pending_confidence, ask_reason, …)`, one row of optional facts per transaction, and the reads of
  `transactions.list`, `transactions.detail` and the review answering from it. A pending review on the
  wire is built from `pending_reason`, `pending_line_id` (answered as the name that line has in the budget
  of the transaction's own month) and `pending_confidence`. There is no column for a justification.
- The classifier settings ({{S1}}): the threshold (50 to 99, default 85) and the minimum of examples (1 to
  50, default 5), stored in `settings` and read by later work. The defaults are the constants
  `defaultConfidenceThreshold` and `defaultMinExamples` in `internal/api/settings_defaults.go` today.
- The guards that already name this package ({{F4b}}, {{F3b}}): the test that forbids floats and the test
  that forbids `time.Now` in non-test files were written to cover `internal/classrules` from its first
  file without being edited. Check that they now inspect the files this work adds.

**Part 1: `classrules.Decide`.** The package takes plain values and returns plain values; it opens
nothing, does no SQL and no I/O, and knows no HTTP, as `internal/txrules`, `internal/cardrules` and
`internal/potrules` do today. It depends on `internal/money` and `internal/brday` only, so it does not
import `internal/txrules`: its input is a struct of its own, which the ingest ({{R2}}) fills from the
interpreted row (`txrules.Transaction`: `Movement` is `OwnTransfer` or `BillPayment` for a movement,
`Unconverted`, `Refund`, `Fee`, `Person`, `EstablishmentKey`, `Day`, the sign of `Amount`) and from the
app's database. What it needs to know about one transaction: whether it is a movement between own accounts
or a bill payment; whether it is unconverted (a foreign amount with no value in reais); whether it is a
credit; whether the ledger's rule marks it as a refund; whether it is a fee row (the charge, or the credit
that discounts it); whether the other side is a person; whether that establishment or person has a
nickname; the establishment's default line, if any; the set of line ids the budget of the transaction's
own month has (the fees line included when that budget has any line); the examples; the threshold and the
minimum of examples.

`Decide` is called only for a transaction that was never evaluated and that has neither a line nor a
pending review; the ingest guarantees both. Its six steps, first match wins:

1. A movement between own accounts, a bill payment, an unconverted row, or a credit the ledger's rule marks
   as a refund: **leave it**. A refund waits for the person to point it at a line by hand; it does not go
   to the queue.
2. A fee row: **nothing to store**; it already counts on the fees line by rule (the budget's arithmetic
   counts a fee row that is on no line on the fees line: a charge adds, the credit that discounts it takes
   off).
3. Its establishment has a default line that the budget of the transaction's month has: **apply it, by
   rule**. A default line the month's budget lacks is passed over, and the steps go on to 4. Only an
   establishment has a default line; a person never does.
4. Otherwise take the examples: the transactions of the same establishment key that the person themselves
   put on a line (not a rule, not the model), not excluded, not split, whose line the budget of the
   transaction's month has. With `total` the number of those examples and `top` the number on the most
   frequent line:
   - with at least the configured minimum of examples (`total >= minimum`), one line strictly ahead of
     every other (`top` greater than the count of every other line), and `top * 100 >= threshold * total`:
     **apply that line, by rule**;
   - with any examples but short of one of those three: **pending, reason "Baixa confiança"**, suggesting
     the most frequent line, and on a tie the line of the example with the latest day, then the lower line
     id; its confidence is `top * 100 / total` rounded half up to a whole number.
5. No examples, and the other side a person with no nickname: **pending, "PIX para pessoa sem apelido"**,
   no suggestion.
6. No examples otherwise: **pending, "Estabelecimento novo"**, no suggestion. A person who has a nickname
   and no examples lands here too, as the steps read.

Credits go through the same steps as debits, so the queue also asks what a received PIX from someone
unknown is. "Excluded" means what it means everywhere: an exclusion that has a reason (an exclusion
switched on without a reason does not take effect, so such an example still counts). "Split" means the
transaction has split parts. The examples are the person's own decisions, so a line applied by rule in the
same run is never an example, and the result of `Decide` for one transaction does not depend on the order
in which the others are evaluated nor on the order its examples arrive in. A line a rule applies gets the
history step "Regra classificou como <linha>" and is stored with who = the rule and no confidence (the
contract's `Transaction.confidence` is "set when the classifier was the model"); both are the ingest's to
write ({{R2}}), and both can be taken back like any other. `belowThreshold` stays false until the model
exists: it is about the model's confidence only. The fourth reason the person named in the interview, a
value out of pattern, needs a judgment this work does not invent; it arrives with the model.

The rounding of the confidence is integer arithmetic, `(top * 200 + total) / (2 * total)`, or anything that
gives the same whole numbers: 2 of 3 is 67, 1 of 3 is 33, 1 of 2 is 50, 5 of 6 is 83, 1 of 8 is 13, 3 of 8
is 38. With the defaults (threshold 85, minimum 5): 5 examples all on Mercado apply Mercado (500 >= 425);
4 all on Mercado are pending "Baixa confiança", Mercado, 100; 6 with 5 on Mercado and 1 on Feira are
pending, Mercado, 83 (500 < 510); 7 with 6 and 1 apply Mercado (600 >= 595); 6 with 3 and 3 are pending,
50, suggesting the line of the latest example. `threshold * total` equal to `top * 100` applies.

**Part 2: `classrules.Pair`.** A pending row and the posted row that replaces it are two ids in the ledger.
The collector's own view `pending_posted_candidates` (`internal/ledger/testdata/ledger-schema-v1.sql`)
pairs them only while both are present, on the same account, amount, currency, description and date, and
does not promise one to one; the clean list (`queryCleanTransactions` in `internal/ledger/queries.go`)
hides a pending row that has such a pair. So the moment the bank posts a charge, the pending row the
person may already have categorised leaves the list and a posted row with a new id appears. `Pair` is
the app's own rule for carrying the person's work across; it is not the collector's view.

`Pair` matches a bank-pending transaction of the index (the app's database's record of the transactions
it has seen) that the ledger no longer lists with a posted transaction the index has never seen: same
account, same amount in cents, same establishment key, the posted day from zero to five days after the
pending one (`0 <= posted - pending <= 5`, in calendar days). A match counts only when it is one to one on
both sides: the pending row has exactly one candidate among the posted rows and that posted row has
exactly one candidate among the pending rows. One pending row matching two posted rows pairs neither; two
pending rows matching one posted row pair neither. `Pair` takes the two candidate sets as plain values
(which rows vanished and which are new is the ingest's to select, from the index and the snapshot ({{R2}}))
and answers the matched pairs; a pending row it does not pair stays unpaired. The cents it compares are
the index's amount and the interpreted row's, which the index defines ({{T1}}); compare like with like.
`internal/brday` has `Day`, `ParseDay`, `DayOf`, `MonthOf` and `MonthPeriod` and no difference of days; a
helper may be added there or kept private here.

**Part 3: the nullable suggestion.** In `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts` today:

```
export interface PendingReview {
  reason: string;
  suggestion: string;
  confidence: number;
  justification: string;
}
```

`suggestion` becomes `string | null`, `confidence` `number | null` and `justification` `string | null`,
each with a one-line comment that says when it is null (no suggestion; no confidence without a
suggestion; no justification until the model). `reason` stays a required string. The manifest is
regenerated, and its `PendingReview` definition then allows null for the three. On the Go side,
`pendingReview` in `internal/api/transactions_wire.go` has `Suggestion string`, `Confidence int` and
`Justification string` today; they become pointers, and wherever the transaction reads build it ({{T1}}) a
`tx_state` row whose `pending_line_id` is null answers `"suggestion":null,"confidence":null`, and
`justification` is null on every pending review the server answers. `TransactionDetail.justification`
(`web/src/api/contract/transaction-detail.ts`) is already `string | null` and the Go detail already has
`Justification *string`; neither changes.

**Part 4: the places of the interface.** A pending transaction without a suggestion is a state of each of
these places, each with its test. The state is: `pending` not null, `pending.suggestion` null (and so
`confidence` null). No place may print "null", "undefined" or "null%".

- The line pill, `web/src/components/transactions/BudgetLinePill.vue`: without a line it shows
  `${pending.suggestion}?` for a pending review and "—" otherwise. Without a line and with a pending review
  that has no suggestion, it shows "Pendente". With a line, the line, as today.
- The list's marks, `web/src/components/transactions/marks.ts`: a pending review adds
  `IA ${pending.confidence}%` (tone `warning`). When the pending review has no confidence, the mark is its
  reason, verbatim ("Estabelecimento novo"), with the same tone. A pending review with a suggestion keeps
  today's mark. The bank's own "Pendente" mark for a row not yet posted is unrelated and unchanged.
- The panel's text, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.ts`: `lineLabel` gives `line ??
  pending.suggestion ?? 'Sem linha'`, which already reads "Sem linha" here. `originSentence` gives
  `sugestão da IA, ${confidence}% de confiança` for a pending review; without a confidence it gives the
  reason, verbatim. The movement sentence keeps its precedence.
- The panel's actions, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`: today "Confirmar" and
  "Alterar" appear exactly when `detail.justification !== null`. After this work they appear whenever there
  is something to confirm: a pending review with a suggestion, with or without a justification, or a line
  the model set (`classifiedBy === 'IA'`, as today). They are hidden for a pending review without a
  suggestion; the line button still opens the menu. The justification text shows only when it is not null.
- The queue item, `web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`: today it prints `Sugestão da IA:
  ${suggestion} · ${confidence}%` and, once another line is picked, `A IA tinha sugerido ${suggestion}.
  Confirme para usar a sua escolha.`; its primary button reads "Aceitar", or "Confirmar" once a line is
  picked. Without a suggestion it prints no suggestion, no confidence and no "A IA tinha sugerido"; once a
  line is picked it reads `Linha escolhida: <linha>`, as today; the reason badge shows as today; and
  "Aceitar" is disabled until a line is picked. A disabled control is dimmed as `StepClose.vue` does,
  with the same `token-exempt` comment, or with a token.
- The answer, `web/src/screens/revisao/usePendingAnswer.ts`: `accept` sends `draft.line ??
  pending.suggestion`; with neither it returns without calling `review.acceptPending`. `pickLine` opens the
  menu with that same value as the current one, which may be null. The menu it opens is the one for the
  item's own month, as the work that made every line menu follow its month left it ({{B1}}).

A pending review *with* a suggestion and a null justification (what the rule's "Baixa confiança" will
produce) is also a state: the pill, the marks and the panel's sentence are today's, the panel offers
"Confirmar" and "Alterar" and shows no justification text, and the queue item shows the suggestion line
with no "why" text.

**The stand-in follows the type change and nothing else.** Its dataset keeps its suggestions and
justifications (the parity check measures the prototype's screens built on it, and they must not move).
Where the change breaks a type, the stand-in and the tests follow it with the least change: today
`web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review.test.ts` and
`web/src/screens/revisao/revisao.test.ts` pass `item.pending.suggestion` as an answer's `line`, which must
be a string. The equality test over an empty ledger (`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`) keeps holding.
The screen tests for the new state build it by handing `createFakeApi` a `prototypeState()` in which one
transaction's pending review has `suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification` null, as
`web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts` already hands it a modified state; no inline stub of the backend.

**Privacy and conventions.** Nothing here touches a real ledger; fixtures are invented. Work happens in a
worktree and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a
session, a work item or a plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the
money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant (this work adds none).
Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; the Portuguese quoted above is
exact. A design value in a component comes from a token, or carries a `token-exempt: <reason>` comment.
Any change that touches a screen runs `npm --prefix web run parity` and its output goes in the report.

## Acceptance criteria
`Decide`
- [ ] Each of these is left: an own transfer, a bill payment, an unconverted row, a card credit the rules
mark as a refund. Each holds even when the establishment has a default line the month has and five
examples on one line.
- [ ] A fee charge and a fee discount credit answer nothing to store, also with a default line and
examples.
- [ ] An establishment whose default line the month's budget has is applied that line by rule, whatever
its examples say; a default line the month lacks falls through to the examples.
- [ ] With threshold 85 and minimum 5: 5 of 5 on one line applies it; 4 of 4 is pending "Baixa confiança"
with that line and 100; 5 of 6 is pending with 83; 6 of 7 applies; 3 and 3 is pending with 50 and the line
of the latest example, and when both lines have an example on that latest day, the lower line id.
- [ ] With threshold 50 and minimum 2: 1 of 2 against 1 is pending (no line strictly ahead), and 2 of 3
applies (200 >= 150). With threshold 60 and minimum 5, 3 of 5 against 1 and 1 applies (300 >= 300).
- [ ] Confidence vectors: 2 of 3 is 67, 1 of 3 is 33, 1 of 2 is 50, 5 of 6 is 83, 1 of 8 is 13, 3 of 8 is
38.
- [ ] An example put on its line by a rule, by the model, excluded with a reason, split, or on a line the
transaction's month lacks is not counted; one excluded without a reason is.
- [ ] No examples: a person with no nickname is pending "PIX para pessoa sem apelido" with no suggestion
and no confidence; a person with a nickname and an establishment are pending "Estabelecimento novo" with
no suggestion and no confidence; a received PIX from an unknown person, a credit, gives the first.
- [ ] Shuffling the examples never changes the answer (a property test over generated examples).
`Pair`
- [ ] One pending row and one posted row on the same account, cents and key, posted 0 and 5 days after,
are paired; 6 days after or 1 day before, not; another account, another cent, another key, not.
- [ ] One pending against two posted candidates pairs nothing; two pending against one posted pairs
nothing; with two independent one-to-one matches in one call, both pair; with no candidate, nothing.
- [ ] The answer does not depend on the order of either input.
The contract and the interface
- [ ] `PendingReview.suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification` are nullable in
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`; `npm --prefix web run contract` leaves the manifest unchanged after
the commit; the manifest's `PendingReview` admits null for the three and still requires `reason`.
- [ ] A Go answer carrying a pending review with no suggestion validates against the manifest's result
schema of `transactions.list` and of `transactions.detail` (through the read conformance or a test that
uses the same validator), and marshals as `"suggestion":null,"confidence":null,"justification":null`.
- [ ] Screen tests over a stand-in state with one pending review without a suggestion: the list's pill for
that row reads "Pendente"; its mark is `{ text: 'Estabelecimento novo', tone: 'warning' }` and no mark
contains `%`; the panel's line button reads `Sem linha· Estabelecimento novo▾`, it has no `.confirm` and
no `.justification`; the queue item contains none of "Sugestão da IA", "%" and "A IA tinha sugerido", its
"Aceitar" button is disabled, clicking it leaves `review.acceptPending` uncalled (a spy on the stand-in
records zero calls); after picking "Mercado" it reads "Linha escolhida: Mercado", its button reads
"Confirmar" and is enabled, and accepting sends `line: "Mercado"`.
- [ ] Screen tests over a stand-in state with a pending review that has a suggestion and a null
justification: the panel shows `.confirm` and no `.justification`; the queue item shows the suggestion
with its confidence and no "why" text; accepting sends the suggestion.
- [ ] The existing tests of these places that use the prototype's data pass unchanged, except for the
three type fixes named above; `npm --prefix web run parity` passes with every state as before.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` or `empty/` changes; a file under `full-authored/`
changes only where a pending review's `justification` (and, for a fixture pending without a suggestion,
its `suggestion` and `confidence`) became null.
The guards and the gate
- [ ] A source test fails if a non-test file of `internal/classrules` imports `database/sql`, `os`,
`net/http` or `internal/txrules`; the float and `time.Now` guards inspect at least one file of
`internal/classrules`.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, and the report names the break used for each: the strict
lead check removed (a tie at the top applies); `>=` turned into `>` (the equality case is pending); the
minimum check removed; the tie broken by the higher line id or the earliest day; the confidence truncated
instead of rounded (2 of 3 gives 66); a rule's or the model's example counted; an exclusion without a
reason treated as excluded; a default line applied without checking the month; the refund or the fee
steps placed after step 3; the nickname check dropped from step 5; `Pair` accepting a match that is one
to many; the window made 0 to 4 or allowing a negative gap; the pill, the mark, the panel and the queue
item rendered as before the change (each new screen test fails); the accept guard removed (the spy sees a
call with no line).
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, the table tests cover every outcome of `Decide` and `Pair`
with the ties above, and a queue item without a suggestion sends nothing until a line is chosen.

## Tests
- Table (`internal/classrules`): every step of `Decide` with the vectors above, invented line ids, days
  and keys; the filters of the examples one row each; the tie-break rows.
- Property (`internal/classrules`): over generated examples and settings in their ranges, the answer is
  invariant under shuffling; "apply" never happens below the minimum, without a strict lead or below the
  threshold; every "Baixa confiança" carries a suggestion and a confidence between 1 and 100; the two
  other reasons never carry either.
- Table (`internal/classrules`): `Pair`, one row per case above, with both input orders.
- Unit (`internal/classrules`): the purity guard over the package's sources.
- Unit (`internal/api`): the Go wire type with a null suggestion, validated against the manifest.
- Unit (`web`): `marksOf` in `web/src/components/transactions/transactions.test.ts`; `lineLabel` and
  `originSentence` in `web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.test.ts`.
- Screen test (`web`): the pill in the list, the panel's line section, and the queue item and its answer
  (in the files that test them today: `web/src/components/transaction-panel/transaction-panel.test.ts`,
  `web/src/screens/revisao/weekly.test.ts`, or a new test file beside them), over `createFakeApi` with a
  modified `prototypeState()`.
- Parity: `npm --prefix web run parity`, unchanged.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/classrules/`, `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `internal/contract/contract.json`,
`internal/api/transactions_wire.go`, `web/src/components/transactions/BudgetLinePill.vue`,
`web/src/components/transactions/marks.ts`, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`, `web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/usePendingAnswer.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/review.test.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/revisao.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/transactions/transactions.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/transaction-panel.test.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/weekly.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `internal/txrules/`, `internal/ledger/queries.go`,
`internal/ledger/testdata/ledger-schema-v1.sql`, `internal/brday/`, `internal/money/`,
`internal/api/settings_defaults.go`, `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/transaction-detail.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/`, `web/src/screens/revisao/StepClose.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/PendingQueue.vue`, `web/src/stores/review-view.ts`, `bin/ci`

One new pure package with no caller; one field change in the contract with its generated manifest and its
Go wire type, and the file of the transaction reads that fills it if it is not `transactions_wire.go`;
six interface files, each a small conditional; test files. About eleven code files in three modules, which
is why a split is proposed on the first line. The stand-in's dataset and behaviour are not changed. The
ingest that calls `Decide` and `Pair`, the queue's read and `review.acceptPending` are later work.

title: Read money and whole numbers from JSON into integers with no float
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing the person sees changes with this piece. Today the app only shows amounts; it never receives
one, because every button that changes something is refused. Once the person can type a budget line, a
part of a split purchase or the amount they expect back, the server has to read that number, and this
piece is how: to the cent, exactly as typed, with a fixed rule for a third decimal place and a refusal
for anything that is not an amount. If it were wrong the person would find a line saved one cent off
what they typed, an empty field saved as zero, or a setting rounded the wrong way, and no screen would
say so.

## Outcome
`internal/api` has `ParseReais`, which turns a JSON number into integer cents from its decimal text, and
`ParseWholeNumber`, which turns one into a whole number; the money type `Reais` decodes itself through
the first. Neither touches a float, and the test that forbids floats in the HTTP layer covers the
packages the write side adds. No handler uses them yet.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. Its Go backend answers the API the
interface calls; today it is read-only, and it is about to gain handlers that save what the person
types. Money is held as integer cents (`money.Cents`, an `int64`, in `internal/money`). On the wire an
amount is a JSON number in reais with two decimals (`19.99`, `-65.10`). *The stand-in* is the in-memory
fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on, and the only existing
statement of how writes behave.

**What the code is today (each point checked in the file named).**

- `internal/api/reais.go`: `Reais` is `money.Cents` with a `MarshalJSON` that writes the decimal from
  the integer itself (`decimalOf` works on the magnitude as unsigned so the most negative integer does
  not overflow). There is no way to read an amount: `Reais` has no `UnmarshalJSON`.
- `internal/api/reais_test.go`: `TestMoneyIsWrittenAsADecimalWithTwoPlaces` (a table up to the limits of
  `int64`); `TestAnAbsentFigureIsNullAndNotZero` (a `*Reais` that is nil is written `null`); and
  `TestNoSourceFileOfTheHTTPLayerTouchesAFloat`, which parses every non-test file of `internal/api` and
  fails on the identifiers `float64` and `float32`, on a call named `ParseFloat` or `FromFloat`, and on
  a float literal.
- `internal/money/money.go`: `FromFloat` converts what the ledger hands over (floats read out of JSON),
  rounding half away from zero on the shortest decimal the float prints as, and refuses a magnitude of
  `1e12` or more. That is the boundary with the bank's records and is not used for what a person types.
- `internal/api/arguments.go`: `decodeArgument` decodes one argument strictly (`DisallowUnknownFields`,
  nothing after the value) and answers `badArgumentsError`, which the router turns into `bad_request`.
- `internal/api/percent.go`: `Percent` is a rate the bank states, kept as text with two decimals.
- The stand-in rounds and clamps three settings with `clamp` in `web/src/api/fake/settings-rules.ts`:
  `Math.round`, then the range's minimum and maximum, a non-finite value becoming the minimum.
  `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts` types those three as `number`: `setThreshold(percent)`,
  `setMinExamples(count)` and the manual day of `setClosing(mode, manualDay)`.

**`ParseReais(raw) (money.Cents, error)`.** It turns a JSON number into integer cents from its decimal
text, exponent form included, with no float. It rounds half away from zero beyond two places. It refuses
anything that is not a finite number within one billion reais: the bound is inclusive and is on the
result, 100,000,000,000 cents in magnitude, so exactly one billion reais is accepted, positive or
negative, and one cent more is not. What is not a JSON number is refused: `null`, a string, a boolean,
an array, an object, an empty input, and the spellings JSON does not have (`1.`, `.5`, `+1`, `01`,
`NaN`, `Infinity`). It must not do work proportional to the size of an exponent: `1e999999999` is
refused at once, without building the number, and `0e999999999` is zero.

**`Reais.UnmarshalJSON`.** `Reais` gains `UnmarshalJSON` on top of `ParseReais`, so a budget line's
amount and a split part's amount decode directly inside the struct a handler decodes. It refuses `null`
like everything else that is not a number, so an absent amount can never read as zero; a field that may
be absent is a `*Reais`, which Go leaves nil for `null` without calling the method.

**A negative amount.** An amount that cannot be negative (a budget line, a split part, an expected
reimbursement) is `bad_request` when it is. `ParseReais` itself accepts a negative, because other
amounts can be one; the handler that takes such an amount applies the rule. Those handlers belong to
later slices.

**`ParseWholeNumber(raw) (int, error)`.** It reads the three settings the contract types as `number`. It
rounds to the nearest whole number, a half upward (72.5 becomes 73, -72.5 becomes -72), which is what
the stand-in's `Math.round` gives. It answers an error, which its caller turns into `bad_request`, for a
number beyond one billion in magnitude or not finite, and for anything that is not a JSON number; the
bound is on the result, as it is for money, so one billion itself is accepted. The handler then clamps
to the contract's range, as the stand-in does (for the threshold's 50 to 99, 72.6 becomes 73 and 10
becomes 50); the clamping and the ranges belong to the settings' own slice (finwise-suc: the confidence
threshold, the minimum of examples, the card's label and the closing day), not here. No float, and the
same rule about exponents.

**The rule both parsers serve, binding on every later handler.** All arithmetic is integer cents. Where
the stand-in rounds a float, the port states its rounding in cents, and a table test pins each case
including a negative half. A percentage the server computes (a progress, a fill, a bar, a confidence) is
a whole number rounded half up, as the existing reads already answer them; the stand-in's fractions are
not copied. A rate the bank states, such as a pot's share of the CDI, keeps the two decimals it has
today (`Percent`).

**The float guard widens.** The test that forbids floats covers the new packages too:
`internal/authored` (the package that owns the app's own database, `finwise.db`), `internal/ingest` (the
job that brings a new snapshot of the bank's records into that database) and the three rule packages
`internal/budgetrules`, `internal/classrules` and `internal/subrules`. None of the five may exist when
this lands. The test must already name them, so each is covered from its first file without anyone
editing the test; a directory that is not there yet must not fail the gate, and a present one must not
be skipped. If `internal/authored` arrives with a guard of its own, the overlap is harmless.
`big.Float` is a float too, although the guard's patterns do not see it.

**Why here, and what lost.** A JSON decoder that reads a number into a `float64` and multiplies by a
hundred is right on round figures and wrong on `1.005`, silently; so the amount is read from its text.
`money.FromFloat` is not reused: it starts from a float. The two bounds differ on purpose: what the
ledger hands over is trusted up to `1e12`, what a person types up to one billion.

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. Nothing
in this slice touches a ledger; every amount in its tests is invented, and no value from a real snapshot
(amount, description, name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead
or a pull request.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic,
Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit
message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path, which is this slice's whole
subject. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant (this slice runs none).
Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; a design value in a component
comes from a token (this slice touches no component).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ParseReais` returns, in cents: `0` and `-0` 0; `19.99` 1999; `-65.10` -6510; `8000` 800000;
`0.005` 1; `-0.005` -1; `1.005` 101; `-1.005` -101; `1.0049` 100; `2.675` 268; `0.994999` 99; `1e2`
10000; `1.5e-1` 15; `12E-1` 120; `1e-400` 0; `0e999999999` 0.
- [ ] At the bound, `ParseReais` returns 99999999999 for `999999999.99`, 100000000000 for `1000000000`,
`1000000000.00`, `1e9` and `1000000000.004`, and -100000000000 for `-1000000000`; it refuses
`1000000000.005`, `1000000000.01`, `-1000000000.01`, `1e10`, `1e400` and `1e999999999`.
- [ ] `ParseReais` refuses `"19.99"`, `null`, `true`, `[1]`, `{}`, the empty input, `1.`, `.5`, `+1`,
`01`, `NaN`, `Infinity` and `1 2`.
- [ ] For every amount in a generated range of cents that includes negatives and both bounds,
`ParseReais` of what `Reais` writes is the same amount.
- [ ] A struct field of type `Reais` decodes `19.99` to 1999 and makes the decode fail for `null` and
for `"19.99"`; a field of type `*Reais` is nil for `null`.
- [ ] `ParseWholeNumber` returns 73 for `73`, `72.6`, `72.5` and `7.3e1`; 72 for `72.4`; -72 for
`-72.5`; -73 for `-72.6`; 1 for `0.5`; 0 for `-0.5`, `0.4` and `-0`; 1000000000 for `1000000000` and
`1000000000.4`; -1000000000 for `-1000000000.5`.
- [ ] `ParseWholeNumber` refuses `1000000000.5`, `1000000001`, `-1000000001`, `1e400`, `1e999999999`,
`"73"`, `null`, `true` and the empty input.
- [ ] Neither parser builds the number for an enormous exponent: a test shows that each allocates no
more bytes for `1e999999999` than for `1e400`.
- [ ] The float test fails for a float planted in a non-test file of `internal/api` and of a scratch
directory standing for each of the five packages named above, and passes while those five do not exist.
- [ ] `git diff --stat` against the commit this work started from lists only `internal/api/reais.go`,
`internal/api/reais_test.go` and the new files of `ParseWholeNumber`; no handler is changed.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against its own deliberate break, named in the final
report: the rounding rows against truncation and against rounding half to even; the bound rows against
an exclusive bound; the `null` row against an `UnmarshalJSON` that returns without error; the whole
number's negative half against rounding half away from zero; one row of each table against
`strconv.ParseFloat`, which the float test must catch too.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, every vector above (decimal, exponent, huge, negative half,
out of bound) is a row of a table test, and no non-test file of `internal/api` names a float.

## Tests
- Table (`internal/api`), over the vectors of the criteria: `ParseReais`, accepted and refused, with the
  rows at the bound.
- Property: `ParseReais` over what `Reais.MarshalJSON` writes, for generated cents between the two
  bounds, negatives included.
- Unit: `Reais` and `*Reais` as struct fields decoded with `decodeArgument`.
- Table: `ParseWholeNumber`, accepted and refused, with the halves of both signs and the rows at the
  bound.
- Unit: the bytes each parser allocates on `1e999999999` against `1e400`.
- Source test: the float guard over `internal/api` and the five packages to come, with a test of the
  test over scratch directories.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/reais.go`, `internal/api/reais_test.go`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/arguments.go`, `internal/api/percent.go`, `internal/money/money.go`,
`web/src/api/fake/settings-rules.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`, `bin/ci`

One package and two existing files, plus one new file for `ParseWholeNumber` and its test file. No
