**Known next users, not built here:** the rules that classify new transactions read the threshold and the
minimum (finwise-9gz, finwise-82m); the pots' bucket and linked lines (finwise-7ss: the pots' writes and the reads
that use a pot's bucket) and the establishments and people of the settings overview with their two
writes (finwise-s2k) add to `settings.overview` and to the settings writes beside this work, in files of their
own; the last backup in the overview's data section is another slice's (finwise-72p).

**Left to the implementer** (what makes this bead `spec:open`), each with what constrains it: the
name and shape of the exported closing method in `cardrules`; how `cardView` keeps the bank's
view for the bank day beside the one with the manual day; the names of the new files.

**Privacy and conventions.** Nothing here needs a real ledger. A real ledger is a person's whole financial
history and this repository is public: fixtures are invented, and no value from a real snapshot (an
amount, a description, a name, a document, an id) is ever printed, logged or copied into a file, a
commit, a bead or a pull request. Work in your own git worktree, on your own branch, and stop at local
commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a
plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; a test
already forbids floats in `internal/api` and covers `internal/authored`. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is
English; this work adds no Portuguese. A design value in a component comes from a token; this work
touches no component. Register the four handlers in a registration function of this slice's own file,
listed where write dispatch lists them, so the sibling settings slices add their own files instead of
editing these lines. New files in `internal/api` log nothing: the request log holds the verb, the route,
the status, the duration and the error kind, never an argument, a body or a label.

## Acceptance criteria
The invented ledgers run on a clock fixed at 2026-03-20 unless a criterion says otherwise.

The writes (with `--db`)
- [ ] `settings.setThreshold` with 10, 100, 72.6, 72.5, 72.4 and 1000 makes `settings.overview` answer
`categorization.threshold` 50, 99, 73, 73, 72 and 99; with `"73"`, `null` and `2e9` it answers 400
`bad_request` and the canonical dump is unchanged.
- [ ] `settings.setMinExamples` with 0, 80 and 12 makes the overview answer `minExamples` 1, 50 and 12.
- [ ] `settings.setClosing("manual", 31)` makes the overview answer `closing` `{"mode":"manual",
"bankDay":28,"manualDay":28}` over the full invented ledger; `setClosing("manual", 0)` answers
`manualDay` 1; `setClosing("auto", 12)` answers `{"mode":"auto","bankDay":28,"manualDay":12}`;
`setClosing("weekly", 10)` answers 400 `bad_request`.
- [ ] After `setClosing("manual", 10)` and `changes.undo` of its change, the overview answers
`{"mode":"auto","bankDay":28,"manualDay":28}` and the canonical dump is the one taken before.
- [ ] `settings.setCardLabel("  Virtual ")` makes the overview answer `"cardLabel":"Virtual"`;
`setCardLabel("   ")` answers `""`; undoing the first, on a database with nothing else set, answers
`"Físico"`.
- [ ] Each of the four answers 200 `{"changeId":"<decimal id>"}` that validates against the manifest, is
one change with author `person` and its own qualified method name, has effects on `settings` only, and
undoing it returns the canonical dump of every journaled table to the one taken before; none of the four
remains in `writesWithoutHandler`.
- [ ] `setThreshold(73)` after `setThreshold(72.6)`, and `setClosing` with the stored mode and day, each
answer a change id whose change has no row in `change_effects`; its `changes.undo` succeeds and changes
nothing.
- [ ] With the snapshot file missing, each of the four succeeds and its effect is stored.
- [ ] On a server without the app's database the four answer 403 `read_only` before their body is read,
and `settings.overview`, `card.overview`, `home.summary` and `review.closing` answer byte for byte what
they answered before; the existing tests of `settings_test.go`, `card_test.go`, `home_test.go` and
`review_closing_test.go` pass unchanged.

The card
- [ ] Over `noTableLedger` (a bank with no closing table and bill `bill-it` due 2026-03-25 with no closing
date) in mode `auto`, `card.overview` answers `closesOn`, `dueOn`, `bestPurchaseDay` and
`payAhead.amount` null, as today; after `setClosing("manual", 22)` it answers `closesOn` and
`bestPurchaseDay` `"2026-03-22"`, `dueOn` `"2026-03-25"` and `payAhead.amount` `0.00`, while
`settings.overview` answers `bankDay` null.
- [ ] Over `c6Ledger` at 2026-03-20, after `setClosing("manual", 25)`: the past bill `bill-jan`, whose
closing date the ledger carries, keeps `closedOn` `"2026-02-04"`; `bill-feb`, which the ledger gives no
closing date, has `closedOn` `"2026-02-25"` (it is `"2026-03-04"` by the bank's table in mode `auto`);
the open bill has `closesOn` `"2026-03-25"` and `dueOn` `"2026-04-10"`; `settings.overview` still answers
`bankDay` 3.
- [ ] Over the full invented ledger, whose open bill `bill-mar` carries the closing date 2026-03-28,
`setClosing("manual", 10)` leaves `card.overview`'s `closesOn` `"2026-03-28"` and the whole answer of
`card.overview` byte for byte as in mode `auto`, and `bankDay` 28.
- [ ] Over a ledger built for the test with card purchases on and after a manual closing day of the
current month, of a bank with no closing table and with no closing date in the ledger,
`home.summary`'s `payAhead.amount` and the amount of `review.closing`'s `cardBill` equal
`card.overview`'s `payAhead.amount` in mode `manual`, and in mode `auto` over the same ledger
`home.summary`'s `payAhead` and `review.closing`'s `cardBill` are null.
- [ ] No non-test file of `internal/api` calls `Table.ClosingDate` after this work (a source check or a
test), and `cycle.go`'s comment on `ManualClosingDay` is unchanged.

Calibration and the rules' inputs
- [ ] Over the full invented ledger, with an authored state that sets every one of the five settings,
`categorization.calibration` is exactly the five bands 50–59, 60–69, 70–79, 80–89, 90–100 with
`correctionPercent` null, and `suggestedThreshold` is null.
- [ ] Over the full invented ledger with nothing stored, and on a server without `--db`,
`settings.overview` answers threshold 85, minimum 5, `"cardLabel":"Físico"`, mode `auto` and manual day
28, and `internal/api` states none of these five values in a constant of its own.

The harness and the gate
- [ ] The write conformance harness has a recorded-change case for each of the four writes, with its
golden effects file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`.
- [ ] `authoredReadCases` holds `settings.overview` over an authored state that sets all five settings to
values other than the defaults, with its golden file under
`internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`, not written in the shape the interface's equality test
scans for.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` or `empty/` changes, and
`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts` passes untouched.
- [ ] The test that proves no handler logs what it reads passes over the new write cases, with the card
labels of those cases among the strings it looks for, and fails when a handler of this slice is made to
log its argument.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against a deliberate break named in the final report:
the clamp removed from each of the three numeric writes; rounding half to even instead of half up;
`setClosing` storing only the mode; the label stored untrimmed; `closingOf` left calling the table
directly (the `noTableLedger` and `c6Ledger` criteria fail); the manual day applied over a date the
ledger carries (`bill-jan` moves); the bank day computed with the manual day (`bankDay` moves); the manual
day passed in mode `auto`; the clamp bypassed so that an out-of-range value reaches the store (the
database's `CHECK` refuses it and the write answers `internal`, which the clamping criteria catch).
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, the four writes are out of `writesWithoutHandler`, a
setting changed over HTTP on a server started with `--db` is answered by `settings.overview` after the
process restarts, and the `noTableLedger`, `c6Ledger` and full-ledger card criteria pass.

## Tests
- Table (`internal/api`, the handlers below the router): each write's parsing and clamping over the rows
  of the criteria, halves of both signs included, and the refusals of what is not a number or is beyond
  the bound.
- Conformance, recorded-change mode, over the full invented ledger of `internal/api/fixtures_test.go` and
  an authored state built with `authoredtest`: one case per write, effects golden under
  `testdata/golden/writes/`, the harness's undo check; an empty-change case for the threshold and for the
  closing.
- Unit (`internal/cardrules`, `closing_test.go` or a new test file there): the exported closing method
  answers the manual date when a manual day is set, the table's date when not, and nothing for a bank with
  no table and no manual day; `PlacePurchase` and the new method agree on every cycle of a card with one
  dated and one undated bill.
- Unit (`internal/api/card_test.go`, over `noTableLedger`, `c6Ledger`, the full invented ledger and a
  ledger built for the test with `addCardPurchase`): the card criteria, in both modes; the pay-ahead of
  `home.summary` and the card bill of `review.closing` against `card.overview`.
- Unit (`internal/api/settings_test.go`): the bank day with each mode and manual day over the three
  fixtures; calibration over an authored state; the defaults over the empty authored view.
- Golden: the authored read case of `settings.overview` in `testdata/golden/full-authored/`; `full/` and
  `empty/` unchanged.
- Integration with `httptest` over a router built on both stores: `bad_request` for what the manifest's
  schema refuses (a mode outside the enum, a string for a number); `read_only` without the database; a
  setting answered after the database is closed and opened again.
- Unit: the no-leak test over the new write cases, with a handler that logs.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/settings_writes.go`, `internal/api/settings.go`,
`internal/api/settings_defaults.go`, `internal/api/card.go`, `internal/api/home.go`,
`internal/api/review_closing.go`, `internal/cardrules/cycle.go`, `internal/cardrules/closing_test.go`,
`internal/api/settings_test.go`, `internal/api/settings_writes_test.go`, `internal/api/card_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`
**Reads only:** `internal/authored/`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/`, `internal/api/whole_number.go`,
`internal/api/arguments.go`, `web/src/api/fake/settings.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/settings-rules.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/settings.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/card-rules.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/card.ts`, `web/src/screens/config/`, `internal/contract/contract.json`,
`internal/cardrules/closing.go`, `internal/cardrules/placement.go`, `internal/cardrules/nextbill.go`,
`internal/api/messages.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/`,
`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`, `bin/ci`

In `internal/api`, one new file for the four write handlers, the overview reading the stored values,
`settings_defaults.go` giving up its own copies of the defaults, and `card.go` brought under the card
rule; one exported method in `cardrules/cycle.go` with its test. `home.go` and `review_closing.go` are
edited only if `loadCard` does not already receive the request's authored view when this starts, and then
by one argument at the call. About seven code files in two packages. The store is read, not edited: it
was built before (finwise-11u). No migration. Nothing under `web/` changes: the interface already sends these
writes and refetches after each, and the stand-in is read as the statement of the behaviour. The label
is `critical` because the closing decides which purchases the pay-ahead figure adds, and a wrong one is
wrong about money in silence.
close_reason: settings.setThreshold, setMinExamples, setCardLabel and setClosing have handlers: a number rounded half upward and held to its range, the label trimmed as the interface trims, the closing mode and day as one change, a write of the stored value an empty change; none reads the ledger. The settings, the card, the home and the closing view answer what is stored; in manual mode the person's day places only the bills the ledger gives no closing date, and the bank's day keeps showing as it is. No golden file of full/ or empty/ changed. bin/ci green on the branch merged with main. Review: four independent mutations, all failing tests. The implementer's twenty-one breaks each failed a test; it also resolved the conflict with the budget store and ran the built binary over a scratch database.

title: Check the write side over a real ledger with a scripted series of writes on a scratch database, saying counts and fixed sentences only
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing on screen changes with this piece. Everything the app does when the person changes something (a
category, a split, a reimbursement, a budget, a closed month) has been proved on invented data only, and
a real history has shapes no invented one has: purchases the bank still reports as pending, purchases
abroad, taxes folded under their purchase, fifteen months of one person's habits. After this lands, one
command run on the person's own machine, against their real history and a throwaway copy of the app's
database, says whether every total still adds up after each kind of change and whether taking all of it
back leaves the database exactly as it was. It says so without ever showing an amount, a name or an id.
If this piece were wrong the person would notice in one of two ways: months later, as a total that
silently lost a split purchase or an undo that left a tag behind; or at once, as their own transactions
printed into a terminal, a log or a pull request.

## Outcome
`internal/api` has an opt-in test of the write side over a real ledger. It runs only when
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file, opens that snapshot read-only, creates a scratch `finwise.db` in
the test's temporary directory, and checks: the two invariants of the budget's dispositions in every
month of the ledger, before and after a scripted series of writes on transactions picked by position;
what the ingest counted; that every write of the series that is a recorded change can be undone, and that
once all are undone the journaled tables are exactly as they were before the series; and, apart, that
the index of transactions only grew. Every comparison happens in memory. On success it logs counts; on
failure it says fixed sentences. The same series and the same checks run in every `go test` over the
invented ledger, where each check is also shown to fail.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, and no code here ever writes
to it. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, owned by the package `internal/authored`, where everything
the person authors is kept; the server has one only when started with `--db` (finwise-9h2: the database, its
recognition and its migrations). *The manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, the generated
description of the API's 82 methods; 55 are of class `write` and one, `budget.evaluateScenario`, of class
`evaluate`. *The recorder* is the layer of `internal/authored` through which every change to the app's
database is written, and *the journal* is what it writes: one row in `changes` per change (author,
method, instant, Brazil day, whether it was extended or undone) and one row in `change_effects` per
effect (finwise-wi4: the recorder, the journal and undo). A *journaled table* is one the recorder knows from
its closed registry. The tables that are deliberately not journaled are `changes`, `change_effects`,
`schema_migrations`, `meta`, `tx_index`, `tx_ids`, `lines` and `pin`. *Undo* (`changes.undo(changeId)`)
is the inverse of a change's recorded effects: it restores every `before` and marks the change undone;
it is refused with the error kind `refused` and the reason `stale_change`, changing nothing, when the
change is unknown or already undone or when a later change still in force has an effect on any unit the
change touched; undo is not itself undoable. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under
`web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it plays no part here. *A listed transaction* is
one the API lists: the collector's clean list after the transaction rules (`internal/txrules`) folded tax
rows under their purchases and took the movements of savings pots out.

**The index.** `tx_index(tx_key, account_id, day, cents, establishment_key, bank_pending, first_run,
last_run, evaluated)` and `tx_ids(provider_id, tx_key)` are what the app's database remembers about the
transactions it has evaluated or the person has touched (finwise-jw2: the transactions' tables, the index and
the dispositions). A transaction's key, `tx_key`, is minted by the app's database; `tx_ids` maps every
provider id seen to it. The two tables record observations, not decisions, so they are not journaled: a
write creates or refreshes the index row of each transaction it names, and an undo does not remove it.
No amount shown or summed ever comes from the index.

**What "pending" means.** One definition serves the queue, every count and the closing of a month: a
transaction is pending when it is pending in the app's database, the ledger lists it now, and its month's
budget has at least one line.

**What exists today (each point checked in the file named).**

- Opt-in tests over a real snapshot already exist for the read side, in `internal/ledger`,
  `internal/txrules`, `internal/cardrules`, `internal/potrules` and, in `internal/api`,
  `realsnapshot_test.go`, `realsnapshot_money_test.go`, `fresh_install_realsnapshot_test.go`,
  `pots_yield_realsnapshot_test.go` and `pots_yield_months_realsnapshot_test.go`. None of them writes
  anything.
- `internal/api/golden_test.go` holds `snapshotVariable` (`"FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT"`) and
  `goldenUpdateRefusal`, which refuses `-update` while the variable is set so that a real ledger cannot
  reach a committed file.
- `internal/api/realsnapshot_test.go` holds the helpers this test starts from. `realSnapshotPath` skips
  the test when the variable is unset. `withoutValues` fails a step with the step's name and the error's
  Go type, never its text, because the text of an error can carry a row id. `realRun.answer` calls a read
  through the router with a session open, requires 200, counts the answer, and reports a body that does
  not conform to its result schema with the words "the message is withheld", because a schema error can
  quote the value it rejected. `answerSomeDetails` picks the first, the middle and the last id of a
  month's list: that is what "picked by position" means in this repository. Its file comment states the
  rule the read side follows: no value from the snapshot, "an amount, a description, a name, a document,
  an id, a month", may reach a log or a failure message; a label this package wrote itself is not a value
  from the snapshot.
- `internal/api/realsnapshot_money_test.go` shows the house pattern for an opt-in check that CI never
  runs: the counting it relies on is exercised a second time over invented data
  (`TestTheCardCountsSeparateABillFromAPurchase`), so that it is known to be able to count and to fail.
- `internal/api/harness_test.go` builds the router for a test: `withLedger(path, now)` gives it a ledger
  reader and a fixed clock; `newTestEnv` gives it a log buffer, so the request log of a test goes to
  memory and not to the terminal. Note that `newTestEnv` fails with `t.Fatalf("NewHandler: %v", err)`,
  which prints an error's text.
- `internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`: `TestNoHandlerLogsWhatItReads` runs every read case over the
  two invented ledgers and fails if any log holds one of a list of strings only the fixtures and the
  arguments hold (`tx-`, `acc-`, `card-itau`, `LIVRARIA`, `EXEMPLO`, `Exemplo`, `2026-02`, `no-such`,
  `12345678`).

**What this test stands on, delivered by earlier work.** The write conformance harness (finwise-fst: the
harness for writes, the package `internal/authored/authoredtest` that builds invented states of the app's
database, and the canonical dump) gives three things this test reuses: a way to build a migrated
`finwise.db` in a temporary directory from a clock handed in; *the canonical dump*, a deterministic text
of the content of every journaled table, taken from the recorder's registry, equal bytes for equal
states; and its checks by mode, each a function that names what is wrong. Those checks were written for
invented data and may quote what they compared. Over a real ledger they are used for their verdict only
and their text is withheld, as `realRun.answer` withholds a conformance problem.

**The dispositions and the two invariants.** `budgetrules.Dispose` (finwise-305) puts every listed transaction
in exactly one disposition and says what it adds to which budget line. Amounts are magnitudes in integer
cents. The first condition that matches wins:

| # | disposition | condition | counts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | unconverted | the ledger has no value in reais for it | nothing |
| 2 | movement | a movement between own accounts or a bill payment | nothing |
| 3 | excluded | excluded with a reason | nothing |
| 4 | waiting | pending review | nothing |
| 5 | split | a debit with two or more parts | each part with a line adds its amount to that line; the rest (the amount less those parts, which is negative when they exceed it) is unassigned |
| 6 | fee | a fee row, charge or discount, that is on no line (as the existing fees rule defines it: posted) or that the person put on the fees line | a charge adds to the fees line; the credit that discounts it takes off |
| 7 | reimbursement | a credit linked to a purchase | no line; the smaller of its amount and the purchase's is applied inside the purchase, and any excess counts nowhere |
| 8 | refund | a credit that is a refund | reduces its refund line by its amount; with no refund line, nothing |
| 9 | income | a credit on a line of the income group | received on that line |
| 10 | other credit | any other credit | nothing |
| 11 | on a line | a debit with a line | its amount less the applied reimbursement |
| 12 | uncategorised | a debit with no line | nothing; its amount less the applied reimbursement is unassigned |

A row the bank still reports as pending is listed and counts like any other; the existing fees rule keeps
counting only posted fee rows. An exclusion takes effect only once it has a reason: switched on without
one, the transaction keeps counting. What a linked credit takes off its purchase is the smaller of the
two amounts, so a purchase's effective amount never changes sign.

Two invariants guard the totals, and this test checks both in every month the ledger holds, by Brazil
month:

1. For every debit of dispositions 5, 11 and 12: what it adds to lines, plus what is unassigned, plus the
   applied reimbursement, equals its amount.
2. Every listed transaction is in exactly one disposition, so the dispositions' counts add up to the
   number of transactions the API lists for the month and their amounts to the sum of the listed
   magnitudes.

Both are already a property test over generated transactions in `internal/budgetrules`. What is new here
is the real composition: the dispositions come from the same function the API uses to dispose a month
(the one that joins the ledger's rows with the authored rows and calls `Dispose`), and the number and the
sum they are held against come from another path, the answer of `transactions.list` for that month
through the router. Amounts read from an answer are turned into cents by `ParseReais` (finwise-po6: the
parser that reads a JSON number into integer cents from its decimal text), never through a float. For
what the magnitude of an unconverted row is, follow the definition the property test of `budgetrules`
uses.

**The ingest and its counts.** `ingest.Run` (finwise-82m: the one function that brings the app's database up
to date with a snapshot) refreshes the index, pairs a vanished bank-pending row with the posted row that
replaced it, and, for every listed transaction dated on or after the *tracking start month* that was
never evaluated and whose month's budget has at least one line, indexes it, marks it evaluated and
applies the rules once: leave it, apply a line by rule, or make it pending with one of three reasons,
"Baixa confiança", "PIX para pessoa sem apelido" or "Estabelecimento novo". The tracking start month is
the Brazil month in which the app's database was created, set once from the injected clock at creation
and never again; earlier transactions are never put in the queue. A transaction whose month has no
budget stays unevaluated. A budget save calls the ingest after its own commit and before it answers. An
evaluated transaction is never evaluated again. If anything authored changed, the run records one change
whose author is `rule`; with nothing to record, no change is written. It returns counts only: indexed,
paired, unpaired, applied by rule, and pending per reason.

On a database created by this test, where nobody has yet put any transaction on a line, the rules leave
no room for some outcomes, and the test asserts exactly these consequences:

- Before any budget exists, a run evaluates nothing: applied by rule is 0 and pending is 0 for every
  reason.
- After the first budget is saved, applied by rule is 0, because a line is applied by rule only from an
  establishment's default line or from examples the person made, and there are none; "Baixa confiança"
  is 0 and no pending transaction carries a suggestion, for the same reason; paired and unpaired are 0,
  because pairing needs an index row from an earlier run.
- The pending counts of the run add up to the pending count `shell.overview` answers and to the number of
  items in the queue of `review.weekly`.
- No item of the queue is dated before the tracking start month.
- A second run right after changes nothing: no row is added to `changes`, the canonical dump is equal,
  and no index row appeared.

**The clock.** The server's clock is injected, never the host's, so that a snapshot copied days ago gives
the same run. "Today" is an instant in the Brazil month of the ledger's latest listed transaction, so the
current month has rows to act on; the scratch database is created at that same instant, so its tracking
start month is the current month, which is the state of the person's first day with the write side. The
month is taken from the ledger in memory and never printed.

**The series.** It is a fixed table of steps in the test's own file. A step names a method, how its
target is picked, and its arguments.

- *Targets are picked by position.* A step takes its transaction, pot, subscription or queue item from a
  list the API answers (the first, the middle or the last of a month's `transactions.list`, the first
  item of the queue, the first pot of the list), as `answerSomeDetails` does. No step searches for a
  name, an amount or an id, so no value of a real ledger is ever in the source.
- *Arguments are the test's own.* Line names, a tag, a note, a nickname, a reason and a scenario's name
  are invented constants of the test; amounts are constants or halves of what the answer just gave,
  computed in cents.
- *Setup, before the series.* The test saves a first budget for the current month through `budget.save`
  with invented lines in the five editable groups (income, fixed, variable, provisions, reserves), so
  that every later step has a line to name and the ingest has a budget to evaluate against. The state
  after this save and its ingest is the series' starting point.
- *Coverage.* The series performs every write whose conformance mode is a recorded change and that has a
  handler when this work is done. There are 47 such methods in the contract: the 24 writes of
  `transactions`; `budget.save`, `budget.saveScenario` and `budget.applyScenario`; `subscriptions.create`,
  `setStatus`, `setLine`, `setReviewDate` and `setNote`; `review.acceptPending`, `dismissWarning`,
  `markStepDone`, `keepSubscription`, `cancelSubscription`, `closeMonth` and `markTransferDone`; and the
  eight writes of `settings`. Among them, `transactions.applyLineToEstablishment` is the extension of an
  earlier change (it appends its effects to the `setLine` change it started from and answers the same id,
  so one undo takes back both) and `transactions.undoHistoryStep` is a recorded change that takes one
  step of a transaction's history back.
- *The other modes, once each.* A write that answers null (the same line set again on a transaction, and
  each of the six methods that answer only null until the thing they act on has a producer:
  `subscriptions.acceptSuggestion`, `subscriptions.rejectSuggestion`, `review.approve`, `review.refuse`,
  `review.propose`, `review.runWarningAction`) adds no row to the journal. The evaluation,
  `budget.evaluateScenario`, changes no table at all. `changes.undo` and `session.changePin` are not
  steps: the first is how the series is taken back, and the second is not a recorded change and has its
  own tests.
- *Three of the 47 may not exist yet.* The work this depends on guarantees handlers for 44 of them. Not
  guaranteed are `review.dismissWarning` (finwise-24r: the warnings derived from subscriptions and their
  dismissal) and `settings.setNickname` and `settings.setDefaultLine` (finwise-s2k: the establishments and
  people of the settings overview and the two settings writes by key). A step exists for each of the 47;
  the three are in a named list of steps allowed to find no handler. A test that needs no snapshot holds
  the table against the registered handlers: a registered recorded-change write with no step fails it,
  and so does a name in that list whose handler exists. Its message says, in one sentence, which method
  needs a step and in which file, so that whoever adds a write later can act on it without this bead.
- *A step with no target is skipped and counted.* A real ledger may have no received PIX to link as a
  reimbursement, no pot with a stable identity, no card purchase in the current month, no warning to
  dismiss, or a single month, so that no month can be closed. Such a step is counted under a fixed label
  and is never a silent pass; a snapshot that lists no transaction at all fails the test with a fixed
  sentence. A write the server refuses with a reason (`refused`) where the step expected a change is a
  failure, reported by the method's name, the status and the reason, which are all from closed lists.

**The order of the run.**

1. Skip unless `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set. Create the scratch database. Run the ingest and assert
   the counts of a database with no budget. Check the two invariants in every month.
2. Setup: save the first budget. Assert the counts of the ingest that followed it. Take the canonical
   dump and the keys of the index: the starting point.
3. Perform the series. After each recorded change, nothing is compared yet; the change's id is kept.
4. With every change of the series in force, check the two invariants in every month again. This is the
   state that matters: splits, linked reimbursements, exclusions with and without a reason, refunds and
   a closed month are all present at once.
5. Assert that the journal gained no change authored by `rule` during the series: every tracked
   transaction was evaluated in step 2, and the rules run once per transaction.
6. Undo every change of the series, newest first. Each undo must succeed: in that order no later change
   still in force stands in the way, so a `stale_change` here is a defect.
7. Take the canonical dump again and compare it with the starting point, in memory, byte for byte.
8. Apart, check the index: every `tx_key` and every provider id present at the starting point is still
   present, and neither table lost a row. Their content may have been refreshed; their rows only grow.

**What may be printed.** The repository's rule, in full: the repository is public and a real ledger is a
person's whole financial history. A real snapshot may be opened read-only. No value from it (amount,
description, name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull
request. A count may be shown to the person running the test and goes into no file: not the pull request
body, not a commit message, not a bead. The test runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file.
Fixtures are invented. This repository also treats a month and a day as values.

For this test that means, on success and on failure alike:

- A message is built only from constants of the test (the number and the method of a step, the name of a
  check, a fixed label), counts, HTTP statuses, error kinds and refusal reasons (both closed lists), the
  names of journaled tables (they come from the recorder's registry, not from the ledger) and the Go type
  of an error. Never the text of an error, a response body, a row, a struct that holds ledger data, a
  diff, an SQL statement's parameter, a month, a day, an id, a key or a tag.
- Dumps and index keys are compared in memory. Nothing of this run is written under `testdata/` or
  anywhere else; no helper that prints a diff on mismatch, or that rewrites a golden file, is called.
- An establishment key (the identity of an establishment or a person, with the prefix `doc:`, `name:` or
  `text:`) can be a document number. It is held in memory like an id and never printed.
- The scratch database holds real values from the moment the ingest runs: the index carries account ids,
  days, amounts and establishment keys. It lives only in `t.TempDir()`, which Go removes when the test
  ends, pass or fail. If the test binary is killed, that directory survives under the system's temporary
  directory: the test's file comment says so, so the person knows what to delete.
- Helpers shared with the fixture tests may print an error's text (`newTestEnv` does). Every call that
  can fail on real data goes through a wrapper that withholds the text, as `withoutValues` does.

**What is left to the implementer, and what constrains it** (this is why the bead is `spec:open`).

- *The steps themselves*: which position each takes, in which order, and the invented arguments, under
  the rules of "The series" above. The order must let every step that can have a target have one (a
  purchase is marked reimbursable before a credit is linked to it; a purchase that will be split is not
  the one that gets a reimbursement, because a split purchase cannot have a linked reimbursement and the
  server refuses it with `split_with_reimbursement`; a subscription is created before its status is set).
- *How the index and the journal's authors are read.* Every SQL statement over the app's database is a
  registered constant of `internal/authored`, so the test carries no SQL of its own. If the functions the
  package and `authoredtest` already expose do not answer "which keys does the index hold" and "which
  authors does the journal hold since this change", the smallest addition goes in `authoredtest`.
- *How the files are divided.* The step table, the checks and the two tests may be one file or three,
  beside the existing real-snapshot tests.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic,
Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit
message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path, in a test included. Every SQL
statement over the app's database is a registered constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and
everything else is English; a design value in a component comes from a token (this work touches no
component).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Without `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT`, `go test ./internal/api -run RealSnapshot -v` reports the new
opt-in test as skipped, and `bin/ci` neither runs it nor needs a snapshot.
- [ ] The same series and the same checks run in an always-on test over the full invented ledger of
`internal/api/fixtures_test.go` and a scratch database built by `authoredtest`, and pass: every step
that can have a target there has one, and the count of steps skipped for lack of a target is asserted
as an exact number.
- [ ] The series' table holds a step for each of the 47 recorded-change writes named in the Context; a
test that needs no snapshot fails when a registered recorded-change write has no step, and when a method
in the list of steps allowed to find no handler has one. The list holds at most `review.dismissWarning`,
`settings.setNickname` and `settings.setDefaultLine`.
- [ ] Each of the six null-only methods and one same-line `transactions.setLine` is called once, answers
`null`, and adds no row to `changes`; `budget.evaluateScenario` is called once and changes no table.
- [ ] The two invariants are checked in every month of the ledger at two moments: on the fresh database
and with every change of the series in force. The count and the sum of invariant 2 come from the
answer of `transactions.list`, parsed with `ParseReais`.
- [ ] The ingest's counts are asserted as the Context lists them: all zero before a budget exists; after
the first save, applied by rule 0, "Baixa confiança" 0, paired 0, unpaired 0, no suggestion on any
pending transaction; pending per reason adding up to the pending count of `shell.overview` and to the
length of the queue of `review.weekly`; no queue item before the tracking start month; a second run
adding no row to `changes` and leaving the dump and the index as they were.
- [ ] The journal gains no change authored by `rule` between the first and the last step of the series.
- [ ] Every change the series recorded is undone newest first and each undo answers 200; afterwards the
canonical dump of every journaled table equals, byte for byte, the dump taken before the first step.
- [ ] Every `tx_key` and every provider id the index held before the first step is still there after the
last undo, and neither `tx_index` nor `tx_ids` has fewer rows.
- [ ] Each check is a function that returns what is wrong, and an always-on test feeds each its own
break and requires a complaint: one change left out of the undos; one transaction dropped from a
month's dispositions; one split part left out of a debit's sum; one key removed from the index; one
pending count off by one; one change by `rule` added during the series.
- [ ] An always-on test collects every message the checks produce under those breaks over the invented
ledger and fails if any of them contains a string only the fixtures or the series' arguments hold: the
strings of `TestNoHandlerLogsWhatItReads` plus each invented argument of the series.
- [ ] `command grep -n "t.Log\|t.Error\|t.Fatal\|Sprintf\|Errorf" ` over the new files shows no format
verb fed by an error's text, a body, a row, a month, a day, an id or a key: only constants, counts,
statuses, kinds, reasons, table names and `%T`.
- [ ] The final report lists every message the new files can produce, with its format string, in one
place, and the failure path is read by the review, not only by the implementer.
- [ ] The new files write nothing to disk outside `t.TempDir()`, and `git status` after a run with the
variable set shows no new or changed file.
- [ ] The opt-in run over a real snapshot passes. It is made by whoever holds a snapshot (the review, on
the person's machine); the pull request body states that it passed and repeats none of its counts.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against its own deliberate break, named in the final
report: the six breaks above for the checks; a step removed from the table for the coverage test; a
handler registered for a method of the allowed list for the same test; an invented argument printed by
a check for the no-value test.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, the always-on test passes over the invented ledger with
every check shown to fail, and the opt-in run over a real snapshot passes with its output read by the
review and found to hold counts and fixed sentences only.

## Tests
- Integration, opt-in (`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT`), over a real snapshot opened read-only and a scratch
  `finwise.db` in the test's temporary directory: the order of the run in the Context, steps 1 to 8.
- Integration, always on, over the full invented ledger of `fixtures_test.go` and a database built by
  `authoredtest`: the same series and the same checks, with the exact number of steps skipped.
- Unit, in the pattern of `TestTheConformanceCheckRejectsAnAnswerThatDoesNotMatch`: each check fed its
  broken input (an undo left out, a disposition dropped, a split part left out, an index key removed, a
  pending count off by one, a change by `rule` added).
- Unit: the coverage of the step table against the registered recorded-change writes, with a test of the
  test, in the pattern of `TestTheCoverageCheckFailsWhenAHandlerIsMissingOrInvented`.
- Unit: no message of the checks holds a fixture's or an argument's string, over the messages produced
  under the breaks.
- Manual, by the review: the output of one opt-in run and the source of every message, read for values.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/realsnapshot_writes_test.go`, `internal/api/realsnapshot_writes_series_test.go`,
`internal/api/realsnapshot_writes_checks_test.go`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/realsnapshot_test.go`, `internal/api/realsnapshot_money_test.go`,
`internal/api/golden_test.go`, `internal/api/harness_test.go`, `internal/api/helpers_test.go`,
`internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`, `internal/api/fixtures_test.go`, `internal/authored/`,
`internal/budgetrules/`, `internal/ingest/`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `bin/ci`

Test code only: up to three new test files in `internal/api` (one if they read better together; the
names are the implementer's and end in `_test.go`) and, only if a read of the index or of the journal's
authors is missing, one small addition to the test-support package `internal/authored/authoredtest`. No
production file changes, no golden file is written, and the existing real-snapshot tests are read, not
edited: their helpers are in the same package and are called as they are. The collector's snapshot is
opened read-only and nothing is created beside it.

It is labelled critical although it changes no production code: it is the one place where real financial
data meets code that writes, and its mistake would be silent in both directions, a check that cannot
fail or a message that carries a value.
close_reason: An opt-in test runs a scripted series of every recorded write over a real ledger and a scratch database, checking the invariants of each month's dispositions, the ingest's counts, every change undone, the journaled tables as before and the index only grown, in counts and fixed sentences; the same series runs over the invented ledger in every go test. Verified: gate green on the branch merged with main; each check shown to fail against a break of its own; three defects planted in production code in review, each failing the series; the real run made once in review and passed.

title: Add a command-line interface for agents and the approval flow for the changes they or the model propose
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the person is the only one who changes anything in the app, through the screens, and the buttons that
exist for a change somebody else proposes (approve, refuse) do nothing: the approvals the screen is built to
show never arrive, because nothing is able to propose. After this lands the person can let an agent (an
assistant working for them in a terminal) read and change their finance data through a command, within
limits they set, and everything the agent proposes that needs a yes shows up in the app waiting for their
answer, with the reason, and can be taken back like any other change. If it were wrong the person would
find out as a change to their budget or to their transactions made by something that was never allowed to
make it, or as a request for approval that does nothing when they answer.

## Outcome
This is a tracking bead. It holds the subject so it is not lost and tells whoever picks it up what was
decided, why it waits, what it will need from the write side and what must be decided first. It is not
ready to implement. It is finished when the open decisions below are answered by the person, written into
this bead, and the implementation beads exist, each written whole and depending on the write side being
complete.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The app's database* (`finwise.db`,
created by `finwise serve --db`) holds everything the person authors. *The journal* is the record that
database keeps of every change (author, method, instant, effects), which is what makes a change undoable.
*A handler* is the function that answers one method of the API; the API's methods are listed in the
manifest `internal/contract/contract.json`, 82 of them, 56 of which change something (class `write` or
`evaluate`). *The approval flow* is the contract's `review.propose`, `review.approve` and `review.refuse`:
something proposes a change, the person sees it as an `ApprovalRequest` (`id`, `title`, `reason`: "a change
the model proposed that waits for a yes or a no") and answers yes or no. *The stand-in* is the in-memory
fake backend of the design prototype (`web/src/api/fake/`); it shows approvals as seeded data.

**What was decided.** The command-line interface and the approval flow are not part of the write side:
their shape and an agent's limits are a plan of their own. The write side makes the three methods exist and
answer null (nothing produces a proposal until the model or the command-line interface does), which the
interface already treats as "nothing happened". The monthly report's paragraphs can carry a `proposalId` and
a `sent` flag ("the suggested change is already waiting for approval"); nothing sets them yet.

**What the write side leaves ready for it:**

- *The handlers are meant to be callable outside HTTP.* Each write is a function over a recorder that
  already holds one transaction and the facts of the change (author, method, instant, Brazil day); HTTP is
  one caller of it. A command can call the same functions, with its own author and clock.
- *The journal's author is one of three:* `person` (an HTTP session), `rule` (the ingest) and `model`
  (reserved for the nightly call). An agent working through a command is none of these. Whether it is a new
  author, or acts as one of them, is open.
- *Every recorded change can be undone,* and an undo is refused as stale when what it would overwrite has
  changed since. That is what makes giving an agent write access reviewable: its changes are rows the
  person can list and take back.
- *Commands already exist in `cmd/finwise`* (`serve`, `hash-pin`, `backup`, `ingest`) with the repository's
  habits: exit 0 for success, 1 for a failure, 2 for a usage error; messages are fixed sentences that name a
  path and a reason and never the content of a file, because an SQLite error can quote a value; only
  `cmd/finwise` logs what the ingest or the PIN source did.
- *Access today is a session cookie* behind a PIN, over HTTP. A command has no session; how it
  proves it may act is open.
- The pot targets decision (see the tracking bead for pot targets) names this interface as the likely way to
  author the four Rainy Funds targets, since the design has no control for them.

**What an implementer must respect**: money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path;
every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant and only `internal/authored` executes
it; the files of `internal/api` log nothing and read the clock only from the request; a real ledger is a
person's whole financial history, so nothing a command prints or logs holds a value from it that the person
did not ask to see.

**Corrections, read in the code on 2026-11-23.**

- Both items this one waited for are closed (`finwise-4ph`, `finwise-8kt`).
- No read lists changes: the contract of `changes` has only `undo`, which takes any change id, while the
  interface offers undo for the change made last only.
- An undo is refused as stale for more causes than a value overwritten since (`internal/authored/undo.go`),
  among them a row the undo would take along without restoring.
- The handlers cannot be called outside the router as they stand: the router builds their views, records
  the author `person` for every write (`serveWrite` in `internal/api/writes.go`) and holds the retry that
  takes a new snapshot in before a write.
- `review.propose`, `review.approve` and `review.refuse` are registered and answer null
  (`internal/api/review_approvals.go`); the approvals card exists on the weekly tab
  (`web/src/screens/revisao/ApprovalsCard.vue`) and its list is always empty.

## What must be decided first
Answered by the person on 2026-11-23, one point at a time. Each answer says what lost.

1. **The shape of the interface.** A thin client of the contract over HTTP, with three verbs: call any read
   by its name and print the JSON answer; propose (a method, its arguments, a reason); list its own
   proposals with the outcome of each. Exit statuses 0, 1 and 2, as the other commands have; the server's
   address and the token come from the environment. The read-only command is the first delivery.
2. **What an agent may do alone and what only proposes.** Nothing alone: an agent reads and proposes, and
   never writes directly. In the first version it may propose what belongs to a transaction (its line, its
   tags and its note, with the bulk and the whole-establishment variants) and also budget, subscriptions,
   exclusions, splits and reimbursements. Out of an agent's reach until the person says otherwise: closing a
   month, the PIN, settings. A proposal stores the method, its arguments and the reason the agent wrote; the
   app, not the agent, words what will happen, from the method; approving runs the same handler the screen
   uses, with its refusals. Lost: read only; direct writes for some classes of change with proposals for
   others (it needs limits per class, a screen to list and undo what an agent did, and more room to be wrong
   with the person's money); only line, tag and note; everything but the PIN.
3. **Who the author is.** A change applied from an approved proposal is journaled under the author `model`,
   which the journal already accepts, and carries the name its proposer gave: the person reads that it was
   proposed by that name and approved by them, and undoes it as any change. Accepting a suggestion in the
   queue stays the person's own change, as accepting the rule's suggestion is today.
4. **How a command proves it may act.** Over HTTP to the running server, with a token of the agent's own
   that opens the reads and `review.propose` and nothing else; the server refuses any other write for it.
   One token, made by a command and kept only as a hash in a variable of the server, as the PIN's hash is;
   revoking it is changing the variable and restarting. Lost: the PIN (a session equal to the person's, held
   back only by the agent's obedience); the command opening the database itself, as `finwise ingest` does
   (it works only where the files are and repeats what only the router does). A known limit: a process on
   the machine and under the user that owns the database file can open it from outside; the token guards
   the API, not that.
5. **How approvals reach the person.** A line proposed for a transaction still pending shows in the weekly
   queue itself, as the suggested line with the agent's reason, and the person accepts it or picks another;
   a pending review already carries `suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification`
   (`PendingReview` in `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`), the last null until something explains a
   suggestion. Everything else goes to the approvals card, with a view of the values before and after: the
   person asked for that view, a budget proposal needs it in any case, and it needs a design, since the
   prototype has none. A refusal closes the proposal and may carry a reason the person writes, which the
   agent reads. A proposal nobody answers stays, with no expiry; when what it would change has changed,
   approving answers the usual refusal and the proposal closes as stale. The card has an "approve all". The
   app applies an approved change, never the proposer. Lost: everything on the card (forty line proposals
   become forty loose sentences away from their transactions); a refusal with no reason; expiry after a
   number of days.
6. **How an agent is given its limits.** There is nothing to configure: the token only reads and proposes,
   and the list of what may be proposed is fixed in the server (item 2).
7. **Whether it authors the pot targets.** Struck out here: it belongs to the item on targets, `finwise-5xb`.
8. **How it is verified.** With invented data and the app's own tests, and one end-to-end test of the
   command against the real server over an invented ledger. Nothing is run against a real ledger.

**Left for later, with an item of its own:** a screen with the history of answered proposals, each approved
one with its undo (`finwise-moo`).

**Still owed before this item closes:** the implementation items, each written whole. A likely cut, to be
confirmed when they are written: the token and the read command; the storage of proposals with
`review.propose`, the command's propose and list verbs, and the approvals card backed for the proposals one
sentence describes; the line suggested for a pending transaction in the queue; the difference view, with
the budget proposal and the line of a transaction already categorised, after its design.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every item of "What must be decided first" has an answer written into this bead by the person, or is
struck out with the reason.
- [ ] The implementation beads exist, each written to the standard (self-contained, checkable criteria),
each depending on the write side's last piece, and none grants an agent a power the person has not given.
- [ ] This bead changes no code: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` before and after, and no test is added, so
there is none to see failing.
- [ ] Done when: the decisions are recorded here, the implementation beads are written and ready, and the
three approval methods are not mistaken for finished work by anyone who sees them answer null.

## Tests
None: nothing is implemented here. The implementation beads must carry: an agent's change recorded under
its author and undone; a refusal when what the agent changed was overwritten; a proposal that appears,
is approved and applied exactly once; a proposal that is refused changes nothing; every output of a
command free of ledger values.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none now (this bead edits only the tracker). When implemented, expect: `cmd/finwise` (the
commands), `internal/api` (the three approval handlers and what they store), `internal/authored` (a place
to keep a proposal, which means a migration owned by that work, and possibly a new author), the review
screens if an approval needs more than they show.
**Reads only:** `cmd/finwise/`, `internal/api/`, `internal/authored/`, `internal/contract/contract.json`,
`web/src/api/contract/review.ts`

Not statable in a few lines until the shape is decided.
close_reason: A tracking item, and its own criteria are met. Its eight questions were answered by the person on 2026-11-23 and are written into it with what lost: an agent reads and proposes and never writes; it reaches the running server over HTTP with a token of its own; a line for a pending transaction shows in the weekly queue and every other proposal on the approvals card, with a difference view for the ones a sentence cannot describe. The implementation items exist, held: finwise-qpr, finwise-oxu, finwise-80b and finwise-ek3, with the design question finwise-utf and the later item finwise-moo. No code changed with this item.

title: Answer the transaction list, detail and filter options with what the person authored, and resolve the transaction a write names
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the transaction list, the transaction panel and the filters show only what the bank sent: no
transaction is ever on a budget line, no tag, note or nickname appears, the panel's history is always empty,
and nothing a person could decide about a purchase (not counting it, splitting it, calling it a refund)
shows. This work makes those screens show what is kept about each transaction: once the writes that follow
it land, a purchase put on a line shows that line under the name its own month's budget gives it, a split
shows its parts and what they still lack, a nickname replaces the bank's wording, the tag filter offers the
tags in use, and the panel lists what was done to the purchase and offers to take back only what can still
be taken back. On its own nothing changes on screen, because nothing writes those things yet. What the
person would notice if it were wrong: a purchase shown on a line its month's budget never had, a month
whose transactions do not add up to its totals, a nickname shown on one purchase and not on the next at the
same shop, or a "Desfazer" offered on a step that then refuses.

## Outcome
`transactions.list`, `transactions.detail` and `transactions.filterOptions` answer every field the person
can author from the app's database, joined in Go by key with the ledger's rows inside one request; on a
server without the app's database, or with an empty one, they answer byte for byte what they answer today.
Four functions every later slice shares land in `internal/api`: the lookup that resolves the transaction a
write names and indexes it; the function that gives the name to show for an establishment key; the merge of
authored rows into a listed transaction; and the function that disposes a month by joining the ledger's rows
with the authored rows and calling `budgetrules.Dispose`. A third golden state, `full-authored/`, proves the
merged answers; `full/` and `empty/` do not change.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite snapshot that a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, and the collector may swap the
file under it at any time. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, owned by the Go package `internal/authored`,
the only package that executes SQL against it; the server has one only when started with `--db`. *The
stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it is
the only existing statement of how the panel's fields behave, and its behaviour is the rule here except
where this text says otherwise. *The contract* is the TypeScript interface `FinwiseApi`
(`web/src/api/contract/`); *the manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it. *A listed
transaction* is one the API lists: a row of the collector's clean list (which already hides a bank-pending
row that has its posted pair) after `internal/txrules` has folded tax rows under their purchases and taken
the movements of savings pots out. *A budget line* has an integer id minted by the app's database and a name
that belongs to a budget version; *the budget in force for a month* is the latest version starting at or
before it (a month before the first version uses the first). *The fees line* is the built-in `Tarifas e
juros`, in no group, with a fixed id. *The current month* is the Brazil month of the request's instant
(`brday.MonthOf(nowOf(ctx))`), never the host's clock. *An establishment key* is the identity of an
establishment or a person (`doc:`, `name:` or `text:`); under `doc:` it is a document number, never logged.
*A golden file* is the committed, exact answer of one call over an invented fixture.

**What this builds on, delivered by earlier work.** Read each in the code as that work left it.

- What a transaction counts for (finwise-305): `internal/budgetrules.Dispose` takes plain values (for each
  listed transaction its signed cents, the ledger's facts and what the person authored; for the month its
  budget's line ids with their groups and the fees line's id) and puts every transaction in exactly one of
  twelve dispositions: unconverted, movement, excluded with a reason, waiting for review, split, fee, a
  credit linked to a purchase as its reimbursement, refund, income, other credit, a debit on a line, an
  uncategorised debit, first match wins. It answers what each adds to or takes off which line, the
  unassigned amount and the applied reimbursement (the smaller of the linked credit's cents and the
  purchase's magnitude), and it states how it treats a line id the month's budget does not have.
- The transactions' tables and the index (finwise-jw2): migration `0003_transactions` with `tx_index(tx_key,
  account_id, day, cents, establishment_key, bank_pending, first_run, last_run, evaluated)` and
  `tx_ids(provider_id, tx_key)`, not journaled; `tx_state(tx_key, line_id, classified_by, confidence,
  pending_reason, pending_line_id, pending_confidence, ask_reason, note, exclusion, refund, refund_line_id,
  reimbursable, expected_cents, credit_tx_key, credit_cents)`; `tx_tags`, `tx_split_parts`,
  `establishments(key, nickname, default_line_id)`, `establishment_tags`, `history_steps(id, tx_key,
  change_id, kind, text, day)` and `history_step_reasons`, owned by its step. In `tx_state`, `exclusion` is
  null for "counts", empty for "switched on, no reason yet" and a text for the reason; `refund` is null for
  "as the ledger's rule says" and 0 or 1 for what the person set; a transaction is pending when
  `pending_reason` is set, with `pending_line_id` and `pending_confidence` as its suggestion. It also
  delivers the store half of the target lookup (given a provider id and the row's facts, mint or refresh the
  index row inside a write's transaction and answer the key), the reads the authored view offers over those
  tables, and the `authoredtest` builders for them.
- The budget's tables and line lookup (finwise-ef7, through the tables above): one function of "the lines a
  month's budget has" (each line's id, its name in that version and its group; the fees line too when the
  set is not empty), from which the menu `transactions.filterOptions(month).lines` and every lookup of a
  line's name in a month come. The month argument of `transactions.filterOptions` comes from the contract
  change before it (finwise-m9q).
- The views handed to handlers (finwise-jzw): a handler's third parameter is one value carrying a view of each
  store for the request. The ledger view is one handle and one read-only transaction, so every ledger query
  of a request sees the same snapshot. The authored view is one read-only transaction on the app's
  database, so an answer is wholly before or wholly after a concurrent write; without `--db` it is an empty
  view that answers "nothing authored", so read code has one path.
- The recorder (finwise-wi4, through the harness below): a read-only function that says whether the inverse of a
  chosen part of a change would be refused (a later change still in force touches one of those units, or a
  unit no longer holds the change's last value), usable inside a read-only transaction.
- The write conformance harness (finwise-fst): read conformance has a third state, the full invented ledger of
  `internal/api/fixtures_test.go` with an invented authored state, whose cases are a list of their own,
  `authoredReadCases`, of a type and constructor of their own, with golden files under
  `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`; the interface's equality test
  (`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`) checks that it never picks one up. Write dispatch (finwise-2s5, before
  it) hands a write handler a recorder holding one immediate transaction and the request's ledger view.

**What the code is today** (each point read in the file named).

- `internal/api/transactions.go`: `registerTransactions` registers `transactions.list`,
  `transactions.filterOptions` and `transactions.detail`. `readTransactionsList` parses the query
  (`queryPeriod`, `periodOf` in `transactions_period.go`), loads the ledger context (`loadContext`:
  accounts, identities, bills, bank and account labels) and calls `interpretPeriod`, which reads the period
  widened by `taxPairingDays` (3) on each side, runs `txrules.Interpret`, fails the read when a row went
  nowhere (`checkPlaced`), and keeps the rows inside the period newest first. `readTransactionFilterOptions`
  answers every account, `Tags: []` and the lines of finwise-ef7.
- `internal/api/transactions_wire.go`: `transactionFrom` writes one interpreted row. Today `Name` and
  `OriginalName` are both the ledger's name; `EffectiveAmount` equals `Amount`; `CountsInTotals` is
  `Movement == NotAMovement && !Unconverted`; `Refund` is the ledger's rule; `Line`, `ClassifiedBy`,
  `Confidence` and `Pending` are null; `BelowThreshold`, `ReimbursementIncome`, `Reimbursed`, `Excluded` and
  `Split` are false; `Tags` is `[]`. `pendingReview` has the contract's four fields, all required.
- `internal/api/transaction_detail.go`: `readTransactionDetail` reads the whole clean list
  (`CleanTransactions(ctx, wholeLedger)`), finds the row by its provider id (`rowWithID`), interprets only
  that row's month widened by three days (`interpretMonthOf`), and answers the listed transaction with that
  id, or null when the id is unknown, is a tax row folded into its purchase, or is a pot movement.
  `detailFrom` answers `OwnTags`, `SuggestedTags`, `ReimbursementCandidates` and `History` empty, `Note` and
  `Reason` `""`, `AskReason` false, `Justification`, `SplitParts`, `Reimbursement`, `Exclusion` and
  `RefundLine` null, `SplitRemaining` zero. `sectionsOf` gives the panel's sections; `counterpartyOf`
  answers `{key, nickname: null, defaultLine: null, fixedTags: []}` for an establishment or a person and nil
  for a movement.
- `internal/api/card.go` interprets the whole ledger in one pass (`CleanTransactions(ctx, wholeLedger)` then
  `interpretRows(rows, around, wholeLedger)`); `wholeLedger` is in `shell.go`. `purchaseWireOf` and
  `itemsOf` there copy `transaction.Name` from the interpreted row.
- `internal/api/conformance_test.go`: `readCases` holds five `transactions.list` cases, one
  `transactions.filterOptions` case and eight `transactions.detail` cases (`tx-instalment`, `tx-foreign`,
  `tx-month-end`, `tx-own-transfer`, `tx-pending`, `tx-salary`, `tx-unconverted`, `no-such-transaction`). The
  full invented ledger also holds `tx-foreign-tax` (a tax folded into its purchase) and `tx-pot-transfer` (a
  pot movement); its clock is 2026-03-20.
- The stand-in: `rules.ts` (`toContract`, `allTags`, `effectiveAmount`), `transaction-detail.ts` (`toDetail`,
  `sectionsOf`, `counterpartyOf`, `splitRemaining`), `history.ts`, `model.ts`, and the tests `rules.test.ts`,
  `writes.test.ts` and `panel-writes.test.ts`.

**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

- Ledger rows and authored rows are joined in Go, by key, inside one request that sees one snapshot of each
  store; the index is never the source of a figure shown or summed. Why: the reader hands out rows, never a
  connection, and the snapshot is swapped under it. Rejected: `ATTACH`; copying the ledger into
  `finwise.db`; a fresh ledger handle per query.
- A transaction's line belongs to the budget in force for the transaction's own month; a line named by
  something with no month (an establishment's default line) is resolved in the current month. Why: the
  person decided that a transaction of a closed month can still be recategorised, split, excluded and
  linked, and a line the month's budget lacks would count in no group of that month. Rejected: everything
  against the current month.
- Where a result type allows null, an unknown target answers null; `not_found` is for results that cannot
  be null.

**The target lookup.** The one function every transaction write uses to find what it names. It resolves a
provider id through the same interpreted ledger read the API lists transactions with, the one
`transactions.detail` uses for its target (the whole clean list, the row's own month widened by three days,
the listed transaction with that id), in the request's ledger view, so the write has the row's current
facts: its name, its establishment key, whether the other side is a person, whether it is a movement, its
amount, its day. An id that read does not list (an unknown id, a tax row folded into its purchase, a pot
movement) is unknown, and the caller decides what that answers (null where the result allows it, `refused`
/ `not_found` otherwise). For a known id it then calls the store half (finwise-jw2) inside the write's
transaction, which creates or refreshes the index row and answers the key. A write that spans months ("all
purchases here", the reimbursement candidates) interprets the whole ledger in one pass, as `card.go` does,
and indexes what it touches through the same store half; the lookup offers that whole-ledger form too. The
transaction writes after this work (the line writes, finwise-yfu; tags, note and the establishment, finwise-42n;
split, exclusion and refund, finwise-9je; reimbursements, finwise-ilt) all call it; none of them has a copy. A read
never writes the index, and a listed transaction with no `tx_ids` row has nothing authored. One known
interaction, owned by the ingest (finwise-82m): the pairing of a vanished bank-pending row considers only posted
rows the index has never seen, so a posted row a write indexed first keeps its own key.

**The name function.** One function answers the name to show for an establishment key: the nickname stored
for that key when there is one, otherwise the name the ledger gives the row. The list and the detail use it
here; the card's lists (`purchaseWireOf`, `itemsOf`, and through them the closing view's card bill) are
brought under it by the work on tags and nicknames (finwise-42n), and every later place that shows a name of an
establishment or a person calls it: the toast and the history text of the line writes (finwise-yfu), the
reimbursement's link and candidates (finwise-ilt), the subscription candidates (finwise-ot5), the establishments of a
budget line (finwise-jsx), the settings overview (finwise-s2k).

**Disposing a month.** One function takes the request's views and a month, interprets the month's listed
transactions exactly as `transactions.list` does for that month (widened by three days, then cut), joins
each with its authored rows by key through `tx_ids`, maps each into `Dispose`'s input (the person's `refund`
when set, otherwise the ledger's rule; excluded when `exclusion` is a non-empty text; pending when
`pending_reason` is set; a credit linked when some purchase's `credit_tx_key` is its key; a purchase's linked
credit cents from its `credit_cents`), takes the month's budget from the line lookup, and calls `Dispose`.
The budget's figures (finwise-jsx), the shell's counts and the opt-in real-ledger test of the write side
(finwise-ta2), which checks the two invariants of `Dispose` over every month of a real ledger, call it; nothing
else recomputes dispositions. A fee row on the fees line counts there whoever put it there, the person or a
rule.

**What the reads answer.** A listed transaction with no authored rows answers exactly what it answers
today. Otherwise:

`Transaction` (the list and the detail):

- `name`: the name function's answer; `originalName`: always the ledger's name, so a search still finds it.
- `line`: the name the transaction's line has in the budget of the transaction's own month; null with no
  line. In a period of several months each row is named by its own month's budget. A line id that month's
  budget lacks (unreachable once a budget save clears such references, finwise-oib; possible in a fixture) is
  answered the way `Dispose` treats it, so the read and the disposition agree, and never fails the read.
- `classifiedBy`: `Você` for the person, `Regra` for a rule, `IA` for the model, null for nobody; `confidence`
  as stored; `belowThreshold` false, because it is about the model's confidence only and there is no model
  yet.
- `pending`: null unless pending; then `reason`, `suggestion` (the suggested line's name in the month's
  budget), `confidence` and `justification` `""`. The contract's suggestion, confidence and justification
  are not nullable yet; making them nullable, and answering a pending review without a suggestion, is the
  work on the rules that classify new transactions (finwise-zts). No fixture of this work holds such a row.
- `tags`: the transaction's own tags in the order they were added, followed by the fixed tags of its
  establishment key in the order they were added, without repeats, as the contract says. The stand-in's
  `allTags` lists the fixed ones first; the server departs from it on purpose.
- `effectiveAmount`: the amount plus the applied reimbursement (a purchase of -300.00 with a linked credit
  of 150.00 answers -150.00; with a credit of 400.00, 0.00).
- `countsInTotals`: false for a movement, an unconverted row and a transaction excluded with a reason, so
  the code's existing false for an unconverted row stays; `excluded`: excluded with a reason.
- `refund`: what the person set, or the ledger's rule when they set nothing.
- `reimbursed`: the purchase has a linked credit; `reimbursementIncome`: the credit is linked to a purchase.
- `split`: two or more parts.

`TransactionDetail`, beyond the above:

- `justification`: `""` for a pending transaction or one the model classified, null otherwise, as the
  stand-in's `toDetail`, until the model exists. The panel shows "Confirmar" while it is not null.
- `askReason` as stored; `reason`: the reason on the latest step that has one, `""` when none has.
- `counterparty`, only where `sectionsOf` shows the establishment or the person section, as today: `{key,
  nickname, defaultLine, fixedTags}`; `defaultLine` is the default line's name in the budget of the current
  month, null when that budget does not have it, while the stored id stays.
- `ownTags`: the own tags alone, in order. `suggestedTags`: the known tags the transaction lacks among its
  own.
- `note` as stored, `""` by default.
- `splitParts`: null when not split, otherwise each part's line name (in the month's budget) or null and its
  amount, in position order; `splitRemaining`: the purchase's magnitude less the parts' sum, negative when
  they exceed it, zero when not split.
- `reimbursement`: null when the purchase is not marked reimbursable, otherwise `{expected, link}` with
  `expected` null when cleared. The `link` (the credit's id, name, day and amount) and
  `reimbursementCandidates` are answered by the work on reimbursements (finwise-ilt), which reads the whole
  ledger for them and owns their golden change in `full/`; here `link` stays null and the candidates `[]`,
  and no fixture of this work holds a link.
- `exclusion`: null when `exclusion` is null, otherwise `{reason}` (`""` while switched on with none).
- `refundLine`: the refund line's name in the month's budget, or null.
- `history`: the transaction's steps newest first, each `{id, text, day, reason, undoable}`: `id` the step's
  id as a decimal string, `text` and `day` as stored, `reason` its owned reason or null, and `undoable`
  computed by the recorder's read-only check over the units of this one transaction that the step's change
  touched, inside the read's transaction; always false for a note. Taking a step back is the line writes'
  work (finwise-yfu), which proves it agrees with this flag.

`TransactionFilterOptions.tags` (the known tags): every distinct tag in `tx_tags` and `establishment_tags`,
alphabetically. The collation is the implementer's: deterministic, and pinned by a test that includes an
accented tag and an upper-case one. `accounts` stays as today and `lines` is the menu of finwise-ef7.

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. A real
snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from it (amount, description, name, document, id) is ever
printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the person
running a test and goes into no file; a test that touches a real ledger runs only when
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. Nothing in this work needs a real ledger. Every fixture is invented,
and `-update` of the golden files refuses to run while `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set. New files in
`internal/api` log nothing (`handler_silence_test.go` allows only `logging.go` and `router.go` to name a
logging package).

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional
Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit message. Money is
integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; the float guard covers `internal/api`. Every SQL
statement over the app's database is a registered constant, and this work adds none in `internal/api`: the
tables are read through the authored view and, in a write, through the recorder's transaction. Interface
text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; a design value in a component comes from a
token (this work touches no component).

**Failure paths that touch this work.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing | the three reads answer `ledger_unavailable` as today; a write's target lookup answers it too and nothing is recorded |
| the snapshot is swapped during a request | the request finishes on the snapshot it opened |
| a transaction disappears from the ledger | its authored rows and index row stay; it is in no list and no count until listed again |
| the bank rewords a row so its establishment key changes | an indexed transaction keeps what it has and its index row takes the new key; it shows the nickname of its new key, if any |

**Left to the implementer** (what makes this bead `spec:open`): which interpreted amount the lookup hands
the store half as `cents` (the ingest's pairing must compare it the same way); the collation of the known
tags, pinned; file and function names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The target lookup, for a listed id with no index row, answers the row's facts and a new key, writes
one `tx_index` and one `tx_ids` row and adds no row to `changes` or `change_effects`; for an indexed id it
mints nothing and refreshes the row; it answers unknown, writing nothing, for `no-such-transaction`,
