  authored state built by `authoredtest`: one case per write with golden effects under
  `testdata/golden/writes/` and the undo check; extension mode for `applyLineToEstablishment`;
  nothing-to-do cases; refusal cases for `stale_change`, `not_found` and `unknown_line`.
- Unit (Go, handlers over the same fixture): the line resolved per month with two budget versions; the
  fees line with and without lines; `askReason`; the reason's owned row and the extension after it; the
  bulk all-or-nothing and its refusal order; every condition of "all purchases here", each on its own;
  the step's undo per column, per transaction, its `askReason`, its own undo.
- Table (Go), ported from `web/src/api/fake/writes.test.ts` ("changing a line", "applying a line to the
  whole establishment", "changing many at once", "undo") and `panel-writes.test.ts` ("confirming the model",
  "correcting the model", "taking a step back"), with the departures above as their own rows.
- Property (Go): random sequences of the six writes and undo, `undoable` against the step's undo.
- Unit: the no-leak test over the new write cases, with a handler that logs.
- Integration, by the review only, over a real snapshot: the two timings, durations only.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/transaction_line_writes.go`, `internal/api/transaction_history_writes.go`,
`internal/api/messages.go`, `internal/authored/`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/`,
`internal/api/transaction_line_writes_test.go`, `internal/api/transaction_history_writes_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/transactions.go`, `internal/api/transaction_detail.go`,
`internal/api/transactions_period.go`, `internal/api/card.go`, `internal/api/fixtures_test.go`,
`internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`, `internal/txrules/`, `web/src/api/fake/transaction-writes.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/transaction-edits.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/history.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/changes.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/writes.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/panel-writes.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/transaction-detail.ts`,
`web/src/components/transactions/useLineChange.ts`,
`web/src/components/transactions/useTransactionActions.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelActions.ts`, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/`, `bin/ci`

Two new handler files in `internal/api` (the names are a proposal), three constants in `messages.go`, the
store functions for a transaction's classification, a history step and its reason in `internal/authored`
(one or two files), and any builder `authoredtest` lacks for them. That is about seven code files in two
packages. No migration is added: if a column of `0003_transactions` proves missing, say so in the report
instead of adding a migration file. No read changes: the detail's history and `undoable` are delivered
before this work, and this work proves its writes agree with them. Nothing under `web/` is edited. The
difficulty is `critical` because a wrong line or a wrong undo changes the totals silently and an undo that
overwrote a later edit would lose the person's work without a word.
close_reason: Six writes registered (setLine, confirmLine, setLineForMany, applyLineToEstablishment, setReason, undoHistoryStep): a line is resolved in the budget of the transaction's own month, settling ends the review, an establishment-wide move extends the change it names, and one step is taken back by the rules of an undo. Verified: gate green on the branch merged with main; about twenty deliberate breaks while writing it and fifteen in review, the two that survived at first now failing tests of their own.

title: Answer a pot's yield fast and open the month into its daily rows
description:
## What changes for the user
Against a real ledger the Cofrinhos screen, a pot's page and the Patrimônio screen each take about fifteen seconds to open, while every other screen opens at once. And on a pot's page the month's yield is one figure, where the person asked for it to open into the days behind it; that list is always empty. After this lands the three screens open as fast as the others, and the month's yield opens into its daily rows, with a day the bank's records cannot support shown as unknown rather than as zero.

## Outcome
Every yield figure the backend answers (the pots list, a pot's page, the net worth) comes from one fast computation over the balance history, which also gives the daily rows of a pot's month. The collector's own yield statement stays in the reader only as the reference the new computation is tested against.

## Context
finwise's read-only Go backend answers the pots and the net worth from the ledger a collector fills every night. The contract's pot detail carries the month's yield and `days`, the rows behind it; the user decided in the feature interview that yield is shown per month and opens to its daily rows.

Yield is not the change in balance: a deposit raises the balance and yields nothing. The collector's README has a statement for it, copied into the reader (`internal/ledger/pot_yield.go`) and run as three statements over the same CTEs because the single statement does not prepare in this module's SQLite. It answers **one figure per window** between two days, with a `reason` column that says when the figure cannot be computed. The balance history is one sighting per night.

**Measured over a real ledger, by the review, three runs each on the built server:** `savingsPots.list` 12.5 to 15.1 s, `savingsPots.detail` 14.7 s, `netWorth.overview` 13.7 to 15.3 s. Every other read answered in under 0.4 s, including `home.summary`, which reads the same pots and balances without asking for a yield. The handlers already ask the statement only once per account that has a pot to follow, twice in all on that ledger, so the cost is the statement itself, about seven seconds a call, not the number of calls.

That statement is also why the daily rows are empty: a row per day means a window per pair of consecutive sightings, and asking it once per pair took about 70 seconds.

The reader already has a fast read of every sighting's balances and pots (`internal/ledger/history.go`), which the net worth's chart uses. `internal/potrules` already has what turns rows into a month: `DayYield`, and `YieldOfMonth`, which sums a pot's rows, keeps them oldest first, and makes the month unknown when any row is.

What is missing is the yield of each pair of consecutive sightings computed without the collector's statement: from the sightings' balances and the transfers between them, in Go or in one set-based statement, with the same formula and the same reasons for "cannot be computed" as the collector's statement gives for that pair. The collector's statement stays as the reference: a test runs both over fixture ledgers and requires the new rows to equal the reference's answer for every pair, including the pairs with a deposit, a withdrawal, a pending transfer, a pot that appears, and a pot that closes. No handler runs the collector's statement at request time.

A wall-clock figure is not something the work can honestly produce on a shared machine; the absence of the slow statement from the request path is, and a test asserts it. The review measures the time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `savingsPots.detail` answers one daily row per pair of consecutive sightings of the month for a pot with a stable identity, oldest first, each with its day and its yield or unknown.
- [ ] When every daily row of a month is known, their sum equals the month's yield to the cent; when any is unknown, the month's yield is unknown.
- [ ] For every pair of consecutive sightings in the fixture ledgers, the new row equals what the collector's statement answers for that pair, figure and reason.
- [ ] A day with a deposit and no yield is a row of zero, not the deposit.
- [ ] A pot without a stable identity has no daily rows and an unknown yield.
- [ ] `savingsPots.list`, `savingsPots.detail` and `netWorth.overview` take their yield figures from the new computation, and a test fails if any read handler runs the collector's yield statement.
- [ ] The golden files of the three methods are re-recorded from the fixture ledgers, and the only differences from before are the daily rows that used to be empty.
- [ ] Any new statement lives in the reader's registry and is prepared against the collector's real schema by the existing test.
- [ ] The time each of the three reads takes over a real ledger is measured **by the review**, not by the lane, three runs each on a quiet machine, against the figures above, and recorded on the pull request; each is expected under one second.
- [ ] A test skipped unless `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set compares the new rows with the collector's statement over a sample of at least 20 pairs of a real ledger and logs counts only: pairs compared, equal, unknown.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` and the opt-in run reports every sampled pair equal.

## Tests
- Unit over fixture ledgers: the new rows against the collector's statement, pair by pair.
- Unit: the daily rows of a month, their order, their sum against the month's figure, unknown days.
- Golden: the answers of the three methods.
- Unit: no read handler reaches the collector's yield statement.
- Integration, opt-in: a sample of pairs of a real ledger, counts only.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/ledger/`, `internal/potrules/`, `internal/api/pots.go`, `internal/api/pots_yield.go`, `internal/api/pots_detail.go`, `internal/api/net_worth.go`, `internal/api/pots_test.go`, `internal/api/net_worth_test.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/contract/savings-pots.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/net-worth.ts`, `bin/ci`

The yield of a pair of sightings gets a second, fast implementation beside the reference one, and the three handlers that show a yield switch to it. The card, the home summary and every other read are not touched.
close_reason: The yield of each pair of sightings is computed by pure rules from one read of the ledger, and a test requires it to equal the collector's statement, figure and reason, for every window of the fixture ledgers, reaching every reason. savingsPots.list, savingsPots.detail and netWorth.overview take their yields from it, a pot's month opens into its daily rows, and a test fails if a read handler can reach the collector's statement. bin/ci: CI green on the tree merged with main. Over a real snapshot every sampled pair equalled the statement. Measured by the review on the built server over a real ledger, three runs each: savingsPots.list 0.34 to 0.44 s, savingsPots.detail 0.34 to 0.35 s, netWorth.overview 0.33 to 0.37 s, against 12.5 to 15.3 s before. Left open: a day that cannot be supported is left out of the rows because the contract's daily amount cannot be unknown.

title: Work out the month's closing from the budget, the transfers, the card and the subscriptions, and let the person mark its steps and keep or cancel a subscription
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, over their real bank data, the "Fechamento" tab of the review is the same empty page for every month:
nothing planned, nothing spent, no transfer to check, no subscription to look at, every step "to do" except
the first, and a "Marcar como feito e seguir" that answers that the app is read-only. Its card step shows the
amount to set aside for the bill of the current month even when the person is looking at January. After this
lands the tab works the month on screen out of the person's own budget and bank data: planned against actual
per group and line, what is left of the variable lines, the month's transfers and which were made, the card
purchases of that month that fall on the next bill, and the subscriptions whose review has come due, which
the person can keep (with a new review date six months after the month ends) or mark to cancel, each with
"Desfazer". The steps the person marks stay marked for that month. The first step counts only the reviews
still waiting from that month or before, so a purchase made this month no longer blocks last month. If this
were wrong the person would see an "actual" that does not match the budget screen, a transfer shown as made
that was not, a bill of the wrong month, or a subscription that keeps coming back after being decided.

## Outcome
On a server with the app's database, `review.closing(month)` answers, for the month asked: its closed state
and day; the eight steps, with the first following the pending reviews dated up to the month's end and steps
2 to 7 following the marks stored for that month; that pending count; planned against actual from the budget
in force for the month and the spending the budget view computes; the leftover; the contributions from the
month's derived transfers and their marks; the card bill of the month asked; the subscriptions to review;
an empty report; and the closed months, newest first. `review.markStepDone`, `review.keepSubscription` and
`review.cancelSubscription` have handlers that record undoable changes. On every server, with or without the
database, the card bill is the bill of the month asked instead of the current month's, which changes one
golden file. The closing's list of contributions keys its rows by position, so two transfers of one name are
two rows.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, and every request reads one
snapshot of it. *The app's own database* is `finwise.db`, owned by the package `internal/authored`, the only
package that executes SQL against it; the server has one only when started with `--db` / `FINWISE_DB`. *The
stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it and
its tests are the only existing statement of how writes behave, and its behaviour is the rule wherever this
text does not say otherwise. *The contract* is the TypeScript interface `FinwiseApi` under
`web/src/api/contract/`; *the manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it, versioned and
never edited by hand. *The journal* is the record of every change to authored data, from which a change is
undone. *A month* is `YYYY-MM` and *a day* `YYYY-MM-DD`, in Brazil time (`internal/brday`; a month's end is
`brday.MonthPeriod(month).Last`); "today" and "the current month" are the Brazil day and month of the instant
in the request's context, never the host's clock. The budget has five groups a person edits: income (`rec`,
"Receita"), fixed (`fix`, "Fixos e essenciais"), variable (`var`, "Variáveis"), provisions (`prov`,
"Provisões") and reserves (`res`, "Reservas de desejo"). A provision is money set aside every month for a bill
that comes once in a while, a reserve money set aside for something wanted; both are carried each month by a
transfer to a pot. *A pot* is a savings place the pots screens list (a bank account's reserve, `reserve:...`,
or an investment, `investment:...`). *Closing a month* freezes its budget, not its transactions.

**What earlier work provides.** None of the following is in the repository when this text is written; each is
delivered before this slice starts and is used here as it landed.

- The app's database and its statement registry (finwise-9h2), the recorder and undo (finwise-wi4: every change to a
  journaled table is one recorded change; a *set table* holds rows that are facts by existing and an effect is
  one row appearing or disappearing; an *attribute table* holds one row of independent facts per key and an
  effect is one column changing; undo restores by inverse and refuses with `stale_change` what a later change
  still in force touched), the per-request views (finwise-jzw: one ledger snapshot and one read-only view of the
  app's database per request, an empty view without `--db`, and the clock required), write dispatch (finwise-2s5:
  arguments validated against the manifest, one immediate transaction with a recorder holding one open change
  of author `person` and the method's name, `read_only` before the body is read without the database or
  without a handler, `writesWithoutHandler` in the manifest walk) and the write conformance harness (finwise-fst:
  every write has a case as a *recorded change*, whose effects match a golden file under
  `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/` and whose undo returns a canonical dump of every journaled table to
  the dump taken before, or as *nothing to do*, a null answer that adds no row to the journal; the builders of
  `internal/authored/authoredtest`; the third read state with cases in `authoredReadCases` and golden files in
  `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`).
- The budget's tables (finwise-ef7): budget versions by month (the budget in force for a month is the latest version
  at or before it; a month before the first version uses the first; with no version a month has five empty
  groups), line ids stable through renames with names owned by each version, and `closed_months(month,
  closed_on)`, which nothing but the close of a month writes (finwise-jro); here a closed month comes from a fixture.
- The budget view (finwise-jsx): the pure package `internal/budgetrules` and the real `budget.view`. Every listed
  transaction of a month is in exactly one disposition, and the view's per-line figure of a month is what that
  month's transactions add to or take off the line, looked up by line id: what was spent for a fixed or
  variable line, what was received for an income line. It also computes the residual (income less the fixed,
  variable, provision and reserve groups), which is the investment.
- The review's migration and the one definition of pending (finwise-rf3, reached through finwise-66k): `0007_review`
  created `closing_steps(month, step)` as a set table whose `step` the database itself restricts to the six
  steps marked by hand (`planned-actual`, `leftover`, `contributions`, `card-bill`, `subscriptions`, `report`);
  and one function answers which transactions are pending (a pending review in `finwise.db`, listed by the
  ledger now, in a month whose budget has at least one line), optionally only those dated up to a given day.
  If no store function for `closing_steps` exists yet, adding it is part of this slice, in the file of
  `internal/authored` that holds the review's tables.
- Subscriptions (finwise-ot5): the `subscriptions` table (an attribute table keyed by a minted id, holding the
  name, the line, `status` in `Manter`, `Analisar`, `Backup e cancelar`, `Cancelar`, `status_day`, `review_on`
  and the note), the pure package `internal/subrules` that derives each one's amount and cycle from the card's
  charges, the reads `subscriptions.list` and `subscriptions.detail`, and one store function that sets the
  status and moves `status_day` to today only when the status really changes, written to be called again by
  this slice. An id is known only when it is the plain decimal text of an existing row.
- The payday transfers (finwise-66k): the transfers of a month, derived (never stored) from the budget in force for
  it, the links between lines and pots and the pots the ledger lists now: one per open, listed pot with linked
  provision or reserve lines (key `pot:<pot id>`, the sum of their amounts, named after the pot or "Sem nome"),
  one per provision or reserve line linked to no such pot (key `line:<line id>`, named after the line), and
  `investment` ("Investimento") for the residual when it is above zero; none of zero; in that order, the pots by
  name then id, the lines in the budget's order. A transfer is done only when marked by hand for that month
  (`transfer_marks(month, transfer_key, done_on)`); a mark counts only while its key is in the month's list. The
  derivation and the read of a month's marks are reachable from outside the payday handler.

**What the code is today (each point read in the file named).**

- `internal/api/review_closing.go`: `registerClosing` registers `review.closing`. `readClosing` parses its
  month with `onlyMonthArgument`, calls `loadCard` and answers `closingViewWire` with `Steps` from
  `freshClosingSteps()` (the first step done, steps 2 to 7 `todo` and markable, the last `todo` and not
  markable), `PendingCount` 0, `PlannedActual` from `emptyPlannedActual()` (the five groups of
  `editableGroupNames` with zeros, `contributions` true for `prov` and `res` through `contributionGroupKeys`),
  `Leftover` 0, `Contributions`, `SubscriptionsToReview`, `Report` and `ClosedMonths` empty, and `CardBill` from
  `closingCardBillOf(card)`. `closingStepOrder` is the contract's `ClosingStepId` in order, and
  `TestTheClosingListsEveryStepOfTheContractOnceAndInOrder` holds it to the manifest.
- `closingCardBillOf(card)` takes `card.overview().PayAhead`, so the bill is always the current month's:
  `cardView.overview()` (`internal/api/card.go`) asks `card.nextBill(brday.Month(card.today[:7]))`, and
  `readClosing` never passes the month it was asked. `cardView` already has what the month needs:
  `nextBill(month)` calls `cardrules.Card.AmountOnNextBill(month, today, purchases)`, `payAheadOf(next)`
  turns its result into the wire with the purchases newest first, and `title()` is the label.
  `AmountOnNextBill` (`internal/cardrules/nextbill.go`) adds the purchases of the month dated on or after two
  days before the closing that falls in the month and not carrying the closed bill's id; it answers known and
  empty before that closing has come, and unknown when no closing falls in the month (`closingWithin` looks only
  at the ledger's bills and the cycles predicted after the latest, `cycles` in `cycle.go`).
- `internal/api/review_closing_test.go` pins: both invented ledgers' answer for 2026-03 (`closingOf`), the
  empty ledger's for 2025-12, the step order against the manifest, the fresh steps, the closing's bill equal to
  the card page's pay-ahead over `c6BillLedger` (80.74, "C6 Carbon · final 8888", three purchases), no bill
  without a card and none when the next-bill amount is unknown (`noTableLedger`), and `bad_request` for a
  month that is not one. Its cases in `readCases` are `review.closing` for `["2026-03"]` and `["2025-12"]`.
- The golden files `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/review.closing.2025-12.json` and
  `full/review.closing.2026-03.json` both carry `"cardBill": {"amount": 0.00, "cardLabel": "Platinum Visa ·
  final 1234", "purchases": []}`. The full invented ledger's card (`internal/api/fixtures_test.go`) has one bill,
  `bill-mar`, due 2026-04-05 and closing 2026-03-28, and its bank has no closing table; with the clock at
  2026-03-20 the March closing has not come (known, empty), and no closing of that card falls in December 2025.
- The stand-in: `web/src/api/fake/closing.ts` (`closing`, `markStepDone`, `keepSubscription`,
  `cancelSubscription`, `KEEP_REVIEW_MONTHS = 6`) and `review-rules.ts` (`closingSteps`, `MARKABLE_STEPS`,
  `plannedActual`, `actualOf`, `differenceOf`, `variableSpent`, `leftover`, `closingContributions`,
  `subscriptionsToReview`, `monthEnd`), with its test `closing.test.ts`. `addMonths` in
  `subscription-rules.ts` keeps the day number and holds it to the last day of a shorter month.
- `web/src/api/contract/review-closing.ts`: `ClosingView`, `ClosingStep` (`markable`: "steps 2 to 7 of a
  month that is still open"), `PlannedActualLine.difference` ("Signed so that negative is the bad direction:
  overspending, or income that fell short"), `ContributionState = 'done' | 'on-target' | 'not-found'`,
  `ClosingApi.markStepDone` ("Null for any other step or a closed month"), `keepSubscription(month, id):
  Promise<KeptSubscription | null>` (`{changeId, name, nextReview}`), `cancelSubscription(id)` (`{changeId,
  name}` or null). `closedMonths` is "Closed months, newest first."
- The screens: `web/src/screens/revisao/ClosingTab.vue` reloads `api.review.closing(month.selected)` on every
  revision and offers "Marcar como feito e seguir" where `step.markable && step.state !== 'done'`;
  `useClosingActions.ts` bumps the revision after `markStepDone` (no toast) and announces
  `` `${kept.name}: mantida. Nova revisão em ${longDay(kept.nextReview)}.` `` and
  `` `${cancelled.name}: marcada para cancelar.` `` with "Desfazer". `StepSubscriptions.vue` hides the buttons
  for a closed month. `StepContributions.vue` draws one row per contribution with `:key="item.name"` and the
  labels "Feito", "No alvo", "Não encontrado"; with transfers derived from the budget two contributions can share
  a name (two pots of one name), and Vue's keys must be unique. Its screen test is
  `web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts`.

**1. The steps.** In the contract's order: `pending`, `planned-actual`, `leftover`, `contributions`,
`card-bill`, `subscriptions`, `report`, `close`.

- A closed month: every step `done`, none markable.
- An open month: `pending` is `done` when the month's pending count (below) is 0 and `pending` otherwise, never
  markable; steps 2 to 7 are `done` when marked for that month and `todo` otherwise, all markable; `close` is
  `todo` and not markable.

**2. The pending count, and the first step.** The pending transactions, under the one definition, dated on or
before the month's end: those of the month and of every earlier month. A pending purchase of a later month
does not count, so the current month's reviews no longer hold the previous month's closing. The same count
for a closed month is answered as computed (the screen shows none for a closed month). The close of a month
looks at exactly these (finwise-jro). Lost: the stand-in's global count (`pendingCount(state)`), which would block
October because of a purchase in November.

**3. Planned against actual.** From the budget in force for the month, the five groups in the fixed order
with their fixed names, each line under the name that version gives it and in the version's order. For each
line: `planned` is its amount; `actual` is, for a line of `rec`, `fix` or `var`, the budget view's figure for
that line in that month (looked up by line id, from the same function `budget.view` uses, so the two screens
never disagree), and for a line of `prov` or `res` the line's planned amount when the transfer that carries it
is marked for that month or the month is closed, and 0.00 otherwise. "The transfer that carries it" is the
month's transfer whose key is `pot:<id>` of the pot the line is linked to when that pot is listed and open,
and `line:<line id>` otherwise; a line of 0.00 has no transfer and its actual is 0.00 either way. `difference`
is `actual - planned` for the income group and `planned - actual` for the others, so negative is the bad
direction. A group's `planned`, `actual` and `difference` are the same from the sums of its lines, and
`contributions` is true for `prov` and `res`. The fees line and the investment are in no group and are not
listed. All in integer cents; there is no rounding to state.

**4. Leftover.** The variable cap (the sum of the `var` lines of the month's budget) less the sum of the
variable lines' actual of section 3; negative when they went over.

**5. Contributions.** The month's transfers, in their order, each `{name, amount, state}`: `done` when the
month is closed or the transfer is marked for that month, `not-found` otherwise. The server never answers
`on-target`: it belongs to a pot at its target, and nobody can author a pot's target yet (the person decided
that pot targets get no control for now). The `investment` transfer is among them when the residual is above
zero, as the stand-in lists "Investimento".

**6. The card bill of the month asked.** `cardBill` is what the month's card purchases charge on the bill after
the closing that falls in that month: `cardView.nextBill(month)` for the month asked, through the existing
`payAheadOf`, with the card's `title()` as `cardLabel` and each purchase as `{name, day, amount}` with the amount
as a positive figure; null when the ledger holds no card or the next-bill amount of that month is not known. A
month whose closing has not come answers a bill of 0.00 with no purchase, as the card's rule says. The names
are those the card page's pay-ahead shows, nicknames included once the card's purchases show them. The card
page itself, `home.summary` and every other caller of `overview()` are unchanged. This applies with or without
the app's database. Lost: the bill of the current month shown for every month.

**7. Subscriptions to review.** The subscriptions whose `review_on` is on or before the month's end and whose
status is not `Cancelar`, in the order they were created (by id), each `{id, name, amount, cycle, reviewOn}`:
the stored name, the amount and cycle `subrules` derives (the same values `subscriptions.list` answers), and the
review day. For a month that ended before a review day, that subscription is not listed.

**8. The rest.** `month` is the month asked; `closed` and `closedOn` come from `closed_months`; `report` is an
empty list until the model writes one; `closedMonths` lists every closed month as `{month, closedOn}`, newest
first. The month is parsed as today (`2026-13` stays `bad_request`). With the snapshot missing the read answers
`ledger_unavailable`. On a server without the database, or with an empty one, every field is what it is today
except the card bill of section 6, because a month with no budget has five empty groups, no transfer and no
pending review, and nothing is closed or marked.

**9. `review.markStepDone(month, step)`.** The step is checked against the manifest's `ClosingStepId` by the
dispatcher (anything else is `bad_request`), the month is parsed (`2026-13` is `bad_request`). Then:

- a closed month, or the step `pending` or `close`: null, nothing recorded (the contract's comment: "Null for
  any other step or a closed month");
- a step already marked for that month: an empty change, and its id is answered; its undo is a no-op (the plan
  of the write side says so for this write, and the stand-in begins a change in that case too);
- otherwise one row of `closing_steps(month, step)`, recorded as a set-table effect, and `{"changeId": "<id>"}`.

It reads nothing from the ledger, so it answers the same with the snapshot missing. A future month and a month
before any budget are marked like any other: no rule refuses them. `changes.undo` of the change removes the row.
A mark is of its month only: marking `contributions` for 2026-03 leaves 2026-04 `todo`.

**10. `review.keepSubscription(month, id)` and `review.cancelSubscription(id)`.**

- Keep: status `Manter` and `review_on` = the month's end plus six months, the day number kept and held to the
  last day of a shorter month (2026-11 gives 2027-05-30, the stand-in's vector; 2026-03 gives 2026-09-30;
  2026-08 gives 2027-02-28; 2026-02 gives 2026-08-28). Answers `{changeId, name, nextReview}`, the name being the
  subscription's stored name.
- Cancel: status `Cancelar`. Answers `{changeId, name}`.
- Both set the status through the subscriptions' store function, so `status_day` moves to today in the same
  change only when the status really changes, and both are one recorded change undone by `changes.undo`.
- Both answer null and record nothing for an id the database does not have (`"999"`, `"sub-1"`, `""`). Where
  the contract's result allows null, "nothing to do" answers null too: a keep that would change neither the
  status nor the review day (already `Manter` with that day) and a cancel of a subscription already `Cancelar`
  answer null and record nothing. That is the write side's general rule for nullable results; the stand-in
  begins a change in those cases, so this is a departure, pinned by a test.
- Neither reads the ledger. Neither is refused for a closed month (the interface hides the buttons there, and
  closing freezes the budget, not the subscriptions).

**Where the server departs from the stand-in on purpose,** each pinned by a test the final report names: the
pending count and the first step look at the month's own pending reviews (dated up to its end) instead of the
global count; the card bill is the month's instead of the current month's; planned against actual uses the
spending of the month asked, derived from the ledger, instead of a seeded baseline; the contributions are the
derived transfers, joined to a line by its link and not by name, and never `on-target`; keeping or cancelling
an unknown subscription answers null and records nothing (the stand-in's own answer, kept on purpose and listed
because the subscription screen's setters refuse an unknown subscription with `not_found` instead: these two
results are nullable and theirs are not); a keep or a cancel that changes nothing answers null; undo is by
inverse instead of restoring a snapshot.

**Failure paths that touch this slice.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing | the read answers `ledger_unavailable`; the three writes read no ledger and work |
| a write fails halfway, or waits out the five-second lock | one transaction: nothing of it is kept; `internal` |
| two tabs mark the same step | the writes queue; the first records the row, the second records an empty change |
| an undo meets a later change (a keep undone after a later `setStatus` still in force) | `stale_change`; nothing is restored |
| the budget or a link changes after a transfer was marked | the mark counts only while its key is in the month's list (finwise-66k) |
| a pending row vanishes from the ledger | it leaves the count, and the first step can turn `done`; it comes back if listed again |

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. Nothing in this
slice needs one: every ledger and authored state here is invented. If one is opened to check a shape, it is
opened read-only; no value from it (amount, description, name, document, id) is printed, logged, or copied into
a file, a commit, a bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the person running the test and goes into no
file; a test that touches it runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. New files of `internal/api`
log nothing.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of your own and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional
Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit message. Money is
integer cents and no float may appear in the money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a
registered constant of `internal/authored`. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is
English. A design value in a component comes from a token; the one component touched changes its row key and no
style. A golden file changes only with `go test ./internal/api -run TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile
-update`, which refuses to run while `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set, and every changed golden file is read
before it is committed.

## Acceptance criteria
The examples use an invented state, the clock at 2026-03-20. The budget in force for 2026-03: `rec` Salário
8.000,00; `fix` Aluguel 2.500,00; `var` Mercado 900,00 and Lazer 300,00; `prov` IPTU 150,00 (linked to an open,
listed pot named "Caixinha da casa") and Revisão do carro 200,00 (no pot); `res` Viagem 400,00 (no pot). In
March the budget view answers Salário received 7.500,00, Aluguel 2.500,00, Mercado 950,00, Lazer 120,00. The
pot's transfer is marked for 2026-03; nothing else is.

The view
- [ ] `review.closing(["2026-03"])` answers `plannedActual`: Receita 8000.00 / 7500.00 / -500.00; Fixos e
essenciais 2500.00 / 2500.00 / 0.00; Variáveis 1200.00 / 1070.00 / 130.00 with Mercado 900.00 / 950.00 / -50.00
and Lazer 300.00 / 120.00 / 180.00; Provisões 350.00 / 150.00 / 200.00 with IPTU 150.00 / 150.00 / 0.00 and
Revisão do carro 200.00 / 0.00 / 200.00; Reservas de desejo 400.00 / 0.00 / 400.00; `contributions` true only for
the last two groups.
- [ ] `leftover` is 130.00; with Mercado at 1.500,00 spent it is -420.00.
- [ ] `contributions` is, in order: Caixinha da casa 150.00 `done`; Revisão do carro 200.00 `not-found`; Viagem
400.00 `not-found`; Investimento 3550.00 `not-found`. No state is `on-target`.
- [ ] Each line's `actual` of `rec`, `fix` and `var` equals the figure `budget.view(["2026-03"])` answers for the
same line.
- [ ] With 2026-02 closed under the same budget, `review.closing(["2026-02"])` answers `closed` true, its
`closedOn`, every step `done` and none markable, every provision and reserve line's actual equal to its planned,
and every contribution `done`.
- [ ] With three pending reviews dated 2026-02-27, 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-05, the count is 2 for 2026-02 (first
step `pending`) and 3 for 2026-03; with only the one of 2026-03-05, 2026-02 answers 0 and its first step `done`
(a pending purchase of a later month does not block the view); a pending review whose transaction the snapshot no
longer lists is in neither count.
- [ ] Steps 2 to 7 marked in `closing_steps` for 2026-03 answer `done`, and the same steps answer `todo` for
2026-04.
- [ ] With subscriptions S1 (`Analisar`, review 2026-03-15), S2 (`Cancelar`, review 2026-03-01), S3 (`Manter`,
review 2026-04-10) and S4 (`Manter`, review 2026-03-31), created in that order, `subscriptionsToReview` is S1, S4
for 2026-03, none for 2026-02 and S1, S3, S4 for 2026-04, each with the amount and cycle `subscriptions.detail`
answers for it.
- [ ] `closedMonths` with 2025-12 and 2026-02 closed is `[2026-02, 2025-12]` with their days; `report` is `[]`.

The card bill
- [ ] Over `c6Ledger` with the purchases of `c6BillLedger` and four of February (2026-02-01 for 30.00;
2026-02-03 for 12.00 carrying `bill-jan`'s id; 2026-02-03 for 7.00 with no bill id; 2026-02-15 for 40.00),
`review.closing(["2026-02"])` answers a bill of 47.00 with the purchases of 2026-02-15 and 2026-02-03 (7.00), in
that order; `review.closing(["2026-03"])` still answers 80.74 with its three purchases, equal to the card page's
pay-ahead; `review.closing(["2026-04"])` answers 0.00 with no purchase; a month in which no closing of the card
falls answers `cardBill` null.
- [ ] `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/review.closing.2025-12.json` changes in `cardBill` alone, from the
March figure to `null`; `full/review.closing.2026-03.json`, every file of `empty/` and `card.overview.json` do
not change; the diff is in the final report with one sentence saying why it is right.

The writes
- [ ] `review.markStepDone(["2026-03","leftover"])` answers a change id and adds exactly the row (`2026-03`,
`leftover`); the view then answers `leftover` `done` for 2026-03 and `todo` for 2026-04; `changes.undo` removes the
row and returns the canonical dump to the one taken before.
- [ ] Marking it again answers a change id whose change has no effect, and its undo changes nothing.
- [ ] `markStepDone` answers null and adds no row to `changes` or `change_effects` for the step `pending`, for the
step `close` and for any step of a closed month; it answers 400 `bad_request` for the step `xyz` and the month
`2026-13`; with the snapshot file missing it still answers a change id.
- [ ] `review.keepSubscription(["2026-03","<S1>"])` answers `{changeId, name, nextReview:"2026-09-30"}`; S1 then
has status `Manter`, `review_on` 2026-09-30 and `status_day` 2026-03-20, and leaves March's list; undo puts back
`Analisar`, 2026-03-15 and the previous status day. The months 2026-11, 2026-08 and 2026-02 give 2027-05-30,
2027-02-28 and 2026-08-28.
- [ ] `review.cancelSubscription(["<S4>"])` answers `{changeId, name}`; S4 has status `Cancelar` and `status_day`
today, and leaves the list; undo restores both.
- [ ] Keep and cancel answer null with no row added to the journal for `"999"`, `"sub-1"` and `""`; a keep of a
subscription already `Manter` with that review day, and a cancel of one already `Cancelar`, answer null and
record nothing.
- [ ] Undoing a keep while a later `subscriptions.setStatus` of the same subscription is in force answers 409
with reason `stale_change` and changes nothing.
- [ ] Each of the three writes has a write-conformance case as a recorded change with its golden effects under
`testdata/golden/writes/` (one row appearing in `closing_steps`; the status, its day and the review day changing
in `subscriptions`; the status and its day) and a nothing-to-do case; all three leave `writesWithoutHandler` and
the manifest walk passes. On a server without the database the three answer 403 `read_only` with their body read
0 times.

The interface, goldens and guards
- [ ] In `web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts`, with a stand-in state holding two contributions of the same
name, one done and one not, the step draws two rows, each with its own state label.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` passes on both viewports for every closing state, and its output is in the
final report.
- [ ] `authoredReadCases` gains `review.closing` for an open month with marks, pending reviews, transfers, a
budget and subscriptions, and for a closed month, with golden files under `testdata/golden/full-authored/`.
- [ ] On a server without the database, `review.closing` answers what it answered before for every case except
the card bill of a month other than the current one, and `TestTheClosingListsEveryStepOfTheContractOnceAndInOrder`
passes unchanged.
- [ ] No non-test file added or changed here contains a float or a call to `time.Now`.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against a deliberate break named in the final report: the pending
count made global; the count's last day taken as the month's first; a contribution line joined by name instead of
by its transfer's key; a closed month's contributions left as not found; the income difference signed like the
others; the card bill computed for the current month; a step mark ignoring its month; `markStepDone` recording a
row for `pending`; an already-marked step answering null; the next review computed from the month's first day; a
keep that changes nothing recording a change; an unknown subscription refused with `not_found` instead of null; the contributions keyed by name in the screen.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, parity passes, and the invented state above reproduces every figure
of the view's criteria from the budget, the transactions, the marks and the subscriptions.

## Tests
- Table, `internal/api` (or the rule package that holds the arithmetic, if it lands as a pure function): the
  steps of an open and a closed month; planned against actual with the sign rules and the contributions rule
  (marked, not marked, closed, a line of zero, a line linked to a closed pot); the leftover positive, zero and
  negative; the contributions' states; the next review for the four months of the criteria.
- Integration with `httptest`, `internal/api`, over ledgers built with `ledgertest` and authored states built with
  `authoredtest`: the whole view of the example, the closed month, the pending counts across months and across two
  snapshots, the subscriptions to review over three months.
- Integration, the card bill over `c6Ledger` for February, March and April and a month with no closing, against
  the card page's pay-ahead for March.
- Unit, `internal/authored` over a migrated scratch database: the marks of a month read back; every new statement
  registered and prepared.
- Write conformance (the harness): a recorded-change case per write with golden effects and its undo; a
  nothing-to-do case per write.
- Golden: `full/review.closing.2025-12.json` re-recorded and its diff read; the third state's cases in
  `authoredReadCases`.
- Screen test (vitest, `web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts`): two contributions of one name.
- Parity (the browser): the closing tab's states, by `npm --prefix web run parity`.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the final report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/api/review_closing.go`, `internal/api/review_closing_writes.go`,
`internal/api/review_closing_test.go`, `internal/api/review_closing_writes_test.go`, `internal/authored/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/full/review.closing.2025-12.json`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`, `web/src/screens/revisao/StepContributions.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `internal/api/card.go`, `internal/cardrules/`, `internal/api/budget_view.go`,
`internal/api/messages.go`, `internal/api/fixtures_test.go`, `internal/api/card_test.go`,
`web/src/api/fake/closing.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review-rules.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/subscription-rules.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/review-closing.ts`,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, `web/src/screens/revisao/ClosingTab.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/useClosingActions.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/StepSubscriptions.vue`,
`web/scripts/parity/states.mjs`, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`, `bin/ci`

The closing read is rewritten in place; the three writes go in a new file (the name is a proposal); the
`closing_steps` store function joins the file of `internal/authored` that holds the review's tables if it is not
there yet. The card bill needs no change in `card.go`: `nextBill`, `payAheadOf` and `title` already exist, and
only the closing stops going through `overview()`. One component changes one key. About five code files in three
places, hence `size:L`. The budget view, the transfers' derivation, the subscriptions' rules and store, the pending
function, the payday tab, the close of a month and the shell are used, not changed; the stand-in and the contract
do not change (the stand-in follows only the contract's type changes, and this slice has none).
close_reason: review.closing answers the month asked from the budget, the dispositions the budget view uses, the payday transfers and their marks, the card bill of that month and the subscriptions due; markStepDone, keepSubscription and cancelSubscription record undoable changes. Verified: gate green and parity 174 checked, 0 over on the branch merged with main; about thirty deliberate breaks while writing it and five in review, each failing a named test.

title: Put a field back on the stored value when its save is refused or fails
description:
## What changes for the user

Today, when the person types a nickname, a note or an amount and the app cannot save it, a message says so
and the screen loads again, but the field goes on showing what was typed, with nothing to tell it apart
from a value that was saved. The person leaves believing it is stored and finds it gone later. The likely
case: the session expired overnight, a note is typed in the morning, the PIN is asked for, and after it the
note is still in the field and is in no database. Once this lands, a field whose save did not go through
shows again what is actually stored, so what is on screen is always what the app holds; the person sees the
text go and types it again.

## Outcome

In the settings and in the transaction panel, every field that saves when it is changed returns to the
stored value as soon as its own write is refused or fails, whatever the kind of failure, while the message
of that failure is shown exactly as today. A field the person is typing in while another field's write
fails is not touched. The one editor that has an explicit edit mode keeps its draft open.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the interface against a backend that refuses writes (`npm --prefix web run dev:backend` over a
   read-only `finwise serve`), or in a test mount a screen over `readOnlyApi(createFakeApi(...))`.
2. Open the settings, type a new nickname for an establishment and leave the field.
3. The toast says the app is read-only and the settings are fetched again.

Observed: the field still shows the typed nickname. Expected: the stored nickname (or the empty field, if
there was none).

## Context

Every failure of an API call ends in `web/src/api/failures.ts`: it shows the toast and bumps the revision
counter, and each screen fetches again on a new revision so that none keeps showing what the server does
not hold. That works for everything drawn from the fetched data. It does not work for an input the person
typed in: the fetched value is the same as before the write, so the property handed to the input does not
change, Vue does not render it again, and the element keeps the typed text. Nothing was ever reset on a
failure; while the backend refused every write nobody typed into these fields in earnest.

The person decided what a field does in that case (2026-11-22): it goes back to the stored value. Keeping
the typed text and marking the field as "not saved" was rejected because it needs a visual state the design
does not have, and doing that for the note alone was rejected because it gives two behaviours to explain.
What is typed is lost on a failed save and typed again; that is accepted.

The fields, as they are on `main`, each sending its write when it is changed or released:

- Settings (`web/src/screens/config/`): the nickname of an establishment, the nickname of a person and the
  card's label, all three through `NicknameInput.vue`, which binds `:value` to a property and emits
  `commit` on change (`NicknamesSection.vue` and the card's section use it); the threshold slider of
  `CategorizationSection.vue`, a local value under `v-model` that is synchronised only when the stored
  value changes, and which its label, the marker on the chart and the legend also read; the minimum of
  examples in the same file (`:value` and a change handler); the closing day of `CardSection.vue`.
- Transaction panel (`web/src/components/transaction-panel/`): the nickname of a person in
  `PersonSection.vue`; the note in `NoteSection.vue`; the reason of an exclusion in `ExclusionSection.vue`;
  the "why" of a line in `LineSection.vue`; the expected amount in `ReimbursementSection.vue`; the amount
  of each part in `SplitSection.vue`.

Two things that look alike and are not part of the defect:

- `EstablishmentSection.vue` in the panel has an explicit edit mode: a draft opened by a button and saved
  by another. When its save fails the editor stays open with the draft, which is visibly an edit not yet
  saved, as the budget's edit mode already does. That stays, and gets a test.
- `TagsSection.vue` has a box for a tag to add, cleared when the write succeeds. What is left in it after a
  failure is a tag not yet added, not a stored value shown wrongly. It is not changed.

`PinSection.vue` and `DataSection.vue` of the settings were not examined. If either holds a field of the
kind above, it is fixed the same way and named in the report; the PIN form itself has its own handling and
is not touched.

Constraints on how, which the tests below hold:

- Only the field whose own write failed is reset. A reset tied to the revision counter alone is wrong: the
  counter also moves when another field's write succeeds, and the field the person is typing in at that
  moment would lose its text.
- The failure still reaches `failures.ts`, once, with its toast and its one fetch. A place that needs to act
  on a failure before it gets there catches, acts and throws the same failure again, as
  `BudgetScreen.vue` does for a save refused because the month was closed. No call site swallows a failure.
- One mechanism for all the fields, written once and used by each, not a copy per component. Its shape is
  the implementer's choice (a composable, a small wrapper around the write, a method the input exposes);
  say which and why in the report.
- No new visual state, no new text, no style change. A value from the design in a component comes from a
  token, and the parity check must not move.
- When the failed write was in fact stored (a `network` failure after the server committed), the field
  ends on the stored value, which is then the typed one, once the fetch that follows arrives.

Tests fail one chosen method of the stand-in with `failingOne(api, 'domain.method', kind, reason?)` and
refuse every write with `readOnlyApi(api)`, both in `web/src/test/readOnly.ts`. The method each field
sends is in the component or in the actions file it calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each of the twelve fields named above (three uses of the nickname input, the threshold, the
      minimum of examples, the closing day, and the six of the panel), a screen test types or sets a new
      value, has the field's own write answered `internal`, and finds the field showing the stored value
      again, the toast of a failed save shown once, and the stand-in's stored value unchanged.
- [ ] For the threshold, the label, the marker on the chart and the legend also show the stored value
      again.
- [ ] For one field of the settings and one of the panel, the same holds for each of `read_only`,
      `refused` (with any reason), `internal` and `network`.
- [ ] A field with no stored value (a nickname never set, an empty note) goes back to empty.
- [ ] With the write of field A failing, text typed meanwhile into field B, not yet committed, is still
      in field B afterwards. With the write of field A succeeding, the same.
- [ ] After a `network` failure of a write the stand-in did store, the field shows the typed value once
      the fetch arrives.
- [ ] A write that succeeds leaves every field showing what was stored, as today; the existing tests of
      the settings and of the panel pass unchanged.
- [ ] The establishment editor of the panel, when its save fails, is still open with the draft that was
      typed.
- [ ] The tag box of the panel behaves as today after a failed write.
- [ ] The reset is written once: the report names the one place, and no component has its own copy of it.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` ends with every state at 0 over the limit, and its summary line is in
      the report.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once against the code before the fix or against a deliberate break
      of the mechanism, and the report names which.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: no field of the two directories shows a typed value the app did not store, in tests that
      fail on today's code.

## Tests

- Screen tests (vitest, over `createFakeApi` wrapped with `failingOne` or `readOnlyApi`), one per field, for
  a failed write; the four kinds of failure for one field of each screen; the two-fields case; the
  `network` failure that was stored; the editor that keeps its draft; the tag box.
- Unit test of the shared mechanism by itself, if it is a function or a composable that can be called
  without a screen.
- Golden: none. Parity: the visual check of the ported screens, run once at the end on a still tree.

## Blast radius

**Edits:** `web/src/screens/config/NicknameInput.vue`, `web/src/screens/config/NicknamesSection.vue`,
`web/src/screens/config/CategorizationSection.vue`, `web/src/screens/config/CardSection.vue`,
`web/src/screens/config/useSettingsWrites.ts`, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/PersonSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/NoteSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/ExclusionSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/ReimbursementSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/SplitSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelActions.ts`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/failures.ts`, `web/src/test/readOnly.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/EstablishmentSection.vue`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/TagsSection.vue`, `web/src/screens/budget/BudgetScreen.vue`

Nine components of one kind in two directories, the two files their writes pass through, one new file for
the shared mechanism wherever the implementer puts it, and their tests. Nothing outside `web/src`, no
contract type, no store, no template text, no style. The list of files is where the fields are; a file in
it that turns out to need no change is left alone and said so.

## Recovery path

Nothing stored changes shape and nothing is migrated. Reverting the commits brings back today's behaviour.
close_reason: A field that saves when it is changed goes back to the stored value when its own save is refused or fails (the three uses of the nickname input, the threshold with its label, marker and legend, the closing mode radios), and a field being typed in is no longer erased when another field of its section saves (the six fields of the panel, the minimum of examples, the closing day). One module, web/src/lib/storedField.ts: a directive that writes the element only when the stored value changes or after its own save, and a restore-and-rethrow around the save. bin/ci green on the branch merged with main; parity 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%. Review: three independent mutations; one survived at first (restore to the value the field was mounted with) and now fails six tests. The bead's list of affected fields came from reading the code and was wrong about eight of them; the implementer ran the tests against main first, corrected it, and found the erased-neighbour defect.

title: Let a pending review carry no suggestion in the contract, and show such a transaction in the line pill, the list's marks, the panel and the weekly queue without inventing one
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every transaction the app asks about in the weekly queue ("Pendências") comes with a line the model
is said to suggest and a percentage of confidence, because the prototype's examples were written that way.
Soon the app will ask about real purchases with no model behind it, and for a shop it has never seen it
has nothing to suggest. If the screens stayed as they are, the person would read "null?" in a line pill,
"IA null%" beside a purchase, a "Confirmar" button with nothing to confirm, or "A IA tinha sugerido null",
and the queue's "Aceitar" button could send an answer with no line at all. After this work such a
transaction shows "Pendente" in its line pill, its reason ("Estabelecimento novo", "PIX para pessoa sem
apelido") where a percentage used to be, no "Confirmar" in the panel, and in the queue no suggestion, no
percentage and an "Aceitar" button that stays disabled until the person picks a line. A transaction that
has a suggestion but no explanation of it gets its "Confirmar" in the panel and simply no explanation. The
prototype's screens look exactly as before.

## Outcome
In the contract, `PendingReview.suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification` become nullable; the manifest
is regenerated; the Go wire type and the merged transaction reads answer null where the app's database has
no suggestion, and null for every justification. Every place of the interface that shows a pending
transaction (the line pill, the list's marks, the panel's line text and actions, the queue item and its
answer) has a tested state for a pending review without a suggestion and one for a suggestion without a
justification. The stand-in follows the type change and nothing else; the parity check passes unchanged.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite snapshot that a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database* is
`finwise.db`, where everything the person authors is kept. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend
under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on (`vite build --mode prototype`, and the dev
server); it is the only existing statement of how writes behave, and every pending review in its dataset
(`prototype-data.ts`) has a suggestion, a confidence and a justification. *The contract* is the TypeScript
interface `FinwiseApi` (`web/src/api/contract/`); *the manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`,
generated from it by `npm --prefix web run contract`, versioned, never edited by hand, and checked current
by the gate. *A pending review* (`PendingReview` in `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`) is a
transaction waiting for the person to choose its budget line; `Transaction.pending`,
`TransactionDetail.pending` and `ReviewQueueItem.pending` (`web/src/api/contract/review.ts`) carry it. *The
queue* is the list of pending reviews in the weekly review ("Pendências"). *The parity check* is `npm
--prefix web run parity`: it builds in prototype mode and measures every ported screen against the
design's reference screenshots. *The gate* is `bin/ci`.

**The decision, and what lost.** A transaction without a suggestion can be pending: `suggestion`,
`confidence` and `justification` become nullable. Why: the nightly model call is not part of the write
side (decided by the person, 2026-11-21), and without it "new establishment" has nothing to suggest, yet
the queue must still work. What lost: waiting for the model; inventing a suggestion. The rules that will
produce such reviews are separate work: one pure function decides, for a transaction never evaluated,
"leave it", "apply a line by rule" or "pending" with "Baixa confiança" (with a suggested line and a
confidence), "PIX para pessoa sem apelido" or "Estabelecimento novo" (with neither) (finwise-9gz), and the
ingest, the job that brings each new snapshot into the app's database, applies it (finwise-82m). Neither is
needed for this work: the interface is proved over the stand-in, and the Go side over a fixture. This is a
deliberate departure from the stand-in, whose data never has a pending review without a suggestion; the
report names the test that pins it.

**What earlier work provides.** Each is delivered before this bead starts; read its interfaces in the code
as that work left them.

- The merged transaction reads (finwise-tsr: the API side of the transactions' store, which answers the list,
  the detail and the review from what the person authored): a pending review is built from `tx_state`'s
  `pending_reason`, `pending_line_id` (answered as the name that line has in the budget of the
  transaction's own month) and `pending_confidence`, and is answered with `justification: ""` because the
  contract does not allow null yet. There is no column for a justification.
- Line menus that follow a month (finwise-m9q: the line id in the contract and every line menu asking for the
  month it is for): each item of the weekly queue asks for the line menu of its own transaction's month,
  which `usePendingAnswer.ts` opens.

**Part 1: the contract and the Go side.** In `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts` today:

```
export interface PendingReview {
  reason: string;
  suggestion: string;
  confidence: number;
  justification: string;
}
```

`suggestion` becomes `string | null`, `confidence` `number | null` and `justification` `string | null`,
each with a one-line comment that says when it is null (no suggestion; no confidence without a
suggestion; no justification until the model). `reason` stays a required string. The manifest is
regenerated, and its `PendingReview` definition then allows null for the three. On the Go side,
`pendingReview` in `internal/api/transactions_wire.go` has `Suggestion string`, `Confidence int` and
`Justification string` today; they become pointers, and where the merged reads build it, a `tx_state` row
whose `pending_line_id` is null answers `"suggestion":null,"confidence":null`, and `justification` is null
on every pending review the server answers (the `""` goes). `TransactionDetail.justification`
(`web/src/api/contract/transaction-detail.ts`) is already `string | null`, and the Go detail already has
`Justification *string` (`internal/api/transaction_detail.go`); neither changes.

**Part 2: the places of the interface.** A pending transaction without a suggestion is a state of each of
these places, each with its test. The state is: `pending` not null, `pending.suggestion` null (and so
`confidence` null). No place may print "null", "undefined" or "null%".

- The line pill, `web/src/components/transactions/BudgetLinePill.vue`: without a line it shows
  `${pending.suggestion}?` for a pending review and "—" otherwise. Without a line and with a pending review
  that has no suggestion, it shows "Pendente". With a line, the line, as today.
- The list's marks, `web/src/components/transactions/marks.ts`: a pending review adds
  `IA ${pending.confidence}%` (tone `warning`). When the pending review has no confidence, the mark is its
  reason, verbatim ("Estabelecimento novo"), with the same tone. A pending review with a suggestion keeps
  today's mark. The bank's own "Pendente" mark for a row not yet posted is unrelated and unchanged.
- The panel's text, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.ts`: `lineLabel` gives `line ??
  pending.suggestion ?? 'Sem linha'`, which already reads "Sem linha" here. `originSentence` gives
  `sugestão da IA, ${confidence}% de confiança` for a pending review; without a confidence it gives the
  reason, verbatim. The movement sentence keeps its precedence.
- The panel's actions, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`: today "Confirmar" and
  "Alterar" appear exactly when `detail.justification !== null`. After this work they appear whenever
  there is something to confirm: a pending review with a suggestion, with or without a justification, or a
  line the model set (`classifiedBy === 'IA'`, as today). They are hidden for a pending review without a
  suggestion; the line button still opens the menu. The justification text shows only when it is not
  null.
- The queue item, `web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`: today it prints `Sugestão da IA:
  ${suggestion} · ${confidence}%` and, once another line is picked, `A IA tinha sugerido ${suggestion}.
  Confirme para usar a sua escolha.`; its primary button reads "Aceitar", or "Confirmar" once a line is
  picked. Without a suggestion it prints no suggestion, no confidence and no "A IA tinha sugerido"; once a
  line is picked it reads `Linha escolhida: <linha>`, as today; the reason badge shows as today; and
  "Aceitar" is disabled until a line is picked. A disabled control is dimmed as `StepClose.vue` does
  (`opacity: 0.4; /* token-exempt: the dimming of a disabled control */`), or with a token. Whether the
  suggestion box is hidden while it has nothing to say is the implementer's; what it must not hold is fixed
  above.
- The answer, `web/src/screens/revisao/usePendingAnswer.ts`: `accept` sends `draft.line ??
  pending.suggestion`; with neither it returns without calling `review.acceptPending`. `pickLine` opens the
  menu with that same value as the current one, which may be null (`openLineMenu` in
  `web/src/components/transactions/useLineChange.ts` already takes `string | null`).

A pending review *with* a suggestion and a null justification (what the rule's "Baixa confiança" will
produce) is also a state: the pill, the marks and the panel's sentence are today's, the panel offers
"Confirmar" and "Alterar" and shows no justification text, and the queue item shows the suggestion line
with no "why" text. The mark and the panel's sentence still say "IA" for it, as today; nothing here
changes that wording.

**The stand-in follows the type change and nothing else.** Its dataset keeps its suggestions and
justifications, so the parity check's screens must not move. Where the change breaks a type, the stand-in
and the tests follow it with the least change: today `web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/review.test.ts` and `web/src/screens/revisao/revisao.test.ts` pass `item.pending.suggestion`
as an answer's `line`, which must be a string. `transaction-edits.ts`, `review.ts`, `transaction-detail.ts`
and `prototype-data.ts` of the stand-in already compile against nullable fields; if one does not, it gets
the smallest type fix and no change of behaviour. The equality test over an empty ledger
(`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`) keeps holding. The screen tests for the new states build them by
handing `createFakeApi` a `prototypeState()` in which one transaction's pending review has `suggestion`,
`confidence` and `justification` null (or only `justification` null), as
`web/src/screens/revisao/closing.test.ts` already hands it a modified state; no inline stub of the backend.

**Privacy and conventions.** Nothing here touches a real ledger; fixtures are invented. Work happens in a
worktree and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a
session, a work item or a plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the
money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant (this work adds none).
Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; the Portuguese quoted above is
exact. A design value in a component comes from a token, or carries a `token-exempt: <reason>` comment.
The parity check's output goes in the report.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `PendingReview.suggestion`, `confidence` and `justification` are nullable in
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`; `npm --prefix web run contract` leaves the manifest unchanged after
the commit; the manifest's `PendingReview` admits null for the three and still requires `reason`.
- [ ] A Go answer carrying a pending review whose `pending_line_id` is null validates against the
manifest's result schema of `transactions.list` and of `transactions.detail` (through the read conformance
or a test that uses the same validator) and holds `"suggestion":null,"confidence":null,"justification":null`;
one with a suggestion holds the line's name, its confidence and `"justification":null`.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` or `empty/` changes; a file under `full-authored/`
changes only where a pending review's `justification` went from `""` to null (and, for a fixture pending
without a suggestion, its `suggestion` and `confidence` became null).
- [ ] Screen tests over a stand-in state with one pending review without a suggestion: the list's pill for
that row reads "Pendente"; its marks are `[{ text: 'Estabelecimento novo', tone: 'warning' }]` (plus its
tags) and no mark contains `%`; the panel's line button reads `Sem linha· Estabelecimento novo▾`, and the
panel has no `.confirm` and no `.justification`; the queue item contains none of "Sugestão da IA", "%" and
"A IA tinha sugerido", its "Aceitar" button is disabled, and clicking it leaves `review.acceptPending`
uncalled (a spy on the stand-in records zero calls); after picking "Mercado" it reads "Linha escolhida:
Mercado", its button reads "Confirmar" and is enabled, and accepting sends `line: "Mercado"`.
- [ ] Screen tests over a stand-in state with a pending review that has a suggestion and a null
justification: the panel shows `.confirm` and no `.justification`; the queue item shows `Sugestão da IA:
<linha> · <n>%` and no "why" text; accepting sends the suggestion.
- [ ] No rendered text of the pill, the marks, the panel or the queue item contains "null" or
"undefined" in either state.
- [ ] The existing tests of these places that use the prototype's data pass unchanged, except for the
three type fixes named above.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` passes with every state as before, and its output is in the report.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, and the report names the break used for each: the pill, the
mark, the panel's sentence, the panel's actions and the queue item each rendered as before the change
(each new screen test fails); the panel's actions gated on the justification again (the suggestion without
a justification loses its "Confirmar"); the accept guard removed (the spy sees a call with no line); the Go
wire type left with plain fields (the null case does not validate).
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, the parity check passes unchanged, and a queue item without a
suggestion sends nothing until a line is chosen.

## Tests
- Unit (`internal/api`): the Go wire type with a null suggestion and with a suggestion and no
  justification, validated against the manifest.
- Golden (`internal/api`, `full-authored/`): the diffs described above, read in review.
- Unit (`web`): `marksOf` in `web/src/components/transactions/transactions.test.ts`; `lineLabel` and
  `originSentence` in `web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.test.ts`.
- Screen test (`web`): the pill in the list, the panel's line section, and the queue item and its answer
  (in `web/src/components/transaction-panel/transaction-panel.test.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/weekly.test.ts`,
  or a new test file beside them), over `createFakeApi` with a modified `prototypeState()`.
- Parity: `npm --prefix web run parity`, unchanged.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `internal/contract/contract.json`,
`internal/api/transactions_wire.go` (and the file of the merged reads that builds a pending review, if it
is another), `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`,
`web/src/components/transactions/BudgetLinePill.vue`, `web/src/components/transactions/marks.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.ts`, `web/src/components/transaction-panel/LineSection.vue`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/PendingItem.vue`, `web/src/screens/revisao/usePendingAnswer.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/review.test.ts`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/revisao.test.ts`, `web/src/components/transactions/transactions.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/panelText.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/transaction-panel/transaction-panel.test.ts`, `web/src/screens/revisao/weekly.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/contract/review.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/transaction-detail.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/`, `web/src/components/transactions/useLineChange.ts`,
`web/src/screens/revisao/StepClose.vue`, `web/src/screens/revisao/PendingQueue.vue`,
`web/src/stores/review-view.ts`, `internal/api/transaction_detail.go`, `bin/ci`

One field change in the contract with its generated manifest, its Go wire type and the read that fills
it; six interface files, each a small conditional; the test files that pin them. Three modules (the
contract, the Go reads, the interface), hence `size:L`, though each edit is small. The stand-in's dataset
and behaviour are not changed. The rules, the ingest, the queue's read and `review.acceptPending` are
other work.
close_reason: A pending review may carry no suggestion: suggestion, confidence and justification are nullable in the contract and the manifest; the server answers null for a review with no line of its month (and then no confidence); the line pill reads Pendente, the mark shows the reason, the panel offers to confirm only a line there is, and the weekly queue sends nothing until a line is picked. No golden file of full/ or empty/ changed. bin/ci green; parity 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%. Review: three independent mutations, all failing tests. The implementer's sixteen breaks each failed a test.
